title: Paginate graph-draft lists and bound batch context building
description: GET /graph-drafts loads every change set with every operation and ships the full context_packet per item (routes/graph_drafts.py:78), and the batch context builder fully hydrates every entity in the project to keep the 10 most recent rows (graph_draft_context.py:309). Pass limit/offset through to the repository, add a summary list schema without context packets, and add ordered limited repository queries. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Move blocking work off the ASGI event loop
description: Both middlewares are async but perform synchronous SQLAlchemy I/O per request (app_parts/middleware.py:77); device-token auth issues a write plus COMMIT on every request for last_used_at (auth.py:489); and async upload handlers drive blocking storage writes (visualizations.py:135). Offload via to_thread/run_in_threadpool, throttle the last_used_at freshness write to a coarse window, and fix the upload handlers. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Push portfolio summary scoping, pagination, and aggregates into SQL
description: GET /portfolio/summary re-introduces the per-project query-loop and unbounded-payload anti-pattern epic 4bk targets, and does not meet the isj acceptance criterion to bound payload/pagination. Per-project N+1 sources (portfolio.py, now 324 lines): (1) query_projects(limit=None) loads every project then scopes/paginates in Python (portfolio.py:62-70). (2) _latest_activity_at loads ALL rows of nine entity types per project just to compute one max(timestamp) (portfolio.py:169-190). (3) _count_statuses issues one query per status value with a wasted limit=1 row (portfolio.py:152-166). (4) _owners_for_project runs query_project_memberships per project (portfolio.py:201-214). (5) _triage_flags_for_project (added by 80i after this bead) runs four more unbounded per-project loads - query_datasets/analyses/claims/goals (portfolio.py:244-300). That is ~20 repo round-trips per project, ~1000 per default 50-project page. ACCEPTANCE: the SQL pushdown MUST preserve vkcj.2's group-before-paginate fix (portfolio.py:68-70 builds all group summaries from the full visible list, then paginates GROUPS with total=#groups); a naive project-level LIMIT/OFFSET pushdown would reintroduce the vkcj.2 split-groups/meta.total bug.
design: Pass accessible_project_ids as WHERE project_id IN (:ids) (admin None short-circuit = no filter) plus LIMIT/OFFSET and use the SQL COUNT for total. Replace _latest_activity_at row loads with select(func.max(created_at/updated_at)) grouped by project_id over all visible projects (existing (project_id, created_at) indexes make this index-cheap). Replace per-status queries with SELECT status, COUNT(*) GROUP BY project_id, status per entity type (or at minimum limit=0). Collapses the endpoint to a small fixed number of aggregate queries independent of project count and size.
notes: Net-new instance not in the 4bk.1 checklist (portfolio.py landed 2026-06-15, after the 4bk epic 2026-06-12). Blocked by 4bk.8: extract the shared visible-projects prefix first so the pushdown happens in one place. Body reconciled 2026-06-17 - re-anchored line numbers and added the 80i triage-flag and _owners_for_project N+1 loops (portfolio.py grew 167->324 lines via sls/769.1/769.2/80i/vkcj after this bead was filed).

title: Extract shared visible_projects() prefix helper (dedupe list_projects / portfolio_summary)
description: portfolio_summary and list_projects still share, verbatim, the visible-projects PREFIX: validate_pagination -> query_projects(limit=None, offset=0) -> filter_project_scoped_items (portfolio.py:60-67 == projects.py:95-101), doubling the surface the 4bk SQL-pushdown must migrate and risking divergence. The blocks diverge AFTER that prefix: since vkcj.2, portfolio_summary builds per-project summaries, groups them, and paginates GROUPS (portfolio.py:68-70), while list_projects paginates the PROJECT list (projects.py:102). So extract a helper that returns the UNPAGINATED visible-project list - e.g. visible_projects(request, repository, status) -> list[Project] - into routes/shared.py and call it from both: list_projects paginates the result, portfolio_summary groups then paginates. (The originally proposed paginated_visible_projects(..., limit, offset) signature no longer fits portfolio_summary's group pagination.)
notes: Blocks the portfolio SQL-pushdown bead 4bk.7 under epic 4bk (extract the shared prefix before the pushdown). Rescoped + repriced to P2 2026-06-17: vkcj.2's group-before-paginate fix made the old "duplicates the paginate block verbatim" premise stale - only the query+filter prefix is now shared, so the helper returns the unpaginated visible list rather than a paginated page.

title: Define a minimal public semantic profile for Lab Tracker graph exports
description:
Successor to the completed LOUD alignment epic. Establish a small, stable public semantic profile for Lab Tracker JSON-LD, ARA extensions, and project-graph mappings without turning persistence models or UI projection tokens into ontology classes.

## Success Criteria
Every child is complete; all emitted custom IRIs resolve; each core resource has one most-specific class; refinements use stable concept IRIs with additive compatibility; project-graph tokens are mapped or explicitly excluded; no persistence migration is introduced.
design: Apply the Linked Art admission rule: mint a class only for a stable independently addressed resource whose shape or relations require consumer branching; represent subtype, status, role, origin, and relation refinements as URI-addressed concepts; materialize edges only when they carry metadata. Preserve the operational domain model and REST write contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Every child issue is complete; every emitted lab: IRI dereferences to a typed definition; each core exported resource has one most-specific class; refinements use stable concept IRIs while legacy literals remain compatible; project-graph tokens have explicit semantic mappings or exclusions; no persistence migration is introduced.
close_reason: All five child beads are complete. Typed dereferenceable vocabulary, minimalist class/concept profile, JSON-LD emission, GoalLink identity, and project-graph semantic boundaries are implemented with 1,555 passing tests and clean Ruff.

title: Restore /terms coverage for every emitted lab: IRI
description:
The closed /terms phase promises that every exported lab: IRI resolves, but instance documents emit custom class IRIs and ARA keys that are absent from the registry.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Generate the standard provenance and ARA JSON-LD documents.
2. Collect custom IRIs used in keys, @type values, predicates, and concept values.
3. Compare them with the current /terms registry and observe missing custom classes and ARA properties, including the crossLayerBinding naming mismatch.

## Acceptance Criteria
Every emitted custom IRI resolves to a non-empty typed registry entry; the machine-readable vocabulary distinguishes classes, properties, and concepts; all builders are covered by a regression test; existing sidecars remain interpretable.
design: Extend the vocabulary entry model to distinguish class, property, and concept terms and to carry the applicable superclass plus optional domain, range, and emitter metadata. Register every currently emitted custom class and property, including the ARA surface. Resolve the crossLayerBinding versus crossLayerBindings mismatch through one canonical term with an explicit compatibility alias if required. Do not introduce the new core class profile in this bug.
acceptance_criteria: A builder-wide conformance test expands or walks every emitted JSON-LD document and proves that each lab: IRI used as a key, @type, predicate value, or concept value resolves to a non-empty typed /terms entry. The machine-readable vocabulary identifies classes and properties correctly, all currently emitted custom classes and ARA properties are covered, and no existing sidecar becomes uninterpretable.
close_reason: Typed /terms registry now covers all emitted custom classes, properties, concepts, and ARA aliases; five-builder closure tests pass.

title: Specify the minimal class-versus-concept contract
description:
Write the decision-complete public application profile that separates structural classes from controlled concepts and qualified relationships. This is the semantic contract for subsequent exporter work, not an internal model redesign.

## Acceptance Criteria
The profile fixes the class-admission rule, exact core and extension class tables, concept schemes and predicates, qualified-edge rule, mapping for every exported record and relationship, Project exclusion, ARA boundary, and additive compatibility policy, leaving no semantic or rollout decision to implementation.
design: The core record classes are ResearchQuestion, Dataset, Claim, Note, Visualization, Goal, and ExplorationNode as subclasses of prov:Entity, plus Analysis and AcquisitionSession as subclasses of prov:Activity. Project is excluded until it has a first-class export. Person and SoftwareAgent use their single standard PROV classes. ClaimRelation, GoalLink, and a qualified question link are resources only where edge role, outcome, status, slot, or provenance metadata requires reification. AraArtifact, AraLayer, and ForensicBinding belong to a separately declared ARA extension; EntityVersion belongs to the provenance extension. Question type, session type, goal type, exploration kind, status, origin, role, outcome, link state, and relation kind are URI-addressed concepts, not subclasses. Existing literal fields remain during this epic and may only be removed in a future explicit profile-major change.
acceptance_criteria: A committed profile document contains the class-admission rule, exact core and extension class tables with superclasses, concept schemes and predicates, qualified-edge rule, mapping for every currently exported record and relationship, Project exclusion, ARA boundary, and additive compatibility policy. It leaves no class-versus-concept, predicate, or rollout decision to the implementation beads.
close_reason: Committed normative semantic profile fixes core/extension classes, SKOS concepts, qualified edges, mappings, exclusions, and additive compatibility.

title: Emit core classes and controlled-concept IRIs in JSON-LD
description:
Implement the approved application profile across standard provenance and ARA JSON-LD builders after the vocabulary contract and class-versus-concept specification are complete.

## Acceptance Criteria
Every core record emits its selected profile class without a redundant explicit superclass; custom classes and concepts dereference with correct hierarchy; concept IRIs accompany legacy literals; JSON-LD expansion, round-trip fixtures, and the worked sidecar pass; no database migration or write-contract change is introduced.
design: Give each core record one most-specific explicit @type and express its PROV superclass in /terms rather than by redundant multiple typing. Emit prov:Person and prov:SoftwareAgent without redundant prov:Agent, and apply the same rule to ExplorationNode and ARA layers. Publish stable concept IRIs and link them through the predicates selected by the profile while retaining existing literal enum fields for compatibility. Keep persistence, REST write payloads, and record lifecycles unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: All core records emit the profile class selected for them; no profile record carries a redundant explicit superclass; custom classes and concepts dereference with correct definitions and hierarchy; concept IRIs are emitted alongside legacy literals; JSON-LD expansion, round-trip fixtures, and the worked sidecar example pass; no database migration or write-contract change is introduced.
close_reason: All core, qualified, provenance, and ARA nodes emit one most-specific type; registered concept IRIs accompany legacy literals; JSON-LD fixture/expansion and full suite pass.

title: Preserve distinct GoalLink slots in project-graph edge identity
description:
GoalLink persistence permits otherwise-identical links in different slots, but project-graph edge IDs omit slot and can collapse those links into one projected edge.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Persist two GoalLinks with the same goal, target, relation, and status but different slots.
2. Build the project graph.
3. Observe that the generated edge identity collides and only one qualified relationship survives the projection.

## Acceptance Criteria
Both links produce distinct stable edges; repeated projection is deterministic; existing single-slot behavior remains compatible where practical; focused collision and non-collision regression tests pass.
design: Build GoalLink projection identity from the full persisted uniqueness tuple, including slot, or from an equally stable canonical link identifier. Keep labels and current wire fields compatible. Coordinate with the structured FigureSpec work in lab-tracker-02e, which makes slot identity more important, but do not absorb that feature.
acceptance_criteria: Two GoalLinks with the same goal, target, relation, and status but different slots produce two distinct stable ProjectGraphEdge records; repeated projection is deterministic; existing single-slot edge IDs remain compatible where practical; focused regression tests cover collision and non-collision cases.
close_reason: Slotted GoalLinks now receive deterministic link-id-qualified project-graph edge IDs while unslotted IDs remain compatible; collision tests pass.

title: Separate project-graph presentation tokens from semantic identifiers
description:
Make the boundary explicit between the frontend-oriented project graph and the public semantic profile. Compact display tokens may remain, but they must not silently become a second uncontrolled ontology.

## Acceptance Criteria
Every emitted node and edge token maps to the semantic profile or has an explicit presentation-only exclusion; differences involving projects, exploration nodes, and external artifacts are intentional and tested; standard provenance and ARA projections share one semantic registry; frontend responses remain compatible.
design: Keep ProjectGraphRead entity_type and relationship wire fields compatible. Centralize mappings from node types to profile classes and from relationship tokens to predicates, qualified-edge kinds, or controlled concepts. Composite UI strings remain presentation identifiers. Reconcile EntityType, ENTITY_TYPE_ORDER, and project-graph node ordering through explicit mappings rather than forcing one enum to serve incompatible use cases. Document any deliberately non-semantic token. Coordinate with lab-tracker-n5kp.12, lab-tracker-n5kp.4, and lab-tracker-cap1.9 without duplicating their scopes.
acceptance_criteria: Every emitted project-graph node and edge token has a tested mapping to the semantic profile or an explicit documented presentation-only exclusion; project, exploration-node, and external-artifact differences are intentional and tested; standard provenance and ARA projections use the same semantic class and relation registry; current frontend graph responses remain compatible; no unconstrained token is treated as a public ontology term by accident.
close_reason: Every project-graph node/edge token now resolves through tested semantic mappings or explicit exclusions; mappings use the shared vocabulary and the wire format remains compatible.

Stand up a hosted demo instance (seeded sample data, ideally read-only or self-resetting) at a stable URL, and make it the first line of the README and the repo homepageUrl. title: Frontend workflow integrity and offline identity
description: Findings from the 2026-07-15 ArjanCodes-style deep review of the React/PWA surface. Protect resource identity, authorization context, queued-job ownership, and mutation outcomes across route changes, concurrent requests, logout/account switching, and offline replay.
design: Model workflows with resource-keyed state and operation-local pending/error results. Persist job ownership but never bearer credentials. Keep server authorization as the backstop while ensuring the UI does not offer or execute actions based on stale project or route state. Extract controllers only after behavior is covered.
acceptance_criteria: All child correctness issues are fixed or explicitly deferred; offline jobs cannot cross identities; stale responses cannot mutate the wrong resource; partial mutations are accurately reported; frontend lint/tests and targeted browser coverage pass.

title: Bind offline upload jobs to an identity without persisting bearer tokens
description:
The IndexedDB upload queue persists the enqueue-time bearer token and may fall back to it when no live token is supplied. Logout can therefore be followed by an upload using the old still-valid credential; after account switching, a new user's token can submit a prior user's queued job and misattribute the capture.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Sign in as user A, enqueue an offline upload, and inspect IndexedDB to find A's bearer token stored with the job.
2. Log out and allow the retry effect to drain without a live token; observe fallback to the persisted token.
3. Alternatively sign in as B and observe the queued A job can be submitted using B's live token.
design: Persist a stable job-owner identity and non-secret request data, never credentials. Drain only with an active session whose identity matches the job owner. Quarantine or explicitly hand off jobs after logout/account switch; do not silently rewrite attribution.
acceptance_criteria: IndexedDB contains no bearer token for newly queued jobs; logout cannot drain with the old credential; account B cannot submit account A's job; matching-user login can intentionally resume its own queue; migration behavior for legacy token-bearing jobs is safe and tested; offline/service-worker tests pass.

title: Key frontend project access to the loaded resource and reject stale membership responses
description:
AppShell derives contribution/management permissions from members of the mutable dashboard-selected project. Membership requests are not sequenced or cancelled and previous membership remains during loading, so a late response can overwrite the current project and direct-linked question/note/session views can receive permissions for the wrong project.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Select project A and delay its members response.
2. Select project B and let B's members response complete first.
3. Release A's response and observe it overwrites membership used to derive B's controls.
4. Open a direct-linked resource from another project and observe controls still use the dashboard-selected project.
design: Create one useProjectAccess(projectId) boundary returning explicit loading/unknown/allowed states, keyed to each resource's own project_id. Sequence or abort requests, clear stale membership immediately, and keep the server as the authorization backstop.
acceptance_criteria: Out-of-order A/B membership responses cannot change B's access; direct-linked resources use their own project_id regardless of dashboard selection; controls are disabled while access is unknown; contributor/owner/admin scenarios and stale-request regression tests pass.

title: Prevent stale graph-draft route state from mutating the wrong draft
description:
GraphDraftDetailCard neither clears changeSet nor rejects stale load responses when changeSetId changes. The previous draft remains actionable while the next route loads, a late old response can overwrite the new state, and mutation handlers target changeSet.change_set_id rather than proving it matches the route.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open graph draft A and, before or after it loads, navigate the same component to draft B while requests are in flight.
2. Observe A remains displayed/actionable or a late A response overwrites B.
3. Trigger a mutation and observe the handler targets changeSet.change_set_id rather than a state proven to match the route.
design: Use an abort/request-generation pattern at the resource gateway, reset route-scoped state immediately, and couple command eligibility to loadedResourceId === routeId. Preserve unsaved-edit UX deliberately rather than through stale component state.
acceptance_criteria: Rapid A→B route changes cannot display A as B or send any mutation to A; late A responses are ignored; actions remain disabled until the loaded ID matches the route; regression tests cover navigation during loading and an in-flight mutation.

title: Replace ambient busy/error state with explicit frontend mutation results
description:
saveOperation catches errors without returning failure, so Accept all continues and later successes can overwrite an earlier error while leaving a partially accepted draft. A shared application-wide busy boolean is also set and cleared by unrelated or nested operations, allowing duplicate non-idempotent submissions while work remains in flight.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In Accept all, make an early saveOperation request fail and a later one succeed.
2. Observe processing continues, the later success can replace the error flash, and the draft is only partially accepted.
3. Start overlapping/nested mutations and observe one finally block clears the shared busy flag while another request remains in flight.
design: Introduce operation-local command state with execute, pending, and typed Result/error. Stop or aggregate Accept all outcomes explicitly; add per-command in-flight guards. Use a counter only for optional global activity indication. Consider a server batch command only if atomic acceptance is a domain requirement.
acceptance_criteria: Accept all never reports blanket success after a partial failure and exposes exactly which operations changed; nested mutations cannot clear another command's pending state; duplicate submissions are prevented for non-idempotent commands; buttons reflect local pending state; focused graph-draft/note tests pass.

title: Resolve AppLink href and programmatic navigation through one prefix rule
description:
AppLink applies the deployed Pages prefix during intercepted navigation but renders the raw unprefixed target in href. Normal clicks work while open-in-new-tab, copied links, modifier clicks, and native navigation can leave /lab-tracker/app for root /app and fail.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Serve the app below a prefix such as /lab-tracker/app.
2. Render an AppLink to /app/graph.
3. Normal click uses prefixed programmatic navigation, but copy the href or open in a new tab and observe navigation to the unprefixed root path.
design: Resolve the application path once and use the same canonical URL for href and navigation. Keep external URLs and browser-native link semantics intact.
acceptance_criteria: Click, copy, modifier-click, and open-in-new-tab resolve identically under root and /lab-tracker prefixes; external links remain untouched; a component-level routing test covers the rendered href and intercepted navigation.

title: Add typed, runtime-validated frontend API gateways
description: The centralized apiRequest layer converts malformed successful envelopes to null or empty lists while downstream components trust raw shapes. Backend contract drift can therefore look like an empty result in one path and a render crash in another.
design: Define domain gateways such as projects.list and datasets.get using generated OpenAPI TypeScript types or checked JSDoc plus runtime validators at the network boundary. Invalid 2xx payloads must fail loudly as typed contract errors; components consume validated domain DTOs.
acceptance_criteria: Representative project, dataset, note, graph-draft, and auth responses are statically described and runtime-validated; malformed 2xx envelopes produce one explicit contract error rather than null/empty data; raw fetch/envelope parsing is not duplicated in feature controllers; lint/tests and generated-contract drift checks pass.

title: Hide auth persistence behind a resilient storage adapter
description:
Initial auth token reads catch unavailable localStorage, but synchronization writes and removals are unguarded. Quota, privacy-mode, or SecurityError failures after a successful login can escape into the top-level error boundary.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the app with localStorage.setItem or removeItem throwing SecurityError or QuotaExceededError.
2. Complete a successful login, token refresh, or logout.
3. Observe the unguarded synchronization write escapes to the application error boundary.
design: Provide one injected auth-storage adapter with symmetric read/write/remove error handling and an in-memory fallback. Surface degraded persistence without discarding a valid live session, and keep logout semantics explicit.
acceptance_criteria: Login, token refresh, and logout remain usable when storage get/set/remove each throw; degraded persistence is observable but does not crash the application; normal persistence behavior is unchanged; tests cover quota and security failures.

title: Extract graph-draft and mobile-capture workflow controllers

The stale-resource, partial-failure, and pending-state defects are symptoms of too many reasons to change.
design: After the correctness beads land, extract reducer/state-machine workflow models, domain commands, browser-media/offline adapters, and small presentational sections. Preserve behavior and avoid a generic component framework; split along actual lifecycle boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Each controller's data loading, command workflow, and browser adapter can be tested without rendering the full page; major view sections are presentational; state-cell count and component size drop materially; existing behavior tests remain green and feature-focused tests own their scenarios.

title: [medium] First-run admin setup in the UI (eliminate raw-HTTP-POST bootstrap)
description:
Creating the first writable account is only possible via a raw HTTP POST to /auth/register with a bootstrap token (routes/auth.py:44-62; schemas.py:140-144); the UI register form only sends username/password (useAuthSession.js:84-99) and public registration creates read-only viewer accounts (mobile-capture.jsx capture buttons disabled on !canWrite). Preserve the commit subject/body, file summary, and a bounded textual diff in the staged evidence note; include a bounded text-asset excerpt in daily-batch model context; render a safe text preview in the review UI; degrade gracefully when the asset is missing or undecodable.
acceptance_criteria: A repository commit captured through lt repo produces a Daily Review narrative that can describe the change rather than listing only its hash; the model receives bounded commit metadata/file summary/diff text; the browser can inspect the bounded source text safely; large files report truncation; non-text assets and unreadable/missing text keep existing behavior; focused backend/client/frontend tests pass.

title: Batch draft generator: configurable provider + OpenAI batch client
description:
Given a batch context packet (from the context builder), call Claude to produce a structured set of proposed graph operations: new nodes, new edges, claim updates, suggested links between notes and existing graph entities, and proposed multi-note merges (e.g. three gel photos -> one observation).

Output is a structured JSON proposal stored as a 'pending batch' record for the review UI. No commits happen ? only proposals.

- Given a context packet, returns a structured proposal set (typed schema)
- Supports multi-note merge proposals
- Supports link proposals (note -> question/session/dataset)
- Stores result as a pending batch with full traceability back to source notes
- Failure modes (model timeout, invalid JSON) handled with retries + dead-letter
notes: Closed with the provider abstraction (GraphDraftClient Protocol + make_graph_draft_client factory) and the OpenAIGraphDraftClient.draft_from_batch method landed in commit 1872618. Settings gain graph_draft_provider (default openai). title: Add claim→question 'answers' relationship (plain answers_question_ids)
description:
Claims have no direct link to the question they answer. Today a claim joins the question hierarchy only transitively via supporting datasets (dataset_question_*), which is ambiguous when a claim draws on datasets addressing different questions. This blocks the questions-first query 'what does the lab currently claim about question X?' and forces the research-group deck to imply a figure/claim->question relationship its edges cannot encode.

Add a plain claim->question 'answers' link: Claim.answers_question_ids: list[UUID]. Verdict (supports/refutes) is inferred from the claim's own statement/status; no outcome_status on the link (decided over the outcome-bearing variant).

Vertical: domain model + ClaimInput; claim_questions association table (mirror claim_datasets/dataset_question_links); mappers; sqlalchemy repository load/save; alembic 0011; schemas ClaimCreate/Update + response; claim_service validation (question in project); routes/claims; MCP create_claim + mcp_api_client; provenance JSON-LD; project_graph edge (claim_question_answers, label 'answers'); presentation_graphs PROJECT_GRAPH_RELATIONSHIPS; the research-group deck JSON + prose; tests across the stack.
design: Relationship string: claim_question_answers; edge direction claim->question; label 'answers'; emitted from project_graph._add_evidence_edges. Storage: claim_questions(claim_id FK->claims CASCADE, question_id FK->questions). No outcome column. Cardinality: list (a claim may answer multiple questions). Surface: retained-v1 core (questions + evidence-linked claims).
acceptance_criteria: answers_question_ids round-trips model<->DB; create_claim (API + MCP) accepts it; service rejects question ids outside the claim's project; project_graph emits claim->question 'answers' edge in full+evidence views; presentation manifest validates with claim_question_answers and the vocabulary test passes; deck JSON uses the answers edge and slide 16 no longer says a figure 'addresses' a question; uv run pytest -q and ruff clean.

title: PI information organization: project groups, people-edges, and portfolio views
description: A PI deploys Lab Tracker with many projects and project-scoped trainees. Today there is no container above Project, no real notion of people (created_by is a free string; the only cross-project tier is global ADMIN), and oversight requires being a global admin. This epic adds an organizing-edge layer — a Lab/project-group container, supervision and ownership edges, and read-only portfolio/lab-health views — without becoming an identity provider, HR system, or grants-management product. Build-vs-buy moat preserved: identity stays offloadable; we own the semantic edges.
design:
CONCEPT: Add the three semantic edges no identity provider models — group ownership, supervision, attribution — onto the existing model; route PI oversight through accessible_project_ids(). No org-chart/HR/IdP/grants-management.

NEW: project_groups (kind=lab) + group_memberships (reuse VIEWER/CONTRIBUTOR/OWNER enum); supervision_edges (dated, own table keyed by user_id, NOT a users column); shadow FK created_by_user_id/executed_by_user_id (additive; string stays, dual-written).
CHANGE: goals.project_id nullable + GoalLink EntityType.PROJECT slot (enum value already exists, models.py:155); accessible_project_ids()/membership_role() group-aware.
REUSE: prov:Agent -> prov:Person/wasAttributedTo/actedOnBehalfOf (export-only); project_graph, decision_context (stays single-project), graph-draft human review, goals.

ACCESS CONTRACT (2.1, asymmetric): group OWNER inherits OWNER on every child project (PI oversight w/o global admin); group VIEWER/CONTRIBUTOR inherit NOTHING unless an explicit per-group group_read_all flag (default false). Direct project membership resolves first; admin short-circuit and >=1-owner-per-project guard untouched.

BOUNDARY: every new edge points at the offloadable users table but adds NO domain column to users itself. Aggregations (portfolio/lab-health) read only over the in-house question/claim/goal graph — not a metrics/ELN dashboard.

PHASES: 0 read-only portfolio (zero schema) -> 1 group container + group-aware access -> 2 attribution FK (isolated) -> 3 spanning goals + supervision + PROV-O people -> 4 offboarding export + ownership reassignment. Each additive, single Alembic head.
notes:
Source: multi-agent design pass (2026-06-15), grounded in db_models.py, services/project_authorization.py, auth.py, provenance.py, docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md, docs/retained-v1-surface.md.
DEFERRED per PI decision (2026-06-15): co-PI / cross-lab / multi-parented projects. Single-parent projects.group_id stands; co-PI handled later by direct per-project membership + goal-level overlap if demand proves it.
NOTE: per-trainee attribution has signal only once multi-user auth (auth_enabled=True) is in use; default local mode collapses all rows to one ADMIN user.

title: Fix portfolio last_activity_at tz-aware/naive HTTP 500 + graph-change-set regression test
description: GET /portfolio/summary returns HTTP 500 for any accessible project that has a graph change set. _latest_activity_at (src/lab_tracker/routes/portfolio.py:122-143) builds a candidate list of tz-aware datetimes (project plus eight entity mappers normalize via as_utc) then calls max(), but change_set_from_model (src/lab_tracker/sqlalchemy_repository_parts/graph_drafts.py:199-200) returns created_at/updated_at WITHOUT as_utc normalization. On SQLite (all tests and local dev) DateTime(timezone=True) returns tz-naive datetimes, so max() over mixed aware/naive raises TypeError. Postgres masks it. Existing tests never create a change set, so it is latent.
design: Defensively normalize each non-None timestamp with as_utc inside _activity_timestamps before max(); additionally normalize change_set_from_model for parity with the other eight mappers (the underlying c1u.5 fix). Add a portfolio route test that creates a graph change set and asserts 200 + correct last_activity_at.
acceptance_criteria: GET /portfolio/summary returns 200 for a project with a graph change set on SQLite; regression test added; change_set_from_model normalized.
notes: Net-new portfolio-specific surface; cross-links lab-tracker-c1u.5 (mapper normalization). Fixing c1u.5 alone resolves the crash but not the route-level guard or the test.

title: Decision: offload auth/RBAC instead of maintaining bespoke identity
description: Entities UserModel, ProjectMembershipModel, DeviceTokenModel, DeviceEnrollmentModel implement identity, project RBAC, and device enrollment in-house. Device enrollment + token is effectively the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628), a fully standardized flow. Maintaining bespoke auth is high-risk and off-core. Candidates: FastAPI-Users (library altitude, likely sweet spot for single-lab deploys), or an IdP such as Keycloak/Authentik (self-host) or Clerk/Auth0 (SaaS) if multi-tenant. Decide whether to offload and at what altitude (library vs service).
design: Apply pointer-not-reimplementation: Lab Tracker keeps project membership/role edges (which user has which role on which project) in the graph, but delegates credential storage, session/token issuance, and the device grant to the chosen provider/library. Avoid running a full IdP unless multi-tenant requirements justify the operational weight.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded decision (offload-to-library / offload-to-IdP / keep-bespoke-with-rationale). If offloading: a migration sketch for existing UserModel/DeviceToken data and a mapping of project roles onto the provider. Operational cost noted for single-lab installs.

title: Add graph context packet size and quality summary
description: Add a compact summary for each graph context packet used in note-to-graph drafting. The summary should help reviewers and developers see what context was available, how large the packet was, which targets were selected, and whether critical derived artifacts were missing.

The summary includes approximate serialized size and selected target IDs/labels. Missing transcript or image/audio artifact warnings are explicit. Draft generation does not quietly hide context builder failures.

title: Lab Health triage flags over portfolio summary

Derived triage flags over /portfolio/summary: stale projects, unanswered questions, datasets without analyses, analyses without claims, unreviewed claims, overdue goals. Read-only over the in-house question/claim/goal graph; explicitly NOT a metrics/experiment-tracker/ELN dashboard.

Depends on the portfolio summary endpoint.

title: Repair schema-invalid batch graph draft operations (GitHub #175)
description: GitHub issue #175 reports two production batch runs failing before review because generated operations did not conform to strict API schemas: create_note omitted required raw_content, then supplied forbidden title. Add deterministic normalization/repair or bounded retry at the model-output boundary so schema-invalid provider output does not strand the whole batch, while preserving the human review gate and strict final validation. Deploy the verified fix to the Lab Tracker applications served from this workstation.
