title: Clarify decision-context ambiguous match window at high volume
description: Follow-up from the rjg1 verification review. lab-tracker-rjg1.2 replaced per-project searches with one scoped matched-project lookup, but the global 500-row match window can narrow ambiguous-project detection when pathological volumes of matches crowd out another matching project. This does not leak data and still auto-resolves to a real match, but the limit should be documented/tested or the lookup should count distinct matching projects more exactly.
acceptance_criteria: Decision-context project auto-resolution has explicit tested behavior when more than 500 scoped question/note matches exist across projects: either widen/count distinct matching project ids so ambiguity is preserved, or document and test the bounded-window behavior; no cross-project leakage; tests pass.

title: [feature] Graph-native "ready work" tool: surface open questions on active goals as the obvious next move
description:
The one genuine FEATURE gap vs Beads. Beads' killer move is `ready`: a short list of unblocked, actionable items that gives an agent an obvious entry action. lab-tracker's `readiness` is infra/DB health (src/lab_tracker/mcp_tools/read.py:19-23), not a work queue, and there is no work-queue tool at all (grep for next_step/ready_question/suggest_next in src/ is empty).

Build a graph-native analog, e.g. `lab_tracker_next_questions` / `open_threads`: active goals -> their active/staged questions not yet answered or linked to a claim -> ranked. This is NOT a 1:1 port: Beads ranks over a task dependency DAG; lab-tracker has goals + questions + notes, so the RANKING SIGNAL is the hard design problem (recency? linked-note count? on the critical path to a goal? question staged vs active?). Medium effort, not trivial.

Value caveat to record on the issue: the payoff is GATED on graph hygiene — if a lab doesn't maintain goals/questions, the tool returns nothing useful. Worth building, but expectations should be set accordingly, and the empty result should itself be informative ("no active goals with open questions — consider creating/activating a goal").
design: Define the candidate set (active goals -> active/staged unanswered questions) and a defensible ranking heuristic; expose as a read-only tool returning a short ranked list with the goal each question advances and why it surfaced. Reuse the decision-context query layer (decision_context_query.py) where possible.
acceptance_criteria: An agent can call one tool and get a short, ranked list of the highest-signal open questions on active goals (with rationale), or an informative empty result; the ranking is documented and tested.

title: Add MATLAB consumer tool parity
description: MATLAB users need a supported consumer-side tool surface equivalent to the Python package component of Lab Tracker. Provide a MATLAB package or toolbox entry point that can connect to a Lab Tracker API instance and capture/register evidence using the retained client-side workflows without adding new backend product concepts.
acceptance_criteria: MATLAB users can configure a Lab Tracker API base URL/token, capture a MATLAB figure as a staged evidence note with source/hash metadata, and run a smoke test or example without requiring Python. Documentation explains installation and usage.

title: GH#79: MCP startup auth probe warns; auth errors self-describing
description: Loud stderr WARN in _ensure_mcp_target_safe on auth-probe 401 (mcp_server.py); distinguish static-key vs login-failed at client boundary (mcp_api_client.py).

title: Remove stale InMemoryStore import from lab_tracker package init
description: src/lab_tracker/__init__.py imports InMemoryStore from lab_tracker.api, but that name was removed during the postgres migration. Any subprocess that imports lab_tracker (including python -m lab_tracker.mcp_server) fails immediately with ImportError. Fix: drop InMemoryStore from the import line and __all__ in __init__.py. Verified via grep that no other module still references it.

title: Decision: integrate an external data-versioning substrate for datasets
description: DatasetModel/DatasetFileModel already capture commit_hash, per-file checksum, and manifest_files plus NWB and BIDS metadata - i.e. bit-level provenance fields - but Lab Tracker has no substrate that produces/stores the bytes. NWB/BIDS signals the neuroscience domain, where DataLad (git-annex) and the DANDI archive are native; DVC and lakeFS are general alternatives. Decide whether dataset bytes + versioning are integrated from an external substrate rather than managed bespoke. Generalizes the earlier idea of a .dvc manifest importer into a pluggable manifest source.
design: Apply pointer-not-reimplementation: an adapter reads an external manifest (.dvc pointer, DataLad dataset, lakeFS commit) into the existing manifest_files/checksum/commit_hash fields, and Lab Tracker keeps the question/claim edges the substrate does not model. Make it an OPTIONAL adapter (one of several manifest sources), not a required dependency - labs that just drop files on a share must still work. Couples one ingestion path to the substrate's file format and only helps labs already using it.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded decision and chosen substrate(s), validated as current. Adapter is optional with a clean no-substrate fallback. Follow-up implementation issue(s) filed (e.g. .dvc/DataLad manifest importer). NWB/BIDS metadata round-trips into the manifest.

title: /groups CRUD and member-management routes
description:
Group CRUD plus group member-management routes (add/remove/change-role), gated by group OWNER. Mirrors the existing project member routes and their validation.

Depends on the group schema.

title: Reload installed app after service worker update
description: Installed Home Screen PWAs can continue rendering an old app bundle after the service worker updates. Make the frontend registration check for updates on boot and reload once when a new worker takes control so the Home Screen icon lands on the current capture UI.

title: HPC analysis capture kit
description:
Build a generic, configurable HPC capture path for Lab Tracker so researchers whose main analysis workflow runs on Slurm/HPC can record durable provenance without copying large outputs or changing their analysis workflow.

The first slice is CLI/docs only: local outbox events sync into staged evidence notes and optional graph drafts. It must preserve the retained-v1 boundary: mechanical provenance can be captured automatically, but graph meaning remains human-reviewed.
design: Client-only v1. Add an lt hpc CLI backed by a lab_tracker_client.hpc module. Use JSON config and offline-first JSON events under .lab-tracker/outbox/hpc/. Store pointers plus summaries, not bulk HPC outputs. Reuse existing note import/upload and graph draft APIs; no server migration or frontend UI.
acceptance_criteria: Users can configure a generic Slurm cluster, capture a run through submit wrapper, script hooks, or watch-folder manifests, and run lt hpc sync to create idempotent staged evidence notes containing scheduler metadata, git context, artifact pointers, summaries, and compact log/metric hints. Optional graph draft generation calls the existing draft endpoint without committing graph changes. Docs include generic Slurm and Bouchet examples. Tests and ruff pass.

title: Design HPC event schema and outbox lifecycle
description: Define the local JSON event shape, sync states, idempotency keys, and retry behavior for generic HPC capture.

title: Implement HPC client outbox core
description: Add client-side config, event models, atomic outbox writes, status inspection, manifest ingestion, and Slurm submission parsing.

title: Add lt hpc init submit begin finish status
description: Expose the core submit wrapper and tiny script-hook flows through the Lab Tracker CLI.

title: Add lt hpc watch-folder capture
description: Allow workflows that only produce output manifests in designated folders to emit the same outbox event format.

title: Sync HPC events into evidence notes and graph drafts
description: Drain outbox events into idempotent staged evidence notes and optionally request graph drafts without graph commits.

title: Document generic Slurm and Bouchet HPC capture
description: Add user docs for generic Slurm setup, Bouchet example config, wrapper/hook/watch modes, manifests, sync, and troubleshooting.

title: Test HPC capture CLI and sync behavior
description: Cover event validation, idempotency, Slurm parsing, CLI flows, note sync, retry, and optional graph draft calls.

title: Deployment, packaging and CI pipeline
description: Deep review 2026-06-12 (gap round): the wheel/Docker image omits sw.js, manifest.json and PWA icons (package-data lists only 4 of 9 bundle files); CI never runs frontend tests/lint/build or a bundle-drift check and only tests the editable install; no dependency lock file exists; the container runs as root and the entrypoint retries failing migrations forever.
notes: P1 child issues completed in this session; epic remains open for remaining P2/P3 follow-up work.

title: Ship all frontend bundle files in the wheel
description: The package-data section in pyproject.toml:44 lists only index.html, app.js, app.css, and styles.css of the nine files in src/lab_tracker/frontend, so the Docker image returns 500 on /app/sw.js and 404 on manifest.json and all PWA icons. Replace the explicit list with a glob and add a packaging test that the wheel file set matches the source directory. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: CI - frontend gates, bundle-drift check, and wheel-install smoke test
description: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs only ruff and pytest on an editable install; npm test/lint/build never run, drift between frontend_src and the committed bundle is undetected, and packaging regressions are invisible because frontend-route tests pass against the source tree (ci.yml:7 and :19). Add npm ci plus lint plus test plus build plus a git diff exit-code check on the bundle, and a wheel-install or docker-build smoke test that curls /app/sw.js. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Commit dependency lock files
description: No uv.lock, compiled requirements, or package-lock.json exists anywhere; runtime dependencies are mostly unpinned (pyproject.toml:10) so CI and every Docker rebuild resolve fresh and float to the newest releases. Commit lock files and use frozen installs in CI and the Dockerfile. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Container hardening - non-root user and bounded migration retries
description: The Dockerfile has no USER directive so the app runs as root (Dockerfile:27), and docker-entrypoint.sh:8 retries a deterministically failing migration 30 times after which the compose restart policy loops the container forever. Add a non-root user and fail fast with a clear log on migration error. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Make packaging guard catch frontend subdirectories
description: Re-review M15: packaging test checks existing package-data paths but cannot detect subdirectory omissions. Add recursive source-vs-wheel coverage or wheel smoke. Details: docs/runs/re-review-2026-06-12.md#M15.

title: Authorization: enforce project-scoped membership on all entity writes
description: Deep review 2026-06-12: notes/goals/graph-drafts enforce per-project contributor membership on writes, but questions, sessions, datasets, analyses, claims, and visualizations gate only on the global EDITOR role and routes use ensure_project_read even for PATCH/DELETE. Any global editor can write to any project; project viewers can mutate/delete. This epic tracks the require_contributor sweep and membership-route fixes.
notes: P1 child issues completed in this session; epic remains open for remaining P2/P3 follow-up work.

title: Require project contributor membership for question/session/dataset writes
description: POST/PATCH/DELETE for questions, sessions, datasets, and dataset files gate on ensure_project_read or nothing (questions.py:43 and :97, sessions.py:50 and :99-183, datasets.py:41 and :85, dataset_files.py), and the services check only the global role (question_service.py:87, session_service.py:84). Any global editor can write into any project and project viewers can mutate/delete. Enforce ProjectAuthorizationPolicy.require_contributor in the services, mirroring NoteService, keeping read gates for GETs. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Require project contributor membership for analysis/claim/visualization writes
description: ClaimService, AnalysisService, and VisualizationService gate mutations on require_role with global WRITE_ROLES only (claim_service.py:65, visualization_service.py:43) while goals/notes use the project-scoped policy. Inject ProjectAuthorizationPolicy and replace the global checks with require_contributor on every create/update/delete/commit path. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Fix PATCH project member semantics - no upsert, validate user exists
description: PATCH /projects/{id}/members/{user_id} (projects.py:226) calls upsert_project_membership which creates a membership when none exists, including for nonexistent user ids, returning 200 instead of 404. Return 404 for non-members and validate the user exists before any membership write. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Fix user enumeration in member-create ordering
description: create_project_member resolves the target user before the owner check that lives inside upsert_project_membership (projects.py:206), so any authenticated user can distinguish 404 user-not-found from 401 owner-required and enumerate usernames. Call ensure_project_owner before resolving the target user. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Make device enrollment consumption atomic
description: DeviceAuthService.consume_enrollment (auth.py:433) loads the enrollment row, checks consumed_at, and only later sets it, with no row lock or conditional update; the public /auth/devices/consume endpoint lets concurrent requests mint multiple device tokens from one QR offer. Use with_for_update or a conditional UPDATE on consumed_at. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Allow project owners to update and delete their projects
description: Re-review M8: ProjectService.update_project/delete_project still use global WRITE_ROLES, so global-viewer project owners pass route ensure_project_owner but fail service authorization, while service callers with global EDITOR can mutate non-member projects. Use ProjectAuthorizationPolicy.require_owner. Details: docs/runs/re-review-2026-06-12.md#M8.

title: GH#8: design spike — smallest-enclosing-assay operator + proxy-debt ledger
description: Produce design-spike doc meeting the acceptance criteria in GH#8 (no retained-v1 entity).

title: Referential-integrity guard: store rename/delete must not orphan store:// references
description: From the y5j8 epic analysis (2026-07-03), verified against main: ExternalArtifactReferences carry a plain store_name string resolved by name at resolve time — no FK, no back-reference, no 'N artifacts reference this store' count anywhere (db_models has no store_name column; references live in JSON on entities). The moment any remove/rename path ships, one action can silently orphan every store-relative reference ever captured. Before DELETE/rename lands: add a reference-count check (scan or index over entity JSON), refuse or warn on destructive ops against referenced stores, and decide rename semantics (forbid vs cascade vs alias). Blocks the DELETE half of the data-store CRUD-completion bead.

title: [medium] Document backup/restore/upgrade procedure for self-hosted instances
description:
A lab running the Docker/Postgres path has no documented way to back up, restore, or safely upgrade; data lives in an undocumented `postgres_data` volume (docker-compose.yml:42) and migrations run automatically on boot (docker-entrypoint.sh:8), so an upgrade can mutate the schema with no prior backup.

Document: where data lives; a `docker compose exec postgres pg_dump` backup recipe and the matching restore; a "back up before you update" note tied to the auto-migrate behavior; and basic restart guidance. Aimed at a non-devops "techy" lab member.

Evidence: docker-compose.yml:42; docker-entrypoint.sh:8; audit barrier #13; lab-manager-deploy persona.
acceptance_criteria: Docs give copy-paste backup and restore commands, state where data lives, and warn to back up before upgrades (which auto-run migrations).

title: Developer-experience & operational hardening
description: Improvements that help the maintainer develop, operate, and safely run Lab Tracker (distinct from end-user features). Ranked by leverage. Headline risk: the default desktop runtime is SQLite (config.py:24) with NO backup path and NO tested restore; the Dolt mirror is export-only CSV (dolt_mirror.py:87-146), not a recovery path. Verified-and-dropped during audit: SQLite FK/WAL pragmas are ALREADY live (db.py:36-44); .env is ALREADY untracked + gitignored (.gitignore:6) with .env.example as the template. Do NOT re-file those.

title: SQLite backup + one-command restore (durability — highest leverage)
description: Eliminate the only unrecoverable-data-loss scenario. Add backup-on-startup in the serve path (cli.py) before alembic upgrade head, plus lab-tracker backup / lab-tracker restore CLI verbs. Correctness musts: WAL is ON (db.py:41) so a naive file copy can miss committed data in the -wal file — use the sqlite3 online-backup API (Connection.backup) or VACUUM INTO. Write at least one copy OFF the live disk/sync folder (backup --to <path> / documented destination) or the backup dies in the same rm/corruption/OneDrive-sync failure it is meant to survive. Prune old snapshots (keep last N); restore must refuse to clobber a live/locked DB.
acceptance_criteria: Backup produces a valid standalone DB while the app is running under WAL; restore refuses to overwrite without confirmation; old snapshots pruned; supports an off-host destination.
notes: Deep review 2026-06-19 independently confirmed this as a HIGH durability gap (finding sweep-integrity-2): the Dolt mirror is export-only and lossy; SQLite deployments have no recovery path. See docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-19.md.

title: Frontend --watch dev script
description: Quality-of-life: add a dev:frontend watch script in package.json around the existing esbuild build (scripts/build-frontend.mjs) to avoid manual rebuilds.

title: Restore roundtrip test: dump -> wipe -> restore -> API roundtrip
description: An untested restore is not a backup. Clone the existing test_migrated_database_supports_api_round_trip pattern in tests/test_migrations.py (~lines 1184-1218) and reuse the conftest.py sqlite fixtures. Prove a restored DB serves the API.

title: CI: add skill-reference drift gate (--check step)
description: The --check flag already exists (scripts/generate_lab_tracker_skill_reference.py:51) but is never run; confirmed absent from .github/workflows/ci.yml. Add a ~3-line step beside the existing frontend-bundle gate so MCP tool docs cannot silently drift from code.

title: Catch-all exception handler that logs unhandled 500s
description: routes/errors.py returns JSON but never calls the logger, and there is no @app.exception_handler(Exception), so a 500 is invisible in logs while /health still reports ok. Add logging inside the existing handlers plus one catch-all, building on the existing structured logging module. Confirm the no-logging finding before implementing.

title: Add pytest-cov (report only, no threshold)
description: Visibility into coverage holes (auth + IndexedDB paths flagged in audit) across the ~535 tests. Add --cov=lab_tracker in pyproject.toml. No gating number yet — just the report.

title: Startup config-summary log line (environment / DB backend / auth)
description: App starts silently. Emit one log line at boot from the existing get_settings() call: environment, database backend, auth enabled. Removes the which-DB-am-I-pointed-at confusion when switching SQLite/Postgres.

title: Enable GitHub branch protection requiring CI
description: Make the existing green CI actually gate merges. Demoted from do-first: low leverage for a solo committer who rebases, and required checks can block your own hotfix when CI is red. Settings change, not code.
notes:
2026-06-19: Could not enable branch protection from this environment. gh is not installed, the GitHub connector returned token_expired, and no GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN is present. Needs authenticated GitHub repository settings access to require the ci workflow checks on main; workflow jobs are test and postgres.
2026-06-19: Resolved later in the same session via Git credential manager-backed GitHub API access. main branch protection now requires test and postgres checks in strict mode with admin enforcement enabled.

title: Seed/demo data script for local development
description: Onboarding friction (not danger). Build on LabTrackerAPI + repository_backed_api() in tests/api_helpers.py to populate a runnable demo dataset.

title: Add Dependabot config
description: Drop in .github/dependabot.yml. Pure buy-not-build, free, low urgency for a solo self-hosted app.

title: Update nanoid transitive dependency for GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8
description: PR #202 CI fails before tests because npm audit reports nanoid 3.3.16, pulled transitively through Vitest, Vite, and PostCSS. Update the lockfile to resolve nanoid at 3.3.17 or newer without broad dependency churn.
design: Use the smallest supported npm lockfile update. Confirm the dependency path, audit result, and that frontend behavior remains unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: npm audit --audit-level=high exits successfully; npm ls nanoid reports 3.3.17 or newer; frontend test, lint, and build gates pass; PR #202 CI is green.
close_reason: Updated nanoid to 3.3.18 with a minimal lockfile-only change; audit, dependency tree, frontend gates, and PR #202 CI passed.

title: serve_app test asserts hardcoded DB URL, fails under a local .env override
description: tests/test_lab_tracker_init.py::test_serve_app_runs_migrations_schedules_browser_and_starts_server (assertion ~line 429) asserts that serve_app calls create_sqlite_backup with the literal 'sqlite+pysqlite:///./lab_tracker.db'. It does NOT monkeypatch LAB_TRACKER_DATABASE_URL, so when a developer has a local .env (untracked) overriding the DB URL — e.g. LAB_TRACKER_DATABASE_URL=sqlite+pysqlite:///./demo_capture.db — the test fails with a URL mismatch. CI passes because it has no .env. Surfaced while validating the backup-hardening work (lab-tracker-gs6a); pre-existing and unrelated to that change. Fix: monkeypatch.setenv the database URL (or monkeypatch get_settings) so the test is deterministic, or assert against get_settings().database_url instead of a hardcoded literal.
acceptance_criteria: Test passes regardless of any local .env LAB_TRACKER_DATABASE_URL value (e.g. with demo_capture.db set).

title: Feature A: figure-capture consumer client (lt.savefig / capture_figures), slice 1
description: New in-package module src/lab_tracker_client/figure.py: lt.savefig(fig, path) drop-in + capture_figures() context manager + self-expiring run_context() + FigureCaptureResult. Real save runs FIRST; one outermost guard so capture NEVER raises; no network when unconfigured; capture-specific 2-3s timeout + per-process circuit breaker + one-shot warnings. Canonical record = source URI + sha256 of the full figure (evidence_* metadata); a bounded review image rides on a STAGED note via POST /notes/upload-file; never a Visualization (Birth Requirement deferred to human promotion). Coalesce-by-stable-logical-path via non-hash-qualified client_capture_id. matplotlib/Pillow optional [figure] extra, lazy Agg-only. No server change/migration in slice 1. Realizes planned FigureSpec slots (lab-tracker-02e); run/git capture aligns with lab-tracker-jxb; the deferred Visualization content-hash pointer relates to lab-tracker-6lx. Adding the symbols to __all__ flips Feature B's figure-idiom gate on.

title: figure.py core: FigureCaptureResult + fail-soft guard + circuit breaker + savefig pointer upload
description: Create src/lab_tracker_client/figure.py: FigureCaptureResult (frozen dataclass modeled on EvidenceImportResult, to_dict()); a capture-specific 2-3s timeout + FIGURE_PREVIEW_MAX_BYTES; ONE outermost guard so capture NEVER raises (catches LTAPIError/LTValidationError/connect/timeout AND a 403-not-a-contributor); a per-process circuit breaker tripped on connect/timeout that short-circuits to sidecar; one-shot stderr warnings in the FIGURE layer (the shared client has a 15s timeout and no breaker). No network when unconfigured (no resolvable project_id/base_url/token). savefig(fig, path, ...) does the REAL save FIRST, then a pointer-only STAGED-note upload via the private LabTracker._upload_note_file_payload (in-package; isolate behind one helper) using build_evidence_metadata; the full-figure sha256 and source URI are KEYS in the metadata mapping, NOT separate kwargs. Also add a private client PATCH helper (_request('PATCH', '/notes/{id}', json=...)) that A3 coalescing needs (no such method exists today).
design: fig=None means the caller already wrote the file (hash from disk). _upload_note_file_payload accepts in-memory bytes so a rendered preview never needs a temp file.
acceptance_criteria: savefig never raises on LTAPIError 500, ConnectError, TimeoutException, or 403-not-contributor (result populated, file still on disk); the capture client timeout <=3s; after one connect failure the breaker opens and the next call makes ZERO network attempt; 10 misconfig calls emit exactly ONE warning; the staged note has status=='staged', evidence_source_uri == saved-path URI, evidence_content_hash == full-figure sha256, and NO analysis_id/dataset/Visualization linkage.

title: Bounded review image (full bytes under cap else downscaled preview) + optional [figure] extra
description: A bounded review image rides to review: full bytes when under a size cap (clamped to the server max_upload_bytes); else a downscaled PNG rendered from the held matplotlib Figure via an Agg canvas (NEVER pyplot) with Pillow; else pointer-only + a no_preview flag. All imaging imports lazy inside functions. Add [project.optional-dependencies] figure = ['matplotlib', 'pillow'] to pyproject.toml. Lab Tracker must never become the durable store of the full figure.
acceptance_criteria: Under-cap uploads the FULL bytes (no_preview False); over-cap with imaging libs uploads a downscaled PNG under the cap while evidence_content_hash stays the FULL figure hash; over-cap without imaging libs falls to pointer-only no_preview with a one-shot no-matplotlib warning; importing figure.py works with imaging libs absent.

title: Stable client_capture_id + latest-wins (metadata) coalescing + stale-bytes flag
description: Coalesce-by-logical-path via a STABLE non-hash-qualified client_capture_id (explicit logical_id else project-relative POSIX path, figure: prefixed, no absolute machine paths). CRITICAL: the server is FIRST-WINS (note_service returns the first existing note and discards new bytes; there is no raw-asset-replace endpoint) AND update_note REPLACES the whole metadata dict (does NOT merge). So on a changed-bytes re-save: read the existing note's FULL metadata, merge refreshed evidence_content_hash + content_hash_current + run/git keys client-side, and PATCH the COMPLETE merged dict via the A1 PATCH helper; the stored review-image bytes stay first-captured (documented degradation). FigureCaptureResult must expose a machine-readable stale-bytes flag. version_every_change=True (opt-in) uploads a new note with a version-qualified id.
acceptance_criteria: Unchanged bytes -> one note, second action=coalesced; changed bytes (default) -> one note whose metadata hash refreshes WHILE evidence_source_uri and all first-capture evidence_* keys SURVIVE the PATCH; client_capture_id is not hash-qualified; the result carries the stale-bytes flag; version_every_change=True -> a second note; path resolution leaks no absolute machine path.

title: Self-expiring run_context (git/run as scalar metadata) + capture_figures diff scoping
description: Add run_context(*, ttl_seconds=1800, extra=None): capture git HEAD + dirty-flag + timestamp via subprocess (swallow all errors to empty/None), store in a process-local ContextVar that auto-expires at read time and clears on __exit__ even when the body raises; flatten into note metadata as SCALAR keys only (client._validate_metadata rejects nested values). NO Analysis is created (anti-scope MLflow-lite; run/git ride as pointer metadata, aligning with lab-tracker-jxb). Add capture_figures(...) snapshotting mtimes on enter and diffing on exit (in finally, never masking a body exception), running the fail-soft core per new/modified image with per-file stable ids.
acceptance_criteria: Absent/failing git yields empty/None and capture proceeds; metadata is scalar-flat and passes _validate_metadata; a stale context after ttl is treated as expired; context clears on __exit__ even when the body raises; capture_figures body exception still runs the finally diff-capture and does not mask it; the diff picks up new + modified, ignores untouched.

title: Flip __all__ gate (export figure symbols) + package docstring + record retained-v1 contract
description: Add a second import block in src/lab_tracker_client/__init__.py: from lab_tracker_client.figure import FigureCaptureResult, RunContext, capture_figures, run_context, savefig; add the five names to __all__ (this auto-activates Feature B's figure-idiom section through the gate) + figure lines in the package docstring. Per the locked decision symbols become a committed public contract on entering __all__, so record the savefig/capture_figures/run_context retained-v1 surface entry in docs/retained-v1-surface.md in THIS change (not a follow-up). Must land AFTER Feature B's generator + gate tests exist.
acceptance_criteria: The five symbols are importable and in __all__; with the gate flipped code_facing_idioms() emits the figure section (Feature B gate-on test now satisfied by real __all__); FigureCaptureResult.to_dict() matches the EvidenceImportResult template; savefig forwards **kwargs to fig.savefig; the retained-v1 surface entry is present.

title: Deferred: content-hash-bearing external pointer on Visualization for figure promotion
description: So human promotion of a captured figure note -> Visualization can carry evidence_source_uri + evidence_content_hash onto the node (today Visualization has only a bare file_path + asset_checksum). Adds external_source_uri/external_content_hash to VisualizationModel + Visualization + create params + the create route + a migration. Relates to lab-tracker-6lx (machine-local-path portability).
acceptance_criteria: Promotion carries the captured URI + content hash onto the Visualization; migration chains off the single alembic head; PROV-O export includes the pointer; tests + ruff pass.

title: Deferred: server endpoint to replace a staged note raw asset by client_capture_id
description: Enables TRUE byte-level latest-wins for figure coalescing. Slice 1 is metadata-only because the server is first-wins with no raw-asset-replace endpoint, so a re-saved figure's review-image bytes stay first-captured. This adds the endpoint + client wrapper to replace bytes for an existing staged note keyed by client_capture_id.
acceptance_criteria: A staged note's raw asset can be replaced by client_capture_id; figure coalescing can refresh the review image, not just metadata; auth/contributor gating preserved; tests + ruff pass.

title: Deferred: @track_figure decorator for centralized save helpers
description: Convenience decorator wrapping a lab's own save_figure() helper, built on the Feature A capture core. Deferred from slice 1 (the drop-in + context manager lead). Lower-touch for labs that already centralize saving.
acceptance_criteria: @track_figure wraps a save helper and routes through the same fail-soft capture core; documented; tests + ruff pass.

title: Deferred: opt-in autotrack() global savefig interception (kill-switchable)
description: Opt-in, explicitly-enabled, kill-switchable (LAB_TRACKER_AUTOTRACK=off) monkeypatch of Figure.savefig for retrofitting legacy scripts with zero per-call edits. Deferred and most fragile (matplotlib version matrix, long-lived kernels); ships last, behind an explicit call, never default, and must NOT auto-stamp analysis/question lineage from ambient context.
acceptance_criteria: autotrack() is opt-in with a documented kill switch; never default; never fabricates lineage; scoped/restorable; documented as a retrofit convenience; tests + ruff pass.

title: Compare GPT-5.6 proposal settings and switch to Sol xhigh standard
description: After the initial gpt-5.6-sol max+pro trial, compare representative Lab Tracker proposal quality and reviewer burden against Sol xhigh+standard and Terra xhigh+standard, then switch both served instances to gpt-5.6-sol with reasoning effort xhigh and reasoning mode standard unless the observed evidence supports a different choice. Preserve the shared credential and 5400-second timeout; recreate app containers only and verify both public services plus Marion's invitation/data state.
design: Automation should change settings only if the deployments still use the expected max+pro trial configuration. Do not overwrite intervening operator changes blindly. Never print credentials or recreate Postgres.
acceptance_criteria: A representative comparison is recorded or its absence is stated; both served app instances use gpt-5.6-sol xhigh+standard unless evidence justifies another documented choice; shared credential and 90-minute timeout remain; app-only recreation succeeds; public health and Marion state are verified.
notes: No new paid provider comparison was run: the prior max+pro 100-note batch spent about 15 minutes before failing schema validation, and the operator explicitly requested a cheaper mechanism. Applied the task's prescribed gpt-5.6-sol xhigh+standard setting to both served app containers, preserving the shared credential and 5400-second timeout. Recreated app containers only; both local and public health checks passed; primary and Marion database row counts were identical before/after; Josh Chen, Yuanchi Ha, and Marion invitation states remained intact. Persisted the Marion Compose setting; the primary legacy served instance was recreated with its deployment overlay because the current generic root Compose intentionally does not embed provider credentials/config.

title: Consumer automation and client-boundary reliability
description: Findings from the 2026-07-15 ArjanCodes-style deep review of the Python consumer, MCP client, watch/repo/HPC automation, and capture helpers. Eliminate poisoned queues, misleading helper semantics, process-global lifecycle traps, and duplicated transport behavior that diverges across unattended workflows.
design: Keep public SDK and MCP façades use-case specific, but share narrow transport/outbox mechanisms. Make ownership and lifecycle explicit, failures observable, retries idempotent, and large uploads streaming. Preserve fail-soft capture only where it does not silently disable later healthy work.
acceptance_criteria: All child reliability issues are fixed or explicitly deferred; unattended queues make progress past bad records; client objects have explicit safe lifetimes; write helpers are honest; SDK/MCP transport behavior is consistent; relevant regression tests pass.

title: Unify outbox draining so bad or terminal records cannot starve pending work
description:
watch.py, repo.py, and hpc.py each decode event files before the per-record recovery block and slice the oldest files before filtering terminal states. One malformed/unsupported record aborts every later record; with a limit, an already-synced oldest record can starve pending work forever. Scheduled --fail-silent runs can hide the stall, and the three copies already differ in temporary-file safety.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Put an already-synced event a.json before pending b.json and drain with limit=1; repeat and observe b.json is never processed.
2. Separately put malformed a.json before valid b.json.
3. Drain through watch, repo, or HPC sync and observe the decode exception aborts the batch before b.json.
design: Extract one typed Outbox component with an injected event codec and processor. Decode/validate/process inside a per-record boundary, quarantine unreadable events with an observable error, select actionable events before applying limit, and use unique atomic writes plus explicit concurrency control.
acceptance_criteria: Corrupt-first/valid-second drains the valid record and quarantines/reports the corrupt one; terminal-first with limit=1 reaches the first pending record; watch/repo/HPC share the same tested semantics; concurrent writers cannot collide or truncate records; scheduled runs expose durable failure status even when console output is suppressed.

title: Remove process-global client lifecycle traps from capture helpers
description:
Figure capture uses a permanent process-global circuit flag: one transient endpoint failure skips all later captures, including calls with a healthy explicit client. Separately, the exported lazy singleton can be used as a context manager that closes its cached httpx client without clearing the cache, leaving subsequent module-level helpers attached to a closed client.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Cause one savefig call to fail with a connection error.
2. Call savefig with a healthy explicit client and observe it is skipped because the process-global circuit is open.
3. Separately use the exported lazy client in a with block, exit it, then call a module-level helper and observe reuse of the closed httpx client.
design: Give circuit-breaker state explicit per-client/per-endpoint ownership with cooldown, half-open retry, observability, and reset. Remove context-manager ownership from the global proxy or make each context own a fresh client and clear it deterministically. Request timeouts must not mutate a shared client's private timeout state.
acceptance_criteria: A failed capture against endpoint A does not skip a healthy explicit client/endpoint B; a breaker recovers after its cooldown/half-open probe; concurrent captures do not race on shared timeout state; using the exported proxy in supported patterns cannot leave a closed cached client; environment/profile changes are observed after recreation; regression tests cover each lifecycle.

title: Default consumer writes to staged and make human transitions explicit
description:
LabTracker.upsert_question defaults to ACTIVE while upsert_note and the lt note command default to COMMITTED, contradicting canonical server defaults and generated guidance that agents may stage evidence but must not accept or commit it. A caller can cross the human gate by omitting a status argument.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call LabTracker.upsert_question without status and inspect the created question; it is active.
2. Call LabTracker.upsert_note or lt note without status and inspect the created note; it is committed.
3. Compare with the server create defaults, which stage both records.
design: Omit status by default and inherit the server's canonical staged state. Expose activation/commit as separately named commands requiring explicit caller intent. Keep backwards compatibility only through deliberate opt-in arguments with migration notes.
acceptance_criteria: Python helper, CLI, MCP guidance, and server defaults agree that new agent/consumer questions and notes are staged; activate/commit requires an explicit named operation; tests prove omission cannot activate/commit; generated skill/reference documentation reflects the behavior.

title: Make upsert helpers atomic and honest about conflicting input
description: upsert_project and upsert_question are client-side list-then-create operations. Concurrent callers can create duplicates, and an existing natural-key match is returned while changed description, status, type, hypothesis, or parents are silently ignored. The current name promises update semantics the implementation does not provide.
design: Choose an explicit contract: rename to get_or_create with a created/reused outcome and conflict detection, or implement a server-side atomic upsert/idempotency command. Compare canonical supplied fields; never silently discard conflicting intent. Coordinate with MCP natural-key disclosure without assuming database uniqueness for every domain entity.
acceptance_criteria: Ambiguous retries and concurrent identical calls produce one canonical entity or a deterministic conflict; changed canonical fields are updated or rejected explicitly rather than ignored; return values distinguish created/reused/updated; pagination cannot hide a match; compatibility and concurrency tests pass.

title: Share a narrow streaming HTTP transport across SDK and MCP clients
description: lab_tracker_client.client and lab_tracker.mcp_api_client independently implement configuration, authentication, retries, pagination, endpoint envelopes, and error translation, and their behavior has diverged. Multiple public upload methods also materialize entire files before the server's 100 MB guard can reject them.
design: Extract a neutral wire/transport layer for auth, request execution, pagination, envelopes, and typed errors while retaining separate use-case façades. Stream file handles through httpx, preflight known sizes, and define retry behavior for non-rewindable bodies. Keep server/domain dependencies out of the consumer contract package where practical.
acceptance_criteria: SDK and MCP clients share one tested transport behavior for auth, pagination, errors, and retries; note/visualization uploads do not read entire files into memory and reject oversize inputs before transfer; bounded-memory tests cover large files; public façade compatibility is documented and tested.

title: Bulk onboard/offboard across the projects in a group
description:
Onboard or offboard a user across all projects in a group in one unit_of_work; offboard fails loudly on sole-owner projects and never silently orphans work. Pairs with the offboarding guard so a membership revoke cannot strand the work of a departing member. Relates to the existing last-owner invariant work (lab-tracker-cq5.6, lab-tracker-fee.3).

title: Add phone-first audio daily review with voice feedback
description: Let a reviewer listen to a daily graph review on a phone and respond without navigating a dense desktop form. Reuse the existing graph-draft revision endpoint and microphone feedback path; add on-device narration of the review summary/proposals, compact touch-friendly controls, and focused batch-detail presentation.
design: Use the browser SpeechSynthesis API for on-device narration (no stored/generated audio or backend dependency). Build a deterministic spoken script from the review summary, proposals, rationale, and uncertainty prompts. Keep voice feedback on the existing multipart /graph-drafts/{id}/revise path. Preserve full proposal decisions and provenance below the compact console; gracefully omit narration controls where speech synthesis is unsupported.
acceptance_criteria: A batch review exposes Listen/Pause/Resume/Stop controls when speech synthesis is supported; a user can record, preview, remove, and submit voice feedback from the compact review surface; the review route is touch-friendly and focused on small screens; speech and microphone resources are stopped on navigation; frontend tests cover narration script/controls and voice feedback submission; frontend lint/test/build pass.

title: Make graph-draft payload contract complete for all entities
description: Veritas production graph-context drafting produced 153 failed change sets. Failures are API-schema mismatches across question, goal, dataset, analysis, and note payloads (missing required text/question_type/goal_type/primary_question_id/raw_content and forbidden presentation or identifier fields such as preview, question_id, note_id, content, title, project_id, label). Add a provider-facing payload contract derived from the strict request schemas, reuse trusted validation retry for per-note and analysis drafts, preserve strict final validation and the human commit gate, and cover representative production failures.

All graph-draft provider prompts now include a compact payload contract derived from strict API schemas; graph-context and analysis drafting use bounded trusted-feedback retries; strict validation and human commit gates remain unchanged. title: [quick-win] Document admin bootstrap + member promotion in plain English
description:
The single most load-bearing deployment step has zero user documentation: the first writable (admin) account can only be created via a raw HTTP POST to /auth/register with a bootstrap token (routes/auth.py:44-62; schemas.py:140-144), because the UI register form only sends username/password (useAuthSession.js:84-99) and public registration yields read-only viewer accounts. The lab-manager persona hit this as a brick wall.

Until the UI fix (separate issue) lands, document the exact sequence in plain English in README/docs: set LAB_TRACKER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_TOKEN, the curl recipe to create the first admin, and how an admin then promotes lab members from viewer to editor. Include a copy-paste block.

Evidence: routes/auth.py:44-62; schemas.py:140-144; useAuthSession.js:84-99; .env.example LAB_TRACKER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_TOKEN; audit barriers #8 and #9; lab-manager-deploy persona.
acceptance_criteria: A "techy" lab member can follow documented steps to create the first admin and promote members to editor without reading source code.

title: Decision: ELN boundary - integrate/link rather than become a lab notebook
description: NoteModel/NoteTargetModel plus project organization overlap heavily with Electronic Lab Notebooks (eLabFTW, Benchling, RSpace, LabArchives) - the biggest mindshare overlap but the worst conceptual fit, since ELNs are document-centric while Lab Tracker is graph-centric. Decide the boundary: integrate with / link out to an ELN, or deliberately avoid ELN scope creep - but do NOT become an ELN.
design: Apply pointer-not-reimplementation: where a lab already uses an ELN, a note can reference an ELN entry (URI + hash) and Lab Tracker keeps the edges the ELN does not model - which question/claim/dataset the note attaches to (NoteTargetModel). Keep the human-gated note-to-graph draft->commit flow (GraphChangeSet/GraphChangeOperation) in-house as a differentiator. Resist adding rich-document/editor features that pull toward becoming an ELN.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded decision (integrate-with-ELN / link-only / stay-standalone-and-bounded). Explicit list of note features in-scope vs out-of-scope (anti-ELN guardrail) added to retained-v1 surface. If integrating, a target ELN identified and its entry-reference shape defined.

title: Harden SQLite backup/restore: cooperative live-server lock + cross-platform read-only URI
description:
Deep review of the merged backup/restore code (src/lab_tracker/backup.py, PR range 140feda..f64ecc8) found a blocking data-integrity defect plus two related backup defects.

BLOCKING: restore_sqlite_backup()'s _assert_database_not_locked() probes with BEGIN EXCLUSIVE, but SQLite locks are transaction-scoped, not connection-scoped. The server runs WAL mode with a SQLAlchemy pool whose connections sit idle between requests; an idle connection does NOT block BEGIN EXCLUSIVE. So a --force restore against a *running* server passes the guard, deletes the live -wal/-shm sidecars, and os.replace()s the DB file under the live process -> torn DB / corruption. The only test holds an ACTIVE BEGIN EXCLUSIVE, so it never exercises the realistic idle-pool state.

RELATED 1: _copy_sqlite_database builds the read-only source URI as f'file:{as_posix()}?mode=ro'. On Windows as_posix() yields C:/... producing a RELATIVE 'file:C:/...' URI (must be file:///C:/...). Paths containing ? or # are also unescaped, silently producing an EMPTY backup that passes integrity_check. POSIX CI never catches it.

RELATED 2: _assert_sqlite_integrity opens the restore source read-WRITE (no mode=ro), touching mtime and potentially spawning sidecars; the backup copy path already uses mode=ro.
design: Cooperative OS advisory lock. New module process_lock.py provides a cross-platform best-effort exclusive ProcessLock (fcntl.flock on POSIX, msvcrt.locking on Windows) on a <db>.lock sidecar; the OS releases it on process exit so a crash leaves no stale lock. The running server acquires it for its lifetime in make_lifespan() (best-effort, sqlite-only, never crashes startup; Postgres/:memory: get no lock). The offline restore process acquires the same lock non-blocking around the destructive section and refuses if it cannot (server is live). BEGIN EXCLUSIVE retained as a secondary active-transaction check. URI fixes: a single _sqlite_ro_uri() helper uses Path.as_uri() (emits file:///C:/... and percent-encodes ?/#) + '?mode=ro', used by both _copy_sqlite_database and _assert_sqlite_integrity (now read-only).
acceptance_criteria: restore refuses when a ProcessLock on <db>.lock is held (test simulates a live idle server, no active txn); existing active-BEGIN-EXCLUSIVE refusal still passes; _copy_sqlite_database round-trips a path containing '?'; _sqlite_ro_uri emits a valid absolute file:// URI for a Windows drive-letter path and encodes special chars; full pytest + ruff green; lifespan lock does not disturb the existing TestClient integration suite.

description: Audit of src/lab_tracker/frontend_src/features/graph-drafts.jsx (the AI-revise composer, separate surface from mobile capture) found three confirmed recording defects: (1) record-reentrancy-stream-leak (medium): startRecording (536-579) is async and only sets isRecording=true AFTER getUserMedia resolves (573); a second click during the permission/await window re-enters and overwrites audioStreamRef/mediaRecorderRef without stopping the first stream -> leaked live mic MediaStream + orphaned MediaRecorder. Fix: set an in-flight flag before awaiting and bail if refs already populated. (2) stop-button-gated-by-caneditdraft (medium): the single toggle button is disabled={!canEditDraft} (918); if an operation action flips changeSet.status mid-recording, Stop becomes unreachable and the mic stays live until unmount. Fix: disabled={isRecording ? false : !canEditDraft} or a useEffect that stops recording when canEditDraft goes false. (3) dictate-not-gated-by-canrecordaudio (low): button not gated by canRecordAudio(), so on unsupported browsers it looks enabled and only fails on click. Fix: const recordingSupported=canRecordAudio(); disabled={!canEditDraft || !recordingSupported}. Found by capture-ui-audit workflow; all three adversarially verified high-confidence.

title: PI lab-health visibility: capture state-transition data for review
description: Backend records current state but rarely WHEN or WHY state changed, so PI review questions about latency, queue depth, time-in-status, decision loops, and zombie projects are unanswerable despite visible counts. This epic captures human-gated transition moments (reviews, decisions, QC verdicts, blocked reasons, status changes) plus epistemic-trust tags, then derives metrics from the existing portfolio aggregation (routes/portfolio.py) and PROV-O traversal. Commodity domains (protocols, rigs, QC reports, colony, inventory) stay pointer-plus-edge or are declined per docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md. Sourced from the 2026-06-16 gap analysis against the lab systems-design doc.
design: Five phases by leverage-per-effort. Phase 0 = pure derivation (no migration). Phases 1-3 = the moat capture. Phase 4 = gated on demonstrated lab demand. DECLINE LIST (do NOT build): animal/colony manager, reagent inventory, equipment/calibration registry, full protocol/ELN entity, generic blocker/task/PM system, HR/career/conflict-case fields, standing RBAC authority matrix, QC computation/dashboards, automated kill-criteria evaluation, configurable workflow stages. Where the doc wants visibility into these, capture only the reason/pointer, never the system of record.

(2) Capture goal status transitions so time-in-status is derivable. (3) Widen GoalStatus with under_review, in_revision, rejected.
design: TIGHTEN (scope review): keep next_action to one action + one owner (no due dates/subtasks). For status transitions, prefer a Note targeting the goal with status metadata (reuse NoteTarget) over a new event table; explicitly forbid generalizing into an activity feed. The same status-timing need recurs for Claim (no decided_at today) - solve once with the chosen minimal pattern. Widened enum stays small/fixed.

acceptance_criteria: Handoff records the scientific contract + decision_needed + known_issues; metadata_complete/qc_status derived by reference; handoff-to-analysis latency derivable; no PM workflow surface; migration single-head.

title: Phase 4: Authorship/contribution record for outputs (Rec 9)
description: Add Authorship(authorship_id, goal_id FK, user_id FK nullable, external_person_name str|None, author_position Int|None, contribution_roles JSON using CRediT taxonomy, status: proposed|agreed|disputed, created_by_user_id). Attribution is in the moat and reduces authorship ambiguity. Enables per-person authorship-load metrics.
design: TIGHTEN (scope review): status=disputed is the ONLY conflict hook - NO HR case management or grievance workflow. external_person_name is strictly an attribution string, no other person fields. contribution_roles uses fixed CRediT taxonomy, not a lab-configurable role set.
acceptance_criteria: Authors recorded per goal with position + CRediT roles + status; disputed surfaces for PI attention; no HR/grievance surface; migration single-head.

title: Phase 4: CriticalSystem + owner/backup roles + verified-handoff extension (Rec 10)
description: Make single-points-of-failure visible. CriticalSystem(system_id, name, kind: rig|pipeline|protocol|infrastructure|institutional_knowledge|other, group_id FK, status: active|retired) + SystemRole(system_id, user_id, role: owner|backup). Recovery-path edge via NoteTarget(role=recovery_path). Extend OwnershipReassignment with system_id FK nullable, handoff_kind (real|rehearsal), outcome (pending|verified|failed), verified_at. SPOFs = systems with backup count 0 (derived).
design: TIGHTEN (scope review - largest/highest-drift item): CriticalSystem holds NO inventory fields (no serial/vendor/cost/calibration) - it is purely a named locus of human-owned risk. kind is a small fixed enum. Reuse User FKs like SupervisionEdge; reuse NoteTarget for recovery-path. The OwnershipReassignment extension is independent and cheap - it can ship FIRST and alone.
acceptance_criteria: Critical systems recorded with owner/backup; unbacked systems and missing recovery paths derivable; OwnershipReassignment records verified handoffs; no equipment-registry fields; migration single-head.

title: Phase 4: expected_departure_date departure-hardening signal (Rec 11)
description: Add a single optional expected_departure_date so the PI can harden ~6 months before someone leaves. Store it on a planned (outcome=pending) OwnershipReassignment row, NOT as a User column.
design: TIGHTEN (scope review): this is the SINGLE HR-adjacent concession - capture ONLY this one date. NO employment status, contract, salary, or leave fields. Keeps HR fields off the minimal User entity. Derives a departure-hardening-due flag crossed against unbacked CriticalSystems the person owns.
acceptance_criteria: A planned departure date recordable without adding HR fields to User; departure-hardening-due flag derivable; depends on CriticalSystem; migration single-head.

title: Phase 4: Onboarding checklist anchored to a reproduce-a-result provenance hook (Rec 12)
description: Add Onboarding(onboarding_id, user_id FK, group_id FK, started_at, completed_at nullable, status) + OnboardingStep(onboarding_id, label, status: todo|done, order, reproduces_analysis_id FK nullable, reproduces_claim_id FK nullable). The reproduce-a-known-result first task points at the prior Analysis/Claim, tying onboarding into the provenance spine.
design: TIGHTEN (scope review - lowest leverage, strongly consider deferring): the provenance hook is the ONLY thing keeping this in scope. Anchor every step to the provenance spine; keep OnboardingStep minimal (no due dates, assignees, free-form checklist proliferation). Must not become a standing task/checklist product. Completion of the reproduce step is derived-verifiable against whether a new Analysis re-supports the Claim.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding tracked with steps anchored to Analysis/Claim provenance; reproduce-a-result step verifiable; no generic checklist/PM surface; migration single-head.

title: Phase 0: GET /portfolio/queues (dominant-constraint view)
description: Read-only aggregation surfacing the lab dominant constraint: analysis queue, claim-review queue, writing queue, question backlog, each with depth, median age, p95 age, oldest item.
design: Derive: analysis queue = committed Dataset with no committed Analysis via AnalysisDataset join; claim-review = Claim.status=proposed; writing = Goal.status in {planned,in_progress} for paper/grant; backlog = Question.status in {staged,active}. Sits alongside existing /portfolio/summary. No schema change.
acceptance_criteria: Endpoint returns each queue with depth and age percentiles from existing timestamps; no new storage.

title: Phase 0: derived portfolio metrics (latency, figure-freshness, missing-metadata)
description: Add derived metrics/flags: dataset-to-analysis latency (median/p95), figure-freshness (viz older than its analysis code_version), and a committed_datasets_missing_metadata triage flag.
design: latency from DatasetModel.created_at vs AnalysisModel.executed_at via AnalysisDatasetModel join (document that executed_at is user-supplied, not wall-clock). figure-freshness from Visualization vs Analysis timestamps. missing-metadata from emptiness of manifest_metadata/nwb/bids on committed datasets; define required minimally (non-empty) to avoid a metadata schema registry. Extend the triage-flag pattern in routes/portfolio.py.
acceptance_criteria: Metrics computed read-time from existing data and exposed via portfolio surfaces; missing-metadata is a triage flag; no schema change.

title: Phase 1: blocked/waiting-on annotation on Project (Rec 2)
description: Add a lightweight blocked annotation so every wait is attributed to a cause: blocked_reason enum (awaiting_pi_review|awaiting_analysis|awaiting_equipment|awaiting_animals_genotype|awaiting_reagents|awaiting_decision|awaiting_handoff|other|null), blocked_since DateTime|None, waiting_on_user_id FK|None. Primary on Project; optionally Session and Goal. Splits the catch-all stale_project flag into idle-vs-blocked and produces the queue taxonomy; surfaces colony/reagent waits by NAMED REASON without building those systems.
design: Keep it ONE structured annotation: no comment threads, no assignment workflow, no subtasks. Enum stays closed/fixed (not lab-customizable). wait-time-by-cause = now - blocked_since grouped by blocked_reason (derived).
acceptance_criteria: Project can be marked blocked with reason + since + waiting_on; portfolio derives wait-time-by-cause and idle-vs-blocked; enum is fixed; Alembic migration added; alembic heads stays single.

title: Phase 1: protocol-version + rig as external pointers on dataset/session (Rec 4)
description: Capture which protocol version and rig produced a dataset/session as ExternalArtifactReference pointers, enabling comparability and drift detection. Store protocol_id + version_label + content_hash (per-version content_hash makes drift detectable) and rig identifier + rig_label only. NO protocol body, NO instrument inventory/calibration.
design: Reuse DatasetModel.manifest_external_artifacts ExternalArtifactReference pattern; add the same optional shape to SessionModel. Add typed semantic edge values protocol_version and rig so the PROV-O exporter materializes them as prov:Entity via prov:used. Protocol-drift flag is then derived (multiple distinct content_hash for same protocol_id across a project). Canonical pointer-not-reimplementation pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Dataset and session can reference protocol_version and rig as external artifacts with typed edges; PROV-O export includes them; no protocol body or equipment registry stored; migration single-head.

title: Phase 2: DatasetQCReport verdict record (Rec 3)
description: Capture QC verdict + timing per dataset. DatasetQCReport(qc_report_id, dataset_id FK, qc_status: unverified|passed|passed_with_caveats|failed, generated_at, generated_by: manual|adapter, summary_metrics JSON thin snapshot {completeness_pct, trial_count, control_response, n_excluded, exclusion_reasons[]}, external_report_ref ExternalArtifactReference, created_at).
design: Store only the VERDICT + thin metrics snapshot + a pointer to the externally-generated report. NEVER run or chart QC (experiment-tracker drift). Keep summary_metrics a frozen thin snapshot; do not grow into a configurable QC threshold/criteria registry. Dataset is the primary QC home; session QC is secondary/derived. time-experiment-to-QC = generated_at - dataset.created_at; pass fraction derived.
acceptance_criteria: Dataset can carry a QC verdict with timestamp, thin metrics, and external report pointer; datasets_committed_without_qc derivable; no QC computation in-app; migration single-head.

title: Phase 2: maturity/evidence-grade tag on Dataset and Claim (Rec 5)
description: Add maturity enum {exploration, validation, production, archival} (default exploration) to BOTH Dataset and Claim. Epistemic-trust axis, DISTINCT from storage-lifecycle status. Enables the cross-check production-grade claim resting on exploration-grade evidence as a derived metric.
design: One low-cardinality column per entity, no new table. The migration MUST state that maturity is distinct from status (staged/committed/archived; proposed/supported/rejected) to avoid conflation.
acceptance_criteria: Dataset and Claim carry maturity; default exploration; production-claim-on-non-production-evidence derivable; migration documents the axis distinction and is single-head.

title: Phase 2: Incident reasoning-node + generic IncidentLink edge (Rec 6)
description: Add a thin Incident node and a generic impact edge so failures are visible and their blast-radius traversable. Incident(incident_id, incident_type: equipment_failure|data_loss|protocol_error|animal_issue|missed_handoff|other, severity, status, summary, occurred_at, audit fields) + IncidentLink(entity_type/entity_id, relation: caused_by|affects|implicates|resolved_by).
design: TIGHTEN (scope review): keep it a thin reasoning node, NOT an IT-helpdesk/ticketing workflow. Freeze severity to a minimal set; keep status to a 2-3 value lifecycle; no triage/notification/assignment surface. animal_issue/equipment_failure are mere tags referencing an event, never colony/equipment management. Mirror the NoteTarget/GoalLink generic-edge pattern; blast-radius is a pure PROV-O traversal (derived).
acceptance_criteria: Incidents recordable and linkable to research entities; blast-radius derivable via existing provenance traversal; open/stale-incident flags derivable; node stays thin; migration single-head.

title: Phase 3: ProjectReviewEvent log + kill_criteria & stage on Project (Rec 1)
description: Add the review control loop: ProjectReviewEvent(review_id, project_id FK, reviewed_at, reviewed_by_user_id FK, decision: continue|pivot|pause|kill|defer, rationale, current_question_id FK nullable, next_decision Text nullable, next_decision_owner_user_id FK nullable, next_review_date Date nullable, evidence_refs JSON referencing existing claim/dataset/analysis/goal, created_at), append-only. Add Project.kill_criteria Text and Project.stage enum (scoping|acquisition|analysis|synthesis|writeup|winddown, distinct from status).
design: last_reviewed/next_review are DERIVED (max reviewed_at / latest next_review_date), no redundant Project columns. Decision-rights captured only at the point they matter (next_decision_owner), NOT a standing RBAC matrix. kill_criteria is human-read free text, NOT auto-evaluated. stage enum stays small and fixed (unconfigurable). zombie/review-overdue flags become derivable.
acceptance_criteria: Reviews recorded with a decision, rationale, next-decision+owner, next-review-date; kill_criteria and stage on Project; zombie_project and review_overdue derivable; no RBAC matrix or auto kill-criteria evaluation; migration single-head.

Depends on the store-registration spine and hash-minting.

Per decisions: real model key, screenshots to docs/ for now.

title: [activation] Set FastMCP `instructions=` to wire the existing consultation policy into agents' system prompt
description:
The single biggest, cheapest salience lever. `server = FastMCP(SERVER_NAME)` (src/lab_tracker/mcp_server.py:64) passes no `instructions=`, so lab-tracker injects nothing into the agent system prompt — it was absent from this session's "MCP Server Instructions" block while Beads/scite/consensus appeared. FastMCP supports an `instructions=` kwarg that MCP clients (e.g. Claude Code) surface in-context.

The content already exists: reuse AGENT_CONSULTATION_POLICY (src/lab_tracker/decision_context_constants.py:16) — distilled to a few sentences — and point at the lab-tracker://quickstart resource. CRITICAL design note: unlike Beads (whose trigger "we track work" fires every session), lab-tracker's trigger ("research-facing decision") is occasional and fuzzy, so the instructions MUST enumerate the trigger crisply (what to plot, which analysis/control, figures, summaries, manuscript/grant text) rather than say a vague "consult before research," or agents won't know when it fires.

Example:
  server = FastMCP(SERVER_NAME, instructions=(
    "This lab uses Lab Tracker as the system of record for research reasoning. "
    "BEFORE research-facing decisions (what to plot, which analysis/control, figures, "
    "summaries, manuscript/grant/abstract text) call `lab_tracker_get_decision_context`. "
    "Read `lab-tracker://quickstart` for setup. Do not mutate records unless asked."))
design: Keep instructions as a single source of truth shared with AGENT_CONSULTATION_POLICY/AGENTS.md so the three copies don't drift; consider deriving the short instructions string from the policy constant. Verify the string actually appears in a Claude Code session's MCP Server Instructions block after the change.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh MCP-connected session shows a lab-tracker entry in the client's "MCP Server Instructions" with a crisp, trigger-enumerated consult directive; the string is sourced from (not duplicated against) the existing policy constant.

title: Resolve graph draft generic semantic type handling
description: Clarify and fix the ambiguity between the graph-draft schema and validation for generic semantic entity operations. Decide whether create_entity and update_entity support generic semantic types; then either remove unsupported generic types from allowed draft output or add complete schema and validation support so model output, review UI, and commit validation agree.
design: Prefer the smallest consistent fix. Do not allow the model prompt to advertise operations that normal API validation cannot commit.
acceptance_criteria: create_entity and update_entity have one consistent allowed-type policy across schema, model prompt, review parsing, and commit validation. Unsupported generic semantic types are rejected early with a clear validation error or fully supported end to end. Tests cover at least one accepted entity operation and one unsupported/invalid semantic type case.
close_reason: Implemented explicit create_entity/update_entity operation-direction validation, updated the model prompt guidance, and added regression coverage for valid and invalid generic semantic operations.

title: Clarify daily review cadence UI
description: The Batches page exposes raw cadence_minutes even though the scheduled workflow is: external poller POSTs /batches/run-due, while per-project settings decide enabled, cadence, local run time, timezone, and next_run_at. Replace or clarify the UI control so selecting cadence writes the actual scheduler settings and does not imply the web app runs a background job.

title: Per-host binding for shared data stores (rclone remote = portable fleet access vs host-pinned local_fs root)
description: Setup is multi-host: a lab has her laptop, instrument/experiment PCs, and a shared core-facility PC — not one server. But DataStoreModel has a SINGLE root + credential_ref per store (db_models.py:1064-1069), so a shared logical store (e.g. lab-onedrive) has ONE root. Consequence: rclone kinds are host-portable (credential_ref = an rclone remote NAME each host maps in its own rclone.conf; root = in-remote path), but a local_fs store's root is an absolute host path that only matches the machine that registered it — a synced-folder store is effectively single-host. check_store_health and the resolvers are explicitly 'from this host' (artifact_resolution.py), so resolution already degrades cleanly per host, but there is no way to bind one shared store to different local access on different machines. Decide/implement: (a) steer multi-host labs to the rclone form as the portable default (detection preference + docs; reserve local_fs for a single machine) with NO schema change, and/or (b) add a per-host store-binding (host -> local root/credential override) so a synced folder can bind differently per machine. Also make explicit: hosts that can't be set up (shared core PC) need NO local Lab Tracker setup — they just upload to the store, and another host resolves + hashes the file (this is the G7 softening).
acceptance_criteria: Docs and detection make the rclone-portable vs local_fs-single-host distinction explicit and state the 'no setup on hosts you cannot control' rule; a shared OneDrive store resolves on at least two heterogeneous hosts (laptop + one other) via the recommended form.

title: Portfolio summary endpoint (GET /portfolio/summary)
description:
New read-only GET /portfolio/summary aggregating a per-project health row (open questions, draft/committed datasets, running analyses, unreviewed claims, last_activity_at, owners) over accessible_project_ids. Default landing data for users with more than one project. Zero schema change.

Design: aggregate via existing repository queries gated by ProjectAuthorizationPolicy.accessible_project_ids(); admin short-circuit (None=all) preserved. Initially a flat list; nesting by project_group is added once groups exist. Bound payload/pagination per the lab-tracker-4bk patterns.

Acceptance: returns per-project health rows only for accessible projects; non-admin scoping enforced; covered by a route test.

title: MCP salience & activation: make AI agents reliably reach for Lab Tracker
description:
Audience: AI coding/research agents (NOT bench scientists — kept separate from the onboarding epic lab-tracker-chv8).

A 2026-06-16 comparison with the Beads MCP found that lab-tracker already has the hard part Beads lacks — a provenance/knowledge graph with `lab_tracker_get_decision_context` — and the salience CONTENT is already written: MCP resources `lab-tracker://quickstart`, `lab-tracker://surface`, `lab-tracker://agent-consultation-policy` (src/lab_tracker/mcp_tools/resources.py:43-58), the AGENT_CONSULTATION_POLICY (src/lab_tracker/decision_context_constants.py:16), and a consult block in AGENTS.md:28-43.

What is missing is ACTIVATION at the two injection points that actually fire, plus the reliability that makes activation safe:
1. The MCP server is built as `FastMCP(SERVER_NAME)` with NO `instructions=` argument (src/lab_tracker/mcp_server.py:64) — so lab-tracker contributes nothing to the agent's system prompt (it was absent from this session's "MCP Server Instructions" block while Beads/scite/consensus were present). This is the single biggest, cheapest lever.
2. There is no lab-tracker SessionStart/conditional hook or managed CLAUDE.md block; the only session hook runs `bd prime` (Beads).
3. Reliability tax: lab-tracker is HTTP-backed and is 502-ing. Salience without reliability is NEGATIVE — items that raise the call rate against a failing endpoint teach agents to abandon the tool. Hardening + a fail-soft error contract is a co-prerequisite, not a footnote.

Design principle: Beads' model does not port 1:1. Beads is frequent + local + behavioral-trigger; lab-tracker is occasional + networked + semantic-trigger. Adaptations must be conditional, fail-soft, and trigger-defined — not an unconditional networked prime, and not a routing god-tool.

Explicitly NOT in scope: Dolt/SQLite/daemon sync, native-binary install, a single routing god-tool.
acceptance_criteria: An agent in a fresh session is oriented toward Lab Tracker at message one (server instructions present), knows to call get_decision_context before research-facing decisions, has an obvious "what should I advance" entry action, and degrades gracefully (clear "Lab Tracker unavailable, proceeding without graph context") when the API is down rather than treating the failure as its own.

title: Batch context builder: assemble notes + graph slice for the model
description:
Build the context packet the model sees when drafting a daily batch. Should include: the full set of unprocessed notes (text, transcripts, image references), the relevant slice of the graph (projects/questions/sessions touched by those notes, plus their immediate neighbors), and any prior batch decisions on related entities.

This is what differentiates the daily batch from per-note drafting ? the model can see multiple related notes together and propose merges/relationships it couldn't see one at a time.
acceptance_criteria:
- Given a set of staged notes, returns a context packet with: notes payload, relevant graph subgraph, recent related decisions
- Context size bounded (paginated or truncated with priority signals if oversized)
- Tested with synthetic batches of varying size and graph density
- Output schema documented so the draft generator can consume it

Remaining human steps such as Cloudflare login/domain ownership are explicit and not hidden in code.

Quick tunnel is ephemeral; durable named tunnel/domain setup remains.

title: Daily review: privacy & data-egress policy for photo, voice, and push
description:
Deferred from the daily-review redesign ('The Morning Read') design session. The redesign escalates always-on bench PHOTOGRAPHY (hero photos surface whatever was incidentally in frame — people, whiteboards with unpublished ideas, IACUC/PHI-relevant subjects), VOICE feedback (ambient lab audio sent to a third-party transcription provider), optional TTS read-aloud (drafted prose sent to a TTS provider — a new third-party egress), and Phase-3 push notifications whose content is lockscreen-visible unpublished science. None of the daily-review design lenses addressed privacy/governance; the product owner has explicitly deferred it for now but wants to revisit before any of these multimodal/push surfaces ship.

This is a PREREQUISITE for: featuring user photos as hero/illustration in the daily review, voice-as-feedback input, TTS output, and push notifications. It is NOT blocking the Phase-1 reading-column reskin or text-based NL feedback.

Decide and document the defaults: what leaves the building (provider egress for voice/TTS/image), what is visible to teammates vs. on a lockscreen, voice-off-by-default?, a 'don't feature this photo' control, and per-capture sensitivity tagging. Tie to retained-v1-surface philosophy and the existing shared-project membership model.
acceptance_criteria: Privacy/egress policy documented in docs/ covering: (1) provider egress for voice transcription, TTS, and image handling; (2) teammate visibility vs. lockscreen visibility of review content; (3) voice/photo capture defaults (e.g. voice-off-by-default, opt-in to feature photos); (4) a per-photo 'don't feature' control; (5) push-notification content sensitivity rules. Policy reviewed before any photo-hero, voice-input, TTS, or push feature ships.

title: Add MLflow run reference adapter for analyses
description: Follow-up to the build-vs-buy analysis boundary decision. Add an adapter/import path that records an external MLflow run (and optionally W&B run URL) as an analysis Activity reference while keeping Lab Tracker's semantic dataset and claim support edges in-house.

Analysis PROV-O export includes the external activity/reference and still emits dataset usage plus claim-support links. Tests cover the mapping and Ruff passes.

Goal: README becomes an easy, almost-enjoyable read focused on what it is, why it matters, and how to START USING it; deep technical/setup material moves into clearly-named docs/ files that a curious reader digs into. Must stay truthful to docs/retained-v1-surface.md and not lose any relocated content.
notes: Done (uncommitted, awaiting review): README cut 402->80 lines into a slim front door (see-it-live demo+screenshots, plain-language 'what you can do', scientists-start-here vs set-it-up split, documentation map). Relocated technical depth into NEW docs/setup.md (install/run/Postgres/LAN/frontend/migrations/first-admin/validation) and NEW docs/configuration.md (full LAB_TRACKER_* env reference + multimodal + evidence inbox). Existing docs (deployment-options, one-click-cloud-deploy, self-hosted-operations, lan-shared-graph, phone-capture-quickstart, lab-tracker-mcp-skills, windows-fresh-clone, evidence-source-metadata) absorb the rest via links. All 20 README links resolve; no tests reference README/doc content. NOT yet committed/pushed.

title: [larger] Signed desktop app or one-click cloud template so no one touches a terminal
description:
There is no installer artifact (.dmg/.exe/.pkg) and no managed deploy; "getting" the software means cloning a public GitHub repo and building it (audit barriers #1-#4), which the target persona is uneasy with and largely unable to do.

Provide a true zero-terminal install: either a signed/notarized desktop app (e.g. packaging the FastAPI server + PWA behind a native shell) or a one-click cloud deploy template (Render/Fly/Railway button) that provisions Postgres, sets secrets, runs migrations, and yields a URL + first-admin flow. Bench scientists then only ever receive a link + login. Larger effort; depends on the launcher (lab-tracker-7x77) and auto-secret Docker work (lab-tracker-z7h2) as building blocks.

Evidence: audit barriers #1, #2, #3; "Discovery" and "Install" dimensions.

title: Guard against multiple Alembic heads + document migration convention
description: Alembic migration filenames use decorative NNNN_ prefixes, but Alembic chains on revision/down_revision strings, not the number.
