There is no dedicated guard asserting a single head, and no written convention for adding a migration. The 0016->0017_daily / 0017_device branch+merge(0019) is legitimate and stays; revision IDs are immutable (recorded in deployed alembic_version), so renumbering is out of scope.
design: Add tests/test_migrations.py::test_alembic_single_head asserting len(get_heads())==1 with an actionable message (chain off current head / use alembic merge). Add a concise 'Database migrations' note to CLAUDE.md: numbers are decorative, run alembic heads, set down_revision to the head, reconcile divergence with alembic merge. No file renames, no revision-ID changes.
acceptance_criteria: test_alembic_single_head fails clearly when >1 head exists and passes at a single head; CLAUDE.md documents the convention; uv run python -m pytest tests/test_migrations.py and ruff both pass.

title: MCP agent write ergonomics for Lab Tracker
description: Track additive MCP improvements from the 2026-06-12 Lab-Tracker MCP Agent Ergonomics Proposal rev 2. Goal: make agents reach Lab Tracker for research-context writes by default while preserving retained-v1 schema, API validation, human-gated graph changes, and manifest/code provenance boundaries.
design: Sequence low-risk schema and tool-description changes before composite authoring. Do not overload sessions; sessions remain acquisition activity. Dataset hashes remain content-addressed manifests. Repo-derived provenance applies only to analyses and code versions. viz_type remains a free string unless a separate product decision standardizes it.

title: Expose MCP schema metadata and enum affordances

design: Generate schema metadata from the existing source of truth: Pydantic request models, lab_tracker.models enums, decision_context_constants.TASK_KIND_VALUES, and service status-transition maps. Treat viz_type separately as a free-string convention unless a later product decision makes it an enum. Prefer a lab_tracker_describe_schema MCP/API surface plus tighter FastMCP argument metadata where feasible.
acceptance_criteria: Agents can discover allowed task_kind values, entity statuses, question/session/goal enums, goal relation/link-status values, required fields, and known lifecycle transitions without reading source. The generated metadata is tested against model constants so it cannot drift silently. Existing create/list tools remain backward-compatible. Ruff and relevant MCP tests pass.

title: Make decision-context MCP output a write-friendly front door

design: Keep the tool read-only. Preserve existing research task_kind values such as plot, analysis, slides, experiment_plan, summary, and research_writing; do not mix them with workflow intents like log_result unless a separate workflow_intent field is introduced. Echo resolved project scope, anchors, candidate IDs, allowed task kinds, and concise guidance for subsequent creates. Coordinate with the schema metadata bead so vocabulary is defined once.
acceptance_criteria: The MCP tool description clearly says to call decision context first for research-facing read-then-write tasks. Responses include enough stable IDs and candidate entities to support subsequent create calls without avoidable project/question/dataset lookups. Existing API response shape stays backward-compatible or changes are additive. Tests cover allowed task_kind reporting and ID echo behavior. Ruff and relevant decision-context/MCP tests pass.

title: Design and implement dry-run record_evidence_bundle MCP tool
description: Authoring one research result through MCP still requires multiple ID-dependent calls across questions, datasets, analyses, claims, visualizations, and optional source notes. Design and implement an additive composite tool that previews and then creates an evidence bundle while preserving Lab Tracker's strict endpoints and provenance boundaries.
design: Add a record_evidence_bundle surface with dry_run defaulting true, explicit idempotency/natural-key behavior, and no silent over-commit. Split provenance by node type: datasets use content-addressed commit manifests from uploaded/resolved artifacts or supplied manifests; repo-derived provenance applies to analyses/code versions through a resolve_code_provenance primitive. Handle locality explicitly: if the MCP client sees a local artifact path but the API server may not, upload or resolve through MCP rather than assuming the server can read the path. Keep strict create endpoints unchanged and route final writes through existing API validation.
acceptance_criteria: A dry run returns a fully reviewable plan including proposed nodes, links, reused records, warnings, and derived provenance values when derivation is possible. Calling with dry_run=false creates or reuses the expected records through existing API paths and returns stable IDs. Re-running with the same idempotency key or natural keys does not create duplicates. Dirty repo state and unreadable/local-only artifacts produce explicit warnings or errors, not fabricated hashes. Tests cover dry-run, commit, idempotent retry, dataset manifest provenance, analysis code provenance, visualization upload/path handling, and backward compatibility of existing MCP create tools. Ruff and relevant backend/MCP tests pass.

Concrete on slides 1,2,4,7,8,10,16,21; keep 11-15 abstract (schema-teaching) and 3/5/6/9/17-20 as mechanism slides. title: Adopt ARA exploration-trajectory + negative-knowledge capture (arXiv:2604.24658)
description:
Lab Tracker has independently converged on the epistemic backbone of the Agent-Native Research Artifact (ARA) protocol (arXiv:2604.24658v3, "The Last Human-Written Paper"): the same provenance taxonomy (EntityOrigin = user/ai_suggested/ai_executed/user_revised, models.py:252), the claim<->analysis<->dataset<->question PROV-O binding spine (provenance.py), typed claim relations (ClaimEdge: extends/contradicts/refutes/depends_on/supersedes, models.py:190), staged->committed crystallization, and human-gated AI proposals (GraphChangeSet). That convergence validates the design.

But Lab Tracker preserves only the convergent RESULT graph (question -> dataset -> analysis -> claim) and discards the divergent EXPLORATION graph that the paper's data identifies as the single highest-value signal. ARA's evaluation finds negative knowledge (dead ends, rejected hypotheses) produces the largest accuracy gain in the whole study (their Claim C06); on RE-Bench, failed runs are 90.2% of cost with a median 113x failed-to-success token ratio. Today Lab Tracker's only representation of that knowledge is the free-text terminal_reason on abandoned/superseded entities (migration 0034) and QuestionRefactor.reason, and it harvests staged human artifacts (notes/photos/voice) rather than the researcher-agent conversation that the paper argues is the free byproduct worth capturing.

This epic adds the missing exploration-trajectory layer, scoped to Lab Tracker's retained-v1 human-gated and build-vs-buy boundaries, in three slices:
1. First-class decision/dead_end/pivot capture (beyond free-text terminal_reason).
2. Falsification criteria + verification plan on Claims.
3. A session-end retrospective that distills the agent conversation into the existing daily-review queue.

OUT OF SCOPE (CS-reproduction-specific and/or conflicting with build-vs-buy): ARA's /src kernel-code layer, the ARA Compiler (legacy-PDF ingest), and Seal Certificates. Code stays referenced by hash/URI, never reimplemented.

Reference: github.com/AmberLJC/Agent-Native-Research-Artifact (Live Research Manager skill is open-source).
design:
Framing: ARA and Lab Tracker solve sibling problems from opposite ends (ARA = preserve a branching CS/ML research trajectory as an agent-executable package; Lab Tracker = preserve lab reasoning as a queryable PROV-O graph). The convergence on EntityOrigin, the binding spine, and human-gated proposals is strong external validation of Lab Tracker's core thesis (knowledge over narrative).

Where Lab Tracker is strongest is exactly ARA's Table 5 weakest column for prior tools: cross-layer bindings (the PROV-O spine is the whole reason Lab Tracker exists). The gap is the exploration-trajectory column, which Lab Tracker scores absent on.

Risk the paper itself flags (its extension experiments): a recorded "prior-run playbook" can CONSTRAIN a more capable agent into the prior box. Therefore exploration/dead-end capture must INFORM future work, not hard-gate it.

Boundary check (see memory build-vs-buy-boundary-principle-for-lab-tracker): "which hypothesis we abandoned and why" is irreducible core that no external tool (ELN, experiment tracker, data versioner) models, so it is correct to BUILD it here rather than offload. Relates to memory meeting-aware-daily-review-design (the daily review = the existing graph-draft batch; slice 3 reuses that path).

Process: follow the repo pattern (deep-think design doc -> phased child backlog -> code), and keep a single Alembic head throughout. Extend PROV-O export to emit the new exploration nodes/edges so the lossless-export guarantee still holds.
acceptance_criteria: All three child slices designed (design docs); at least the data-model slice (decision/dead_end/pivot capture) shipped; retained-v1 human gate preserved (nothing auto-commits); single Alembic head maintained; PROV-O export extended to emit the new exploration nodes and edges.

title: Exploration Graph: capture decision/dead_end/pivot as first-class nodes
description:
PROBLEM. Lab Tracker's only representation of process/negative knowledge is the free-text terminal_reason on abandoned/superseded Question/Dataset/Analysis/Claim (added in migration 0034) plus QuestionRefactor.reason. This collapses the structure ARA shows is most valuable. "We abandoned Q (terminal_reason='low SNR')" loses the hypothesis, the failure mode, and the lesson that would stop the next person or agent from re-running the dead end. The current model is a linear supersession chain, not a DAG.

GOAL. Add typed exploration nodes mirroring ARA's exploration_tree.yaml node kinds:
- decision -> { choice, alternatives[], evidence/rationale }
- dead_end -> { hypothesis, failure_mode, lesson }
- pivot    -> { trigger, rationale, invalidates: <prior decision/claim> }
Each node carries EntityOrigin provenance (reuse the existing enum) and links to the entity it concerns (question/dataset/analysis/claim). Edges form a DAG (parent->child plus an also_depends_on style convergence link), so branches and convergence points are traversable -- ARA's "git log for research". Extend PROV-O export to emit the nodes/edges.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTIONS (resolve in a design doc first, per repo pattern):
- New entity vs. promoting terminal_reason into a structured ExplorationNode/TerminalEvent table.
- Relationship to QuestionRefactor (already stores reason + snapshots) and ClaimEdge (already typed relations) -- avoid duplicating, prefer one exploration substrate.
- Polymorphic target (like NoteTarget / GoalLink entity_type+entity_id) vs. dedicated table.
- Single Alembic head; one additive migration.
design:
Highest-value slice per the paper: ARA Claim C06 (negative knowledge = largest accuracy gain) and the RE-Bench cost data (failed runs 90.2% of cost, 113x token ratio) are the empirical case for first-class dead-end capture. Priority P1 for that reason.

This is irreducible core (build-vs-buy memory): no external ELN / experiment tracker / data-versioner models "the hypothesis we abandoned and why we abandoned it," so build it here. Reuse, do not duplicate: QuestionRefactor.reason and ClaimEdge already carry fragments of decision/pivot semantics -- the design should consolidate onto one exploration substrate rather than add a third overlapping mechanism.

Honor the paper's own caveat: dead-end nodes must inform, not hard-gate, future exploration (a capable agent may legitimately revisit a path that failed under weaker tooling). Consider a model-class/tooling-context tag on dead_end nodes so successors can discount stale failures (ARA suggests exactly this).

Keep the retained-v1 human gate: agent-proposed exploration nodes flow through the existing GraphChangeSet review queue (see child slice 3), they do not auto-commit.
acceptance_criteria: A staged/committed dead_end records hypothesis+failure_mode+lesson and links to its source entity; a decision records alternatives-considered; a pivot records trigger+rationale; nodes form a traversable DAG; PROV-O export emits the nodes and edges; human gate preserved (no auto-commit); single Alembic head; tests cover the new model and export.

title: Falsification criteria + verification plan on Claims
description:
PROBLEM. ARA claims carry status hypothesis/testing/supported, an explicit falsification_criteria field, and a proof pointer via an experiments.md verification plan into /evidence. Lab Tracker's Claim (models.py:679) has statement, confidence (a bare float), status proposed/supported/rejected, and external_citations (migration 0037) -- but records nothing about what would falsify the claim or how it was/will be tested. A claim flips to "supported" without ever stating its test, which makes it an assertion-with-a-number rather than a falsifiable scientific claim.

GOAL (additive, low-risk):
- Add falsification_criteria (text) to Claim.
- Add a verification-plan link: which experiment/analysis tests this claim and what outcome would refute it. Reuse the existing ClaimAnalysis / ClaimDataset edges as the proof pointer; the missing piece is the falsification statement and the predicted/refuting outcome. This complements DatasetQuestionLink.outcome_status (unknown/supports/refutes/inconclusive), which already exists at the dataset->question level.
- Consider an interim "testing" status between proposed and supported/rejected.

Surface the new fields in PROV-O export, the MCP create_claim / describe_schema tools, and the publication-readiness checks.
design:
Cheapest high-value slice: additive fields, no structural change. Aligns a Lab Tracker Claim with a falsifiable scientific assertion (the ARA claims.md schema).

Consider requiring falsification_criteria before a Claim may reach status=supported -- the publication-readiness machinery already flags unsupported claims (models.py PublicationReadinessUnsupportedClaim), so this extends an existing gate rather than inventing one.

Keep confidence as-is for now; ARA does not mandate intervals. The win here is the falsification statement + the refuting-outcome link, not richer uncertainty quantification (that is a separate, deferrable concern).

Single Alembic head; one additive migration. Update describe_schema so agents discover the new fields.
acceptance_criteria: Claim can record falsification_criteria and a verification-plan link (refuting outcome); status vocabulary supports an in-test state; new fields surfaced in PROV-O export and the MCP create_claim/describe_schema tools and publication-readiness checks; single Alembic head; tests.

title: Session-end retrospective: harvest the agent conversation into the daily-review queue
description:
PROBLEM. ARA's central thesis is that the research trajectory is a free byproduct of every researcher-agent session, captured at session boundaries by a Context Harvester -> Event Router -> Maturity Tracker pipeline (shipped as an agent skill). Lab Tracker's daily review distills STAGED HUMAN ARTIFACTS (notes/photos/voice), not the conversation, and the lab-tracker skill restricts agents to read-only consultation + explicit-only writes with no session-boundary hook (docs/retained-v1-surface.md). Tellingly, EntityOrigin.AI_EXECUTED is defined (models.py:252) but never set -- no code path ever produces it. The agent conversation on this very repo IS a research trajectory (decisions, dead ends, rationale) currently thrown away.

GOAL. Add a session-end retrospective -- an extension of the existing lab-tracker / secretary skill plus a thin write path -- that distills decisions, dead ends, and rationale from the agent conversation into PROPOSED exploration nodes (child slice 1) and notes, landing them in the existing GraphChangeSet daily-review queue (/app/batches, POST /batches/run-due) for human accept/reject. Tag harvested records ai_suggested, and ai_executed where the agent actually ran the experiment (finally giving AI_EXECUTED a producer). The closest analog already ships (skills + scheduled run-due); this points it at the conversation instead of only staged captures.

Study the open-source Live Research Manager skill (github.com/AmberLJC/Agent-Native-Research-Artifact) as a reference implementation of the capture pipeline before designing ours.

Depends on child slice 1 (needs the decision/dead_end/pivot vocabulary to land events into).
design:
Reconciling ARA's "silent, zero-overhead, auto-crystallize" capture with Lab Tracker's deliberate human gate: gate only the COMMIT, not the capture. Harvested events become PROPOSALS in the existing GraphChangeSet review queue -- exactly the mechanism graph drafts already use -- so retained-v1's "no autonomous agent writes" holds (these are proposals, not writes). This is additive, not a philosophy change.

Reuses the meeting-aware daily-review path (memory meeting-aware-daily-review-design): the daily review IS the existing retained graph-draft batch; this adds a conversation-derived source alongside staged notes, not a new draft entry point.

Provenance correctness is a concrete deliverable: AI_EXECUTED gets its first real producer (agent-run experiments), AI_SUGGESTED for inferred decisions/hypotheses, USER_REVISED preserved when the human edits a proposal at review time (graph_draft_applier already sets USER_REVISED on UPDATE).

Depends on child slice 1. Design doc first (deep-think), then phased backlog, matching repo convention.
acceptance_criteria: A session-end action distills decisions/dead-ends/rationale from the conversation into PROPOSED exploration/claim/note records (origin ai_suggested, and ai_executed for agent-run experiments) inside a GraphChangeSet visible at /app/batches; nothing auto-commits; provenance tags set correctly so AI_EXECUTED finally has a producer; design doc precedes code.

title: Build-vs-buy: define Lab Tracker responsibility boundaries vs existing tools
description: Lab Tracker's durable product is the PROV-O / JSON-LD semantic provenance spine threading questions -> notes -> sessions -> datasets -> analyses -> claims -> visualizations (see src/lab_tracker/provenance.py). It is anchored by two node types no external tool provides: Questions (broad-to-atomic inquiry structure) and Claims (epistemic layer linking evidence to conclusions with confidence). Many adjacent responsibilities are either commodity infrastructure or owned by mature tool categories that Lab Tracker risks accidentally half-reimplementing: identity/RBAC, byte/asset storage, data versioning, experiment tracking, note capture (ELNs), transcription, and search. This epic decomposes the boundary decisions: for each adjacent responsibility decide offload / integrate-via-adapter / build-in-house, so effort concentrates on the irreducible semantic core. Already-resolved boundaries: voice transcription is offloaded to an explicit note-scoped action (retained-v1); multimodal note-to-graph extraction is offloaded to the LLM while the human-gated draft->commit diff stays in-house; semantic/vector search is explicitly deferred in retained-v1.
design: Shared principle - pointer-not-reimplementation: for each adjacent responsibility, store a reference (URI + content hash) to the external tool's artifact PLUS the semantic edges the external tool does not model (which question a dataset addresses, which claim an analysis supports). Do not reimplement the external tool's core. The PROV-O export is the integration seam: ingest external artifacts (DVC/DataLad manifests, MLflow runs, ELN entries) as PROV entities and connect them to inquiry and claims. Integrate decisions should strengthen the core by letting it focus on the semantic graph, not shrink it. Danger zone: each integrate decision is a slippery slope toward rebuilding half of MLflow or half of an ELN - resist field-by-field creep past a reference + edges.
acceptance_criteria: Each child decision reaches a recorded outcome (offload / integrate-via-adapter / build-in-house / defer) with rationale, a concrete integration seam or boundary description, and follow-up implementation issues filed where needed. The retained-v1 surface doc (docs/retained-v1-surface.md) and architecture notes are updated to reflect chosen boundaries. Tool-landscape names are validated as current before committing to any one.

title: Harden bootstrap disclosure behind reverse proxies (TrustedHostMiddleware + proxy headers)
description: Follow-up to lab-tracker-n5kp.2. _client_is_local now blocks Host-header spoofing, but behind a reverse proxy request.client is the proxy (often loopback/private), so local mode could still disclose. Add a TrustedHostMiddleware allowlist and correct proxy-header (X-Forwarded-For) handling, and document that local mode is unsafe behind an untrusted proxy (prefer never/first_run or public_base_url for hosted deploys).

title: High(sec): bootstrap token disclosed on spoofable Host header -> remote admin takeover
description: routes/auth.py _bootstrap_token_for_status derives the trust boundary from request.url.hostname / base_url (client-controlled Host header). On a fresh internet-exposed deploy an attacker sends Host: 127.0.0.1 to the unauthenticated /auth/bootstrap-status, receives the plaintext first-admin token, and registers as admin. No TrustedHostMiddleware/proxy handling.
acceptance_criteria: Token disclosure in default (local) mode is gated on the real connection peer (request.client.host) being loopback/private/link-local, NOT the Host header. Regression test proves a spoofed Host header does not leak the token. Follow-up filed for TrustedHostMiddleware + proxy-header handling + docs.

title: [activation] Sharpen tool descriptions: make `get_decision_context` say "CALL THIS FIRST"; tighten create_*/list_* sprawl
description:
~35 lab-tracker tools, many near-identical create_*/list_* names, dilute salience — an agent choosing among many similar verbs often picks none. NOTE: this client (Claude Code) already defers tool schemas and loads on demand (ToolSearch), so "too many tools in context" is partly handled by the harness; the higher-leverage fix is DESCRIPTION discipline, not tool removal.

Cheapest high-impact changes: (1) rewrite `lab_tracker_get_decision_context`'s description to lead with "CALL THIS FIRST before research-facing decisions" so it wins selection; (2) make read-vs-write and the create-order (datasets before analyses before claims/visualizations — already stated in the quickstart) obvious in descriptions; (3) ensure descriptions encode WHEN to use each tool, not just what it does.

Explicitly do NOT build a single routing god-tool (suggested in the source comparison) — it trades discoverability for a hard-to-schema monolith and is out of scope per the epic.
acceptance_criteria: get_decision_context's description leads with a clear "call this first" directive; create/list tool descriptions state when to reach for them and the create ordering; no god-tool introduced.

title: Add project graph visualization utilities

title: Epic: PWA capture-first phone workflow
description:
Make phone note capture nearly effortless. The current /app/capture screen requires login, mandatory project selection, and a network round-trip before anything is saved ? too much friction for one-handed bench work.

Goal: a user takes a photo with their phone's normal Camera app, hits Share, picks Lab Tracker, and the note is staged. No browser open, no login each time, no fields required beyond the captured asset.

This requires turning the existing static-bundle frontend into a Progressive Web App: web app manifest (Add to Home Screen), service worker (offline asset cache + upload retry queue), Web Share Target (OS share-sheet integration), and a device-bound auth path (passkey or long-lived device token) that eliminates the password prompt on phone. The note API also needs a minimal-payload quick-capture endpoint that accepts asset + device-default project and defers all linking to the daily draft review.

Pairs with the 'Daily AI graph-draft batch' epic: capture cheaply now, AI proposes structured graph updates once a day for human review.
design: Phone capture flow target: Camera -> Share Sheet -> Lab Tracker -> staged. <3 taps, works offline. Auth via device-bound passkey/token in IndexedDB, not username/password. Quick-capture endpoint accepts only asset + project; everything else (question/session/dataset links) gets proposed by the daily batch and confirmed in the review card.
acceptance_criteria:
- manifest.json served with icons, theme, start URL
- Service worker caches the app shell and queues failed uploads with retry
- Web Share Target registered so OS share sheet routes photos to a capture endpoint
- POST /notes/quick-capture accepts minimal payload (asset + project_id), returns 202 if queued
- Device-bound auth path lets a phone authenticate without typing a password on each visit
- Offline capture survives a network drop and syncs when connectivity returns
- iOS and Android smoke-tested via lab-tracker-e45

description: Apply the LOUD principles (Linked Open Usable Data — Sanderson/Linked Art/LUX) to the PROV-O/JSON-LD provenance surface. Full plan with gaps, phases, and done-when criteria: docs/loud-alignment-plan.md. Six independently shippable phases: stable canonical identifiers, dereferenceable /terms vocabulary, term dedupe + standard-vocabulary reuse, one key style in emitted documents, content negotiation at the resource URI, and a committed working sidecar example.

title: Phase 1: canonical base URL for provenance identifiers
description: IRIs are minted from the incoming request's base URL (_request_base_url in src/lab_tracker/routes/provenance.py), so the same entity gets different @ids per host, and lt export sidecars freeze whichever base was in effect. Add LAB_TRACKER_CANONICAL_BASE_URL (document in docs/configuration.md); when set, all provenance @ids use it. Unset falls back to current behavior, with a one-line lt export warning that identifiers are host-relative. Document the identifier policy in docs/provenance-export.md. See docs/loud-alignment-plan.md Phase 1.
acceptance_criteria: Two exports of one project taken through different hosts with the setting configured produce byte-identical @ids.

title: Phase 2: serve /terms — make the lab: vocabulary dereference
description: The @context maps ~100 custom terms into lab: = {base}/terms#, but no /terms route exists; every custom term 404s. Build a term registry (term -> definition, range, emitting entity types) as the single source of truth that also generates the @context in src/lab_tracker/provenance.py. Serve GET /terms with content negotiation: HTML for people, JSON-LD for machines. Add a test that every term used by any provenance builder appears in the registry with a non-empty definition. See docs/loud-alignment-plan.md Phase 2.
acceptance_criteria: Every lab: IRI in an exported sidecar resolves to a human-readable definition.

title: Phase 3: collapse duplicate context terms; reuse standard vocabulary
description: The @context in src/lab_tracker/provenance.py defines near-duplicates (fileName/filename/filePath, checksum/sha256, contentSize/sizeBytes) and re-mints terms standard vocabularies already define (contentUrl, contentSize, encodingFormat, contentType are schema.org; lab:createdAt/lab:generatedAt shadow dcterms:created/prov:generatedAtTime). Pick one spelling per concept; keep losing spellings as deprecated aliases to the same IRI for one release, then stop emitting them (old sidecars stay interpretable via their frozen contexts). Re-map lookalikes to schema:/dcterms:/prov:. Reserve lab: for genuinely novel research-record terms (falsificationCriteria, questionLink, refutingOutcome, curation state). See docs/loud-alignment-plan.md Phase 3.
acceptance_criteria: Context contains one term per concept; no lab: term duplicates a schema.org, Dublin Core, or PROV term.

title: Phase 4: emit aliased bare keys in provenance documents
description: The @context already aliases wasGeneratedBy, wasAttributedTo, used, wasDerivedFrom to bare keys, but builders emit prefixed forms (prov:wasGeneratedBy, prov:used), so documents mix key styles. Emit the bare aliased keys everywhere (Linked Art rule: the JSON reads naturally as JSON, no colons in keys). JSON-LD expansion is unchanged, so this is mechanical. Add a test that no emitted key contains ':'. See docs/loud-alignment-plan.md Phase 4.
acceptance_criteria: No emitted document key contains a colon; expansion output is unchanged.

title: Phase 5: JSON-LD content negotiation at the resource URI
description: A sidecar's @id dereferences to GET /datasets/{id}, but that returns the plain envelope — a different document with no content negotiation bridging the two. Honor Accept: application/ld+json on single-resource GETs for entity types with provenance builders (datasets, analyses, claims), returning the same document as the /provenance route; keep /provenance paths as stable aliases. Add the canonical URI to single-resource envelopes (an iri field beside the UUID). Out of scope: list endpoints, write paths, or any REST rewrite — the envelope API remains the primary abstraction. See docs/loud-alignment-plan.md Phase 5.
acceptance_criteria: GET on a dataset/analysis/claim URI with Accept: application/ld+json returns the PROV-O document; envelope responses include the canonical iri.

title: Phase 6: commit a worked sidecar example with a drift test
description: No example *.prov.jsonld exists in the repo; docs/provenance-export.md describes the format but never shows it. Commit a real sidecar generated from the demo seed as docs/examples/dataset.prov.jsonld plus an annotated walkthrough of its @graph in docs/provenance-export.md. Add a test that regenerates the example from the demo seed and fails on drift, and that the document expands cleanly with a JSON-LD processor (pyld). Best after phases 3-4 so the example shows the cleaned vocabulary, but valuable even before. See docs/loud-alignment-plan.md Phase 6.
acceptance_criteria: A committed sidecar example exists, is referenced from provenance-export.md with an annotated walkthrough, and CI fails if it drifts from the demo seed or fails JSON-LD expansion.

title: Stream revise-draft uploads with a cumulative size cap (replace in-memory read)
description: src/lab_tracker/routes/graph_drafts.py:264-279 _read_revision_upload does upload.file.read() for the audio file and every attachment, materializing each whole file in memory. The only guard, enforce_request_content_length_limit (graph_drafts.py:218-221), returns WITHOUT enforcing when Content-Length is absent (HTTP/1.1 Transfer-Encoding: chunked) and only bounds the aggregate request, not per-file memory. The notes/dataset paths instead stream chunk-by-chunk via enforce_stream_size_limit (note_storage.py:74, file_storage.py:171). Auth-gated -> single-process DoS. Fix: read uploads through size_limited_chunks/enforce_stream_size_limit with settings.max_upload_bytes, enforcing a cumulative bound across audio + all attachments so the cap holds without Content-Length. Folds test gap: revise upload size enforcement under chunked TE.
acceptance_criteria: A chunked (no Content-Length) revise upload exceeding max_upload_bytes is rejected; cap is cumulative across audio + attachments; regression test added.

This subsumes the approved terse-capture guardrail: 'a label is not a finding; place captures only where context supports; unplaceable captures are gaps -> clarification_requests.' So 'Rig 2 Fly 12' inside a Rig-2 session window becomes legible in prose; the same label with no anchor becomes a clarification rather than a fabricated finding.

Phase 1: prompt rewrite (narrative-first + guardrail) in graph_drafting.py _batch_instructions(); bump BATCH_PROMPT_VERSION v1->v2 (contract change; update the version-pinning test); UI render multi-paragraph prose in graph-drafts.jsx, clamp card titles in batches.jsx; spot-check that identifier-only captures route to clarification.
Phase 1b: context-builder honesty in services/graph_draft_context.py build_batch_graph_context -- always-on batch_window (day boundaries) + ordered timestamped note timeline; pre-compute capture->session-window membership + bundle grouping, so placement is grounded not guessed.
acceptance_criteria: Daily batch summary is a multi-paragraph day-narrative; the prompt instructs routing unplaceable identifier-only captures to clarification_requests; the batch context packet carries day boundaries + an ordered timeline + capture-to-session placement; BATCH_PROMPT_VERSION=v2 and the version test updated; UI renders prose; backend + frontend gates green.

title: [bug] `lab-tracker serve` crashes for pip-installed users: migrations not packaged in the wheel
description:
Found during the 2026-06-16 re-review of the onboarding epic (lab-tracker-chv8). The `lab-tracker serve` launcher subcommand (added for lab-tracker-7x77) works from a git clone + uv, but is BROKEN for anyone who `pip install`s the package without a clone.

Root cause: the wheel does not ship Alembic migration assets. pyproject.toml package-data only includes `lab_tracker = ["frontend/*"]` (pyproject.toml:44-46) and packages.find includes only `lab_tracker*`/`lab_tracker_client*` (pyproject.toml:42). `alembic.ini` and the `alembic/` directory live at the repo root, OUTSIDE `src/lab_tracker/`, so they are absent from the built wheel. serve_app() runs `Config(_repo_root()/"alembic.ini")` then `command.upgrade(...head)` (cli.py:64-65); `_repo_root()` searches cwd and parents for `alembic.ini` (cli.py:147-152) and finds none in an installed environment, so `alembic upgrade head` fails with "No 'script_location' key found in configuration." It only works on the dev box because of the editable (.pth) install.

This is masked by tests: test_lab_tracker_init.py monkeypatches `command.upgrade`, so no test exercises a real wheel.

Scope note: the double-click launchers (launchers/*.command/.bat) drive uv from a clone where alembic.ini is present, so that path is fine. This bug is specifically the pip-install / non-clone path that docs/packaging imply is supported via the `lab-tracker`/`lab_tracker` console scripts.
design: Either (a) package the migrations: move alembic.ini + alembic/ under src/lab_tracker/ (or add them as package-data) and locate them via importlib.resources instead of _repo_root(); or (b) make serve fail fast with an actionable "run from a clone / migrations not packaged" message when assets are missing. Add a wheel smoke test that builds the wheel, installs into a clean venv, and runs `lab_tracker serve --skip-migrations` and a migration path so this regression is caught.
acceptance_criteria: A user who `pip install`s the package (no clone) can run `lab-tracker serve` and it either runs migrations successfully or fails with a clear, actionable message — never an opaque Alembic "script_location" traceback. A CI smoke test exercises the built wheel.

title: [bug] Harden invitations: single-use/revocable tokens, editor-default role, min password length, localhost-link guard
description:
Found during the 2026-06-16 re-review (residual gaps on lab-tracker-9j90 / 5944). The invite flow works but has several footguns for non-technical lab deployment:

1. Invite tokens appear stateless/replayable/unrevocable for the full TTL (LAB_TRACKER_AUTH_INVITE_TTL_HOURS, default 168h = 7 days). There is no InvitationModel persisting single-use state (contrast the single-use DeviceEnrollmentModel). A leaked admin-role invite link is claimable by any holder for a week with no way to revoke it.
2. The invite UI defaults the new member's role to `viewer` (users.jsx:7), which is read-only — so an admin who doesn't notice silently lands invitees in a dead-end (all write/capture buttons disabled).
3. Minimum password length appears to be 1.
4. Self-hosted/LAN invite links can embed localhost/127.0.0.1: _public_base_url() (auth.py:197) falls back to request.base_url when LAB_TRACKER_PUBLIC_BASE_URL is unset; only the Render blueprint backfills it, so a LAN/desktop admin can generate links the invitee cannot reach.
design: Persist invitations as single-use, revocable records with explicit status; default the invite role to editor (or require an explicit role choice and warn on viewer); enforce a sane minimum password length; when generating invite_url, detect a private/localhost host and either require LAB_TRACKER_PUBLIC_BASE_URL or warn the admin that the link is not externally reachable.
acceptance_criteria: Invites are single-use and revocable; an invitee cannot silently land read-only; passwords below a minimum length are rejected; invite links generated on a self-host/LAN deployment either use a reachable base URL or clearly warn the admin.

title: Implement ongoing-project member onboarding MVP
description: Ship the approved in-media-res onboarding flow for ongoing research projects: one immutable member checkpoint, guided plus optional pasted context, exact manual or constrained AI question alignment, deterministic current-state map/brief, one separate real capture, contributor completion with owner commit handoff, owner in-app queue, resumable state, provenance, usage instrumentation, and enabled-by-default workspace entry points. Preserve retained-v1 boundaries and current viewer/contributor/owner authorization.
design: Back the checkpoint with a project-targeted staged note plus reserved server-owned metadata; add project-scoped onboarding orchestration/status endpoints; reuse staged questions, graph drafts, note targets, mobile capture, and owner commit. AI alignment is capped at three create-staged-question or additive link operations and depends on provider-timeout-aware fenced generation leases. Manual exact mappings remain direct human writes. No checkpoint table, history backfill, private notes, goals, claims, or bulk accept.
acceptance_criteria: Contributor/owner can create or resume one checkpoint per project/member, resolve every live question manually or via AI, copy a deterministic labeled brief/map, and complete only after a separate stored text/photo/voice capture targeting the checkpoint. Viewers remain read-only. AI retries are idempotent and fenced against stale completion; failures fall back manually; full source is never silently truncated. Owner can discover/commit submitted AI maps in-app. Reserved metadata is protected, cadence excludes checkpoints, provenance/usage remain honest, OpenAPI/docs are current, and backend, Postgres concurrency, frontend, build, and E2E gates pass.
close_reason: Shipped ongoing-project member onboarding: immutable checkpoints, manual/constrained-AI alignment, deterministic map/brief, first forward capture, owner handoff, provenance, usage, docs, UI, and green backend/frontend/Postgres/E2E gates.

title: Client _list_all total-cap regression breaks upsert idempotency / evidence dedup past 200 rows
description: src/lab_tracker_client/client.py:838-874. _list_all was redefined from page-size to a hard TOTAL cap; every natural-key finder (find_project_by_name, find_question_by_text, find_note_by_marker, find_evidence_note, build_evidence_note_index) calls list_*(limit=MAX_PAGE_SIZE=200) and both client (_validate_limit) and server (validate_pagination) cap a scan at 200. In any project with >200 notes/projects/questions, an existing record past row 200 is invisible, so upsert_* POSTs a duplicate and lt-import-folder re-imports already-captured evidence on every re-sync. No server-side uniqueness constraint on the evidence key exists, so dedup is purely client-side. Introduced this batch (c1u.8); the new test only pins the cap, no multi-page finder test exists. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Add an unbounded _iter_all generator that pages until offset>=total; finders use it instead of list_*(limit=200). Keep limit-as-cap only for public bounded reads. Add a finder test with >200 rows proving a record past offset 200 is found and not duplicated.

title: Project delete fans out goal-link cleanup into a per-entity N+1
description: src/lab_tracker/services/goal_link_cleanup.py:30-54, 70-75. remove_goal_links_to_project_contents (called from project_service.delete_project:127 inside the delete unit_of_work) issues 7 unbounded query_*(limit=None) scans then one query_goals per discovered target entity. Deleting a large long-lived project becomes O(entities) DB round-trips in a single transaction and can time out / hold a long lock. Admin-gated delete path (outside Epic 4bk's literal scope) but the same fan-out anti-pattern. From deep review 2026-06-18 completeness sweep.
acceptance_criteria: Collect all target keys first, then resolve affected goals with a single query_goals filtered by (entity_type, entity_id) IN (...) (or a join), rather than one query per target.

title: portfolio_query._uuid_values duplicates common.uuid_values
description: src/lab_tracker/portfolio_query.py:112-113 defines a private _uuid_values identical to sqlalchemy_repository_parts.common.uuid_values (the established helper used by analyses/core/datasets/graph_drafts/sessions/notes). portfolio_query.py:51 already imports from that module. Maintainability only - two copies of the accessible-id sort/normalization can drift. New code this batch. From deep review 2026-06-18.

title: Dead SQLite FK PRAGMA guard in migrations 0039/0040 (no-op inside Alembic transaction)
description: src/lab_tracker/alembic/versions/0039_not_null_tightening_0014_0024.py:91-94 and 0040_drop_daily_reviews_align_batch_key.py:57-60. _set_sqlite_foreign_keys issues PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF/ON, but Alembic runs migrations inside context.begin_transaction(), where SQLite ignores the PRAGMA - and FK enforcement is already off during migrations (the FK connect-listener is only registered on the app engine, not the migration/test engine). So the guard is doubly inert dead code that misleads future authors. Tests pass regardless. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Drop the ineffective PRAGMA helper, or if suppression is genuinely required set transactional_ddl=False / issue the PRAGMA outside begin_transaction().

title: Migration 0023 was edited in place to add the cq5.8 dedupe (immutability anti-pattern)
description: src/lab_tracker/alembic/versions/0023_goal_link_slot_not_null.py:14-58. The cq5.8 _dedupe_unslotted_goal_links() was added to upgrade() of an already-deployed, descendant-chained revision (0023, 17 descendants, head=0040) rather than a new forward-only revision - violating the project immutability rule (CLAUDE.md). Databases that already ran pre-edit 0023 never re-execute it. Data risk is near-nil (pre-edit 0023's bare UPDATE...SET slot='' would itself have crashed on a DB holding NULL-slot dupes, so a successful apply proves none existed), so this is hygiene, not corruption. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: If 0023 was never deployed anywhere, leave as-is. If it may have been deployed, move _dedupe_unslotted_goal_links() into a new forward-only revision chained after head 0040.

title: Service-worker CACHE_VERSION / asset ?v not bumped despite app.js bundle change
description: src/lab_tracker/frontend/sw.js:12-22. This batch rebuilt the committed bundle (app.js content changed, new markers present) but CACHE_VERSION stayed v18 and SHELL_ASSETS still references app.js?v=18 / styles.css?v=18. The SW serves /app/static/* cache-first and only purges non-v18 caches. Self-mitigated THIS cycle because sw.js's own bytes changed (forces reinstall -> cache.addAll), but a future batch changing only app.js while leaving sw.js/?v fixed would serve a stale bundle to installed PWA users. The static-asset test only enforces v-alignment, not a bump-on-bundle-change. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Drive ?v / CACHE_VERSION from a content hash, or bump them whenever the bundle content changes; add a test that fails if the bundle changed without a version bump.

title: decision-context auto-resolution issues one search per accessible project (per-project N+1)
description: src/lab_tracker/decision_context_use_case.py:171-176, 374-389. When no project_id and no anchor resolves scope, _project_ids_with_search_matches loops over every project from list_projects(limit=CONTEXT_LOOKUP_LIMIT=500) and issues reader.search(query, project_id=..., limit=1) per project (each = query_questions+query_notes), up to ~1000 statements on the get_decision_context request path. Violates Epic 4bk no-per-project-N+1. The single scoped-query primitive already exists in decision_context_query.search (project_ids=accessible). Introduced by 4bk.3 (b2e8b24). From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Replace the per-project loop with one bounded scoped query returning DISTINCT accessible project_ids having a question/note match. Add a test asserting O(1) query count for the auto-resolution path.

title: delete_group_project_memberships retains SELECT-then-DELETE last-owner TOCTOU
description: src/lab_tracker/services/project_service.py:437-463. cq5.6 made the last-owner invariant atomic for delete_project_membership and the group upsert path (lock_project_owner_memberships + re-count in the same unit_of_work), but delete_group_project_memberships still counts owners via an unlocked query and deletes in a separate unit_of_work, taking NO lock. Two concurrent removals (group-delete vs group-delete, or interleaved with the single-project delete) can both pass the owner-count check and leave a project with zero owners; taking no FOR UPDATE lock, it also defeats the hardened single-project path. No DB-level minimum-owner constraint exists. Postgres runtime, per-request sessions. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Re-count owners under repository.lock_project_owner_memberships(project_id) inside the same unit_of_work that performs the deletes; raise ValidationError if any project would drop to zero owners. Add a concurrency test.

title: Batch graph-draft pagination drops staged notes sharing the cutoff created_at
description: src/lab_tracker/services/graph_draft_service.py:1254-1262 (and 417-422, 1236-1251). _limit_notes_to_draft clamps window_end to the 100th note's created_at; the next run sets window_start=that created_at and _staged_notes_in_window uses a strictly-exclusive start (start < created_at <= end). When >=101 staged notes share the exact created_at at the 100-note boundary, notes sorting after the 100th by note_id are excluded from both batches and never drafted. create_batch_graph_draft does not mutate note.status, so the timestamp window is the sole carried state. Reachable via bulk/programmatic import (e.g. datalad/dvc adapters) assigning coarse timestamps. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Use a (created_at, note_id) continuation cursor, or make the window start inclusive with already-drafted note_id de-dup, or push the boundary before the tie group. Add a test with >=101 same-created_at staged notes asserting none are dropped.

title: Recent-committed analyses view fetches the project's entire committed history (4bk regression)
description: src/lab_tracker/frontend_src/hooks/useAnalysisWorkflow.js:45-71. The committed-analyses load changed from a bounded offset query to fetchAllPages(...) then sortByRecent().slice(0, RECENT_COMMITTED_LIMIT=5). fetchAllPages loops 200-row pages to exhaustion, so every workspace refresh downloads all committed analyses for the project to render the 5 newest. Displayed data is correct; this is a payload-bounding regression vs Epic 4bk. GET /analyses exposes no recent_first param though the repository supports recent_first=True (created_at DESC). From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Expose recent_first (and optionally a bounded sort) on GET /analyses, reflect it in docs/retained-v1-surface.md, and have the hook request limit=RECENT_COMMITTED_LIMIT&recent_first=true so only 5 rows cross the wire.

title: Auth-refresh has no minimum-delay floor: short token TTL causes a /auth/refresh storm
description: src/lab_tracker/frontend_src/hooks/useAuthSession.js:187-215. scheduleRefresh uses Math.max(0, expiresAtMs - Date.now() - REFRESH_MARGIN_MS(5min)). If a refreshed token expires within 5 min (operator sets auth_token_ttl_minutes<=5; validator only requires >=1), delay computes <=0, setTimeout fires at 0, and the success path has no backoff, looping POST /auth/refresh which, unlike /auth/login and /auth/register, is NOT rate-limited. Default TTL 720 never triggers it. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Add a MIN_REFRESH_DELAY_MS floor and/or treat near-immediate expiry as an error rather than re-firing at delay 0. Add a test with a short refreshed expiry asserting bounded reschedule.

title: Graph-draft context bounded-fetch can omit recently-updated / superseded questions at scale
description: src/lab_tracker/services/graph_draft_context.py:371-405. _question_context fetches ACTIVE and STAGED via query_questions(limit=50, recent_first=True) which orders by created_at DESC, then re-sorts the union by updated_at and keeps the top 50 - so an old-created but recently-updated question (project with >50 of a status) is dropped before the updated_at sort sees it. Separately, superseded context fetches the most-recent 100 SUPERSEDED then filters to those pointing at active context; with >100 superseded a relevant entry can be dropped. Both diverge from the prior unbounded-then-sort behavior; LLM context completeness only, no scoping impact. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Add an updated_at-desc ordering option so the SQL LIMIT selects by the final sort key (or widen the fetch); query superseded questions filtered by superseded_by_question_id IN (active_context_ids) in SQL.

title: DVC/datalad manifest with a float-formatted size crashes the import adapter
description: src/lab_tracker/provenance_ingestion.py:290-294. _optional_int_value does bare int(value) on the str form of the size field; a JSON float '2048.0' or YAML '2048.0' (isdigit() False) becomes int('2048.0') -> ValueError, aborting the whole dataset_manifest_from_dvc/datalad import. No try/except. DVC normally writes integer sizes so likelihood is low, but a malformed/variant manifest fails the entire import. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Parse defensively: try int(value), fall back to int(float(value)) or None on failure. Add a test with a float-formatted size.

title: import-folder follows symlinks and imports out-of-tree file bytes
description: src/lab_tracker_client/cli.py:280-292. _discover_import_files uses root.rglob('*') filtered by path.is_file(), which follows symlinks; a symlink under --root pointing outside the tree (e.g. ~/.ssh/id_rsa) passes the filter (relative_to(root) still succeeds lexically) and its resolved bytes are read and uploaded as an evidence note, while the recorded source_uri reflects the in-tree symlink path. Local single-user CLI, so a hardening gap not a remote vuln. duz.1 added no symlink handling. From deep review 2026-06-18.
acceptance_criteria: Skip path.is_symlink() during discovery, or require path.resolve() to stay under root.resolve() before reading. Document that symlinks are not followed.

title: Fix flaky frontend test: 'captures a mobile image with context and starts a graph-aware draft'

Do NOT make the mock validators defensive/conditional — swallowing body mismatches would hide real contract regressions.

title: Guided setup + automatic tracking: consent-gated lt setup verbs, enrollment, agent awareness
description: When a user installs lab-tracker, coding agents should become aware of the lt tools for saving files, guide watch-folder setup, and enroll selected repos with commit hooks — easy setup first, then as-automatic-as-possible tracking. Today onboarding is ~9 manual steps across two CLIs (lab_tracker init vs lt) and two hand-edited JSON files (lt_ids.json project_id, watch.json watches[]); the commit hook is PowerShell-only, source-checkout-dependent, and fire-and-forget (unreachable-server commits are lost). Decision (3-design/3-judge review, 2026-07-01): atomic non-interactive consent-gated lt verbs as the spine; wizard lives in agent prose (skill + pointers + MCP resource), NOT an interactive TTY state machine. Grafts: persisted connection profile, outbox-backed lt git snapshot, sha-only drift. Rejected: MCP setup tools, machine-wide standing consent (drive-by enrollment hazard). Full design: docs/guided-setup-and-auto-tracking-design.md
design: docs/guided-setup-and-auto-tracking-design.md

Consent stance: agents run only 'lt setup status' and --dry-run unprompted; humans approve every mutating verb; mutating verbs hard-fail non-interactively without --yes/--dry-run; PAT minting stays human-in-browser.

title: lt setup status: read-only machine/repo inventory (agent-safe, --fail-silent)
description: The substrate agents narrate setup from, and the future SessionStart drift sensor. needs_client=False; network limited to one swallowed GET /health; one JSON payload: server {reachable, base_url, auth_enabled}, repo scaffold presence + managed-block drift (reuse lab_tracker.cli._doctor), lt_ids.json binding, watch config + outbox pending/failed, hook-block presence, skill copy versions. The ONLY setup command agents may run unprompted.
acceptance_criteria: Read-only (writes nothing); --fail-silent never exits nonzero or blocks; JSON-stdout contract preserved; works offline with server section marked unreachable.

title: Skill distribution: lab_tracker init --install-skills (file copy, version-stamped)
description: Skills are useless if never installed. Consent-gated flag copying packaged skills (lab-tracker, lab-tracker-setup) into ~/.claude/skills/ as real file copies (no symlinks — Windows) with a version stamp; --dry-run diffs and --uninstall removal; skipped without the flag, advertised via InitResult.offers; lt setup status reports copy version so upgrades surface as drift.
acceptance_criteria: Copy round-trips with stamp; --dry-run writes nothing; --uninstall removes only our copies; status surfaces stale version.

title: MCP setup-guide resource + setup-aware next_action + cold-start bootstrap line
description: Agents on machines with zero scaffolding need a discovery channel. Add lab-tracker://setup-guide rendering the staged setup script from ONE canonical generator (code_facing_idioms single-source pattern); reference from MCP_SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS + quickstart resource; lab_tracker_unavailable envelope next_action gains a setup hint alongside proceed_without_graph_context; add a copy-paste bootstrap line to README and /app. Deliberately NO new MCP setup tools — setup actions stay on the CLI behind the harness command-approval prompt.
acceptance_criteria: Resource text == generator (drift test); next_action hint non-imperative; no new write-capable MCP tools; README + /app carry the bootstrap line.

title: SessionStart drift hook: lt setup status --fail-silent --brief in scaffolded settings
description: Nothing re-runs init on package upgrade; drift is invisible inside agent sessions. Extend _claude_settings_json scaffold with a SessionStart hook running lt setup status --fail-silent --brief: one line when healthy, short advisory naming the repair verb when drifted. Closes the upgrade-drift gap where agents actually work; the agent then OFFERS the repair command (human runs it).
acceptance_criteria: Hook can never block or fail a session (--fail-silent); healthy output is one line; drifted output names the repair verb non-imperatively; scaffold remains idempotent.

title: lt setup schedule: OS-scheduler enrollment for recurring watch scan+sync
description: Watch scan/sync are one-shot manual commands; tracking is not automatic until something recurs. Emit a Task Scheduler / cron / launchd entry running 'lt watch scan && lt watch sync --fail-silent', mirroring the daily-review installer pattern. External scheduler only — zero server background machinery. Consent-gated like every mutating verb.
acceptance_criteria: Idempotent re-run; uninstall removes the entry; works with profile-based auth (no per-shell env vars); server stays scheduler-free.

title: applied-repos registry + lt doctor --all fleet sweep
description: No registry of initialized/enrolled repos exists, so a package upgrade cannot enumerate consumer repos needing refresh. Record repo roots (+ last-applied content hash) in ~/.lab-tracker/applied-repos.json at init/hooks-install time; lt doctor --all sweeps the registry post-upgrade. Client-side only; registry is metadata for suggestion, never an auto-apply trigger.
acceptance_criteria: Registry written on init/hooks install; --all sweep reports per-repo drift; stale/moved repo entries degrade gracefully.

title: v2: declarative .lab-tracker.toml + lt apply reconciler (treat committed config as untrusted)
description: Best teammate/new-clone story: a committed .lab-tracker.toml declares watch folders + hook enrollment; lt apply reconciles. DEFERRED because it demotes documented hand-editable watch.json to a derived artifact (two-sources-of-truth tax) and the reviewed design's machine-wide standing consent is REJECTED (drive-by enrollment: clone + habitual apply = someone else's committed intent installs hooks). Only viable if the toml is treated as UNTRUSTED input with per-repo diff-and-confirm on first apply. Revisit after the setup verbs ship and teammate friction is observed in practice.
notes: Kept deferred by design after finishing stkn.13/.14 (2026-07-02): the drive-by-enrollment hazard and two-sources-of-truth tax stand; revisit trigger remains observed multi-teammate friction.

title: Guide invited users through Lab Tracker setup
description: Turn invitation acceptance into a guided onboarding handoff. After an invited user creates an account, route them to a resumable setup page that helps create/select a first project, save per-project daily review timing and timezone, connect coding agents with a personal access token, install the packaged Lab Tracker setup skill, and scaffold MCP/instruction files. Preserve the consent-gated setup model and normal login behavior. Rebuild and canary Marion's isolated deployment from the latest authoritative main revision before handoff.
design: Reuse existing projects, graph-draft batch-settings, personal access token, lt setup, and routing surfaces. Avoid a second setup state machine or autonomous writes: the web page coordinates existing user-driven steps; machine/repo mutations remain consent-gated through lt dry-run/--yes.
acceptance_criteria: Invitation registration lands on /app/setup; setup page explains progress and can be reopened/skipped; project and daily-review settings persist through existing APIs; agent/repo commands install current Lab Tracker plus skills and MCP scaffolding; non-invite auth is unchanged; frontend/backend quality gates pass; Marion runs an image built from the latest authoritative SHA with database isolation and the existing primary instance preserved.
close_reason: Invitation acceptance now lands on a resumable setup flow covering project setup, per-user review timing, readiness, current client/skills/MCP setup, and device pairing. Latest-main-based Marion image deployed publicly with backups, isolation, pending invite preservation, and full quality gates verified.

title: lt setup init: delegate repo scaffolding to init_consumer_repo on the lt CLI

Add lt setup init delegating to lab_tracker.cli.init_consumer_repo unchanged (--yes/--dry-run/--force/--uninstall), mirroring the shipped lt doctor -> _doctor delegation seam (lab_tracker_client/cli.py:742). Also add non-imperative guided-setup pointer sentences to managed_claude_block(), the AGENTS fragment, and code_facing_idioms() naming lt setup status / lt watch add / lt hooks install.

title: lt project bind: resolve/create project and fill lt_ids.json

Add lt project bind [--project-id UUID | --name NAME [--create]] using existing upsert_project; write the id into lt_ids.json with a diff preview, gated by --yes/--dry-run. Add an InitResult.offers entry advertising it.

title: lt watch add/list/remove: register watch folders without hand-edited JSON

Add lt watch add <root> [--mode files|manifest] [--sink staged-note|acquisition-output] [--include/--exclude ...] as a read-modify-write with atomic write and entry preview, plus list/remove. Also register --fail-silent on watch scan/sync so hook- and scheduler-fired invocations are safe.

title: Persisted connection profile in LabTracker.from_env (env-first; opt-in token storage)
description: from_env (client.py:258) is env-var-only, so hook-, scheduler-, and GUI-git-fired commands silently die without per-shell env exports — the biggest week-two automaticity gap. Add ~/.lab-tracker/config.json (honor LAB_TRACKER_CONFIG_DIR, alongside install-id) read by from_env with env-vars-FIRST precedence. Stores base_url + default project by default; token persistence is OPT-IN behind its own consent (lt setup connect --save-token), hardened via icacls on Windows (chmod is a no-op there); document short-TTL PATs. Written only by lt setup connect.

title: lt git snapshot: outbox-backed commit capture (port create-analysis-graph-draft transport into client)
description: The current post-commit capture is fire-and-forget: unreachable-server commits are lost (one stderr line, no queue), and the hook depends on a source checkout + .venv. Move scripts/create-analysis-graph-draft.py's evidence rendering + transport into lab_tracker_client as lt git snapshot: render commit metadata/--stat/capped diff, write a deterministic outbox event (capture_id.git.event_id.json, same (provider, external_id, content_hash) dedupe), then best-effort sync; --request-draft flows through the existing draft endpoint on sync; --fail-silent supported.
acceptance_criteria: Server-down snapshot queues and later sync drains it exactly once; re-snapshot of same commit is a no-op; --fail-silent always exits 0; no dependency on a source checkout.

title: lt hooks install/uninstall/status: cross-platform per-repo commit-hook enrollment
description: Enrollment today is a PowerShell-only source-tree script. Pure-Python port: resolve hook path via git rev-parse --git-path; upsert the SAME BEGIN/END LAB TRACKER GRAPH DRAFT HOOK markers (existing installs upgrade in place); POSIX-sh body invoking lt git snapshot --fail-silent, exit 0 unconditionally; absolute lt path recorded at install time (GUI git clients without PATH); refuse pre-existing unmanaged hooks without --force; --dry-run/--yes/--uninstall consent gating; reuse _upsert_managed_block/_strip_managed_block. Deprecate-but-keep the PS1 script. This is the 'select repos to enroll' surface: one consented command per repo.
acceptance_criteria: Marker compatibility with PS1-installed hooks verified byte-for-byte; unmanaged-hook refusal without --force; uninstall strips only the managed block; works on Windows (Git-for-Windows sh) and POSIX; no symlinks.

title: Doctor extension + sha-only drift comparison
description: version_in_sync requires exact version-line equality so every package bump cries wolf, training users to ignore doctor. Compare content sha only. Extend _doctor to also verify: connection profile presence, lt_ids.json binding, .mcp.json, settings hooks, watch config (informational), hook-block presence + stale-lt-path health. Payload gains non-imperative suggestions[] naming the exact repair verb. Doctor never writes.
acceptance_criteria: Version bump with unchanged text reports clean; test_doctor_treats_safe_default_absent_blocks_as_not_installed still passes; suggestions are non-imperative; JSON/exit-code contract preserved.

title: lab-tracker-setup skill: the onboarding wizard as agent prose
description: The conversational wizard lives in skill text, not maintained interactive code. skills/lab-tracker-setup/SKILL.md staged script: inventory (lt setup status) -> connectivity (suggest lab-tracker serve, never auto-start) -> credentials (human mints PAT in browser; agents never handle minting — service principals are blocked from /auth/*) -> scaffold (lt setup init) -> bind (lt project bind) -> watch folders (lt watch add, eliciting which folders matter) -> repo hooks (lt hooks install per user-selected repo) -> optional scheduler. Hard rules embedded: always --dry-run first, show the diff, ONE command per human approval, agent never self-initiates --yes, non-imperative phrasing. Keep command list honest via the existing skill-reference drift-test pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Skill command list covered by a drift test against the CLI; consent choreography rules present verbatim; no imperative mutating instructions.

title: Implement shared watch file observer and sinks
description: Add shared file discovery/fingerprinting utilities and sync sinks for staged evidence notes and acquisition outputs.

title: Recall eval + ranked matching for agentic draft pre-pass
description: Why: the AgenticGraphDraftClient pre-pass (graph_drafting.py: _agentic_read_only_tool_trace) exists to surface existing graph nodes so the draft links instead of duplicating, but nothing measures whether it surfaces the right nodes, and matching is unranked substring over JSON haystacks (a label hit scores the same as an incidental metadata hit; 'dep delay'-style vocabulary mismatches are invisible). What: (1) add a small checked-in recall@K eval — labeled cases mapping staged-note text to expected existing node ids — run in pytest against _agentic_search_existing_nodes; (2) boost label/statement/text field hits over other-metadata hits when ranking the capped 20 matches. Pattern source: Malloy Publisher's get_context_eval.ts + 4x name boosting (see docs/server-resident-agentic-drafting-design.md, 'Adjacent tool landscape', added 2026-07-06).
notes: Follow-up to closed lab-tracker-1325.4. Keep the pre-pass deterministic and read-only; this is measurement + ranking, not an architecture change. Embeddings are explicitly out of scope until the recall eval shows the lexical gap matters.

title: Let project contributors (non-admin) schedule, run, and review their project's daily batch
description: User goal 2026-06-24: a project contributor (e.g. trainee 'josh', global editor + project contributor) should independently schedule, run, and review the daily draft batch for their own project. Today: update_graph_draft_batch_settings requires project OWNER (graph_draft_service.py:457); POST /batches/run-now requires project OWNER (routes/graph_batches.py:158); frontend Batches controls gate on canManageGraph=canManageProjectMembers (admin||owner, app-shell.jsx:429). Review (list/get batches+runs) is already require_read. Change: relax settings + run-now to require_contributor (backend) and gate the frontend Batches/Review controls on canContributeToProject instead of canManageProjectMembers. Keep /batches/run-due admin-only (it is the cron poke across all projects). accept-ALL draft ops stays owner-gated (contributors accept ops individually) — note as minor follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: A project contributor can GET/PATCH their project's batch settings, POST /batches/run-now for their project, and review the resulting batches/drafts in the UI; cannot affect other projects; run-due stays admin-only. Backend authz tests added.

title: test_project_collaboration: order-dependent failures in full pytest run
description:
Two tests in tests/test_project_collaboration.py fail when run as part of the full suite but pass in isolation, suggesting test-ordering or shared-state pollution (e.g. global registry, on-disk artifact, or auth-token cache leaking between tests).

Failing tests (in full-suite run):
- tests/test_project_collaboration.py::test_project_membership_scopes_reads_and_contributor_notes
- tests/test_project_collaboration.py::test_contributor_submits_graph_change_set_for_admin_review

Symptom: POST /notes by 'undergrad'-role user returns 401 Unauthorized (expected 201). Assertion site: tests/test_project_collaboration.py:138.

Repro:
  .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest -q                          # both fail (246 passed, 2 failed)
  .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/test_project_collaboration.py -q   # both pass

First observed on commit f99d1b5 ((feat): retire in-memory API runtime, prescribed by bead lab-tracker-0if.1), which retired the in-memory store and rewrote service-layer auth-context handling across many service modules. Likely related to that teardown — probably an earlier test in the suite mutates shared state (a process-global auth/session cache, env var, or sqlite file) that the membership tests then read as the wrong identity.

Suggested investigation:
1. Run pytest with -p no:randomly (if applicable) and bisect: 'pytest tests/test_X.py tests/test_project_collaboration.py' for each X to find the polluting test.
2. Look for module-level state in the modified services from f99d1b5 (analysis/claim/dataset/note/project/question/session/visualization/graph_draft services) — anything that caches auth context or DB sessions across requests.
3. Check tests/api_helpers.py (new in f99d1b5) for fixtures that might leave state behind.

Likely owner: same author/agent who landed lab-tracker-0if.1, since the failure surface aligns with that change.

title: Preserve concrete agent and device credential provenance on captures
description: Personal access tokens and paired devices correctly resolve to a human user, so multiple agents for that human should share one Daily Review inbox. The concrete credential identity is currently lost: PAT verification yields token_id and label, but middleware drops them when constructing AuthContext; device_token_id is present in AuthContext but note creation and usage events do not persist a principal instance identifier. The record can say that a service principal acting for a user created a capture, but cannot distinguish which agent or device. Preserve credential-level audit provenance without making agent identity an inbox-scoping dimension.
design: Extend request/auth context with a non-secret principal_instance_id and optional label snapshot for PAT, device, and system principals. Persist acting_user_id, principal_type, and principal_instance_id in appropriate capture/provenance or audit records and usage events. Never store bearer secrets or token hashes in research records. Inbox assignment remains the represented human user; credential revocation does not erase historical provenance.
acceptance_criteria: Two PATs and a paired device for one user create captures assigned to the same human review stream but remain distinguishable in audit/provenance output; browser, PAT, device, system, and auth-disabled paths have defined behavior; no secret material is persisted or returned; revocation and user deletion preserve historical attribution safely; tests cover middleware propagation, note creation, usage events, and exports.

title: Reduce architectural complexity above functional need
description: Complexity evaluation (branch claude/codebase-complexity-eval-shg0dd) found the codebase's complexity is mostly architectural breadth, not tangled logic or leftover deferred-feature cruft (OCR/embeddings/vector-search/review-queue residue is ~0 files). Two deliberate abstraction choices dominate the excess and are addressable without a rewrite. Diagram: docs/internal-boundaries.md (Architecture at a Glance). This epic groups the concrete follow-ups.

title: Thin the LabTrackerAPI god-facade
description:
src/lab_tracker/api.py defines a single LabTrackerAPI class with ~164 methods that all 33 route modules delegate to (attached per request via api_from_request(), scope machinery in api.py + app_parts/middleware.py). It is the central coupling point: nearly any feature edit touches this class, and it makes the 26 clean service modules less independently reusable than their structure implies. Highest-value, highest-risk target.

## Context
Diagram + layer description: docs/internal-boundaries.md (Architecture at a Glance). Services already exist and are cleanly split under src/lab_tracker/services/.
acceptance_criteria: Routes depend on the relevant service(s) directly rather than routing every call through one god-object; api.py's method count drops materially; request-scope/commit-rollback lifecycle preserved (see docs/internal-boundaries.md); tests + ruff green.
notes:
Investigation found the facade encodes a real invariant: usage telemetry must fire exactly once at the external route->facade boundary. Services already call each other's mutating methods directly (graph_draft_applier does this 18x; also analysis_service, session_service) and those internal calls deliberately do NOT emit usage events. So the literal 'routes call services directly + telemetry in services' would regress telemetry (internal ops would emit spurious events).

Delivered instead: decomposed the 1322-line LabTrackerAPI monolith into per-domain mixins under src/lab_tracker/api_parts/ (projects, questions, notes, datasets, sessions, analyses, goals, graph_drafts, exploration, provenance, usage), each carrying its own delegation+telemetry methods. api.py now holds only the composition root + request-scope lifecycle (1322 -> 382 lines). Behaviour-preserving: method-level AST parity verified identical (160 methods, 0 missing/added, 0 body diffs); full suite 823 passed / 4 skipped; ruff clean. This kills the edit-coupling pain (a domain change now touches one mixin) and PRESERVES the telemetry boundary. Routes/tests unchanged.

Remaining (optional, larger): to literally make routes call services directly, telemetry would need to move to a route-level/middleware boundary (fires once per HTTP request, naturally external-only). Filing as follow-up.

title: Narrow application ports and add incremental static type checking
description: Every service receives the entire LabTrackerRepository Protocol, some Protocol signatures already omit parameters accepted and used by the concrete SQLAlchemy implementation, and façade mixins erase signatures through *args: Any, **kwargs: Any -> Any. No mypy or pyright gate detects drift.
design: Split broad infrastructure dependencies into use-case role protocols such as readers, stores, and UnitOfWork capabilities. Preserve explicit handler/facade signatures or remove redundant delegates. Introduce pyright or mypy incrementally over ports, application handlers, and composition roots with implementation-conformance tests; do not require a repo-wide strict conversion in one change.
acceptance_criteria: Selected repository/application ports expose only required capabilities; the SQLAlchemy implementation is statically checked against them; route/handler signatures retain useful types without Any delegation; CI runs a documented incremental static-type target; no runtime behavior changes.

title: Split GraphDraftService by generation, scheduling, review, and commit lifecycles
description: The first decomposition extracted GraphContextBuilder, GraphPatchValidator, and GraphPatchApplier, but GraphDraftService remains roughly 2,100 lines with eleven service dependencies and owns draft generation, provider/background execution, batch scheduling, review state, uploads/transcription, and canonical commit.
design: Keep the successful builder/validator/applier seams. Extract focused application coordinators for DraftGeneration, BatchScheduling/Execution, DraftReview, and TransactionalDraftCommit, each depending on narrow role protocols. Avoid a generic workflow framework and preserve the retained human-gated lifecycle.
acceptance_criteria: The four lifecycle responsibilities have explicit owners and focused tests; GraphDraftService is removed or reduced to a thin compatibility façade; constructor dependency breadth and module size fall materially; graph-draft API behavior, scheduling, authorization, and provenance remain unchanged; full graph-draft tests pass.

title: Evaluate collapsing the domain-model <-> ORM mapper layer
description:
Every retained entity is represented as both a Pydantic domain type (models.py) and a SQLAlchemy ORM row (db_models.py, 44 tables), joined by ~37 hand-written translators in sqlalchemy_mappers.py (1520 LOC). This buys persistence-independent domain types but is the largest structural LOC multiplier: adding one field can require edits across domain model, ORM model, mapper, repository, facade, and route. retained-v1-surface.md explicitly favors 'direct repository-backed operations over speculative abstractions'.

## Context
Diagram: docs/internal-boundaries.md. Mapper seam highlighted blue in the diagram.
acceptance_criteria: A written decision (ADR) recommending keep / collapse / partially-unify (e.g. Pydantic from_attributes off the ORM, or SQLModel-style unification), with migration cost and the persistence-independence tradeoff spelled out. If 'collapse', a follow-up implementation issue is filed.
notes: ADR written: docs/domain-orm-mapping-decision.md. Key finding: the mapper is NOT redundant boilerplate — it bridges a real impedance mismatch (nested value objects <-> flat columns, child-row assembly since the ORM has 0 relationship() defs, legacy shapes). BUT ~300+ of its manual conversions are ACCIDENTAL: 222 _uuid/_uuid_str (all IDs are String(36), 0 Uuid cols), 86 enum .value/Status() (enums stored as String, 0 Enum cols), 38 _as_utc, 23 JSON helpers. Decision: KEEP the 3-layer separation (rejected SQLModel unification and from_attributes-only), and remove the accidental churn via TypeDecorators (GUID/enum/UTC-datetime) backed by the SAME String(36) storage => NO migration, plus a round-trip mapping-completeness test. Est. 30-40% mapper shrink + removes a bug class. Higher value / lower risk than the facade purity work.

title: Fold single-endpoint micro-route modules where cohesive
description: Several route modules expose a single endpoint each (assistant.py, portfolio.py, external_artifacts.py, search.py, schema.py). This adds file-count/navigation noise with little real complexity. Low-priority cleanup: consolidate genuinely-related one-endpoint modules where it improves discoverability, WITHOUT changing URLs, envelopes, pagination, or auth (per docs/internal-boundaries.md Route Layout). Leave modules that are one-endpoint-by-domain (e.g. search) alone if folding them muddies ownership.
acceptance_criteria: No change to public URLs/contracts; route count of trivial single-endpoint files reduced only where cohesion improves; tests green. May be closed as wontfix if analysis shows current split is clearer.

title: Move usage telemetry to a route/request boundary so routes can call services directly
description: Follow-up to t4x0.1. The facade currently owns usage-event emission (fires once at the external route->facade boundary). To let routes call services directly (the original t4x0.1 wording), relocate telemetry to a route-level decorator/dependency or ASGI middleware that fires once per HTTP request (naturally external-only), so pushing it into services is unnecessary and internal service-to-service calls still don't double-count. Larger change: touches the telemetry mechanism + ~253 route call sites + tests. Only worth doing if the per-domain mixin decomposition (already landed) proves insufficient.

title: Add domain<->ORM mapping-completeness test
description: Step 1 of the t4x0.2 rollout (docs/domain-orm-mapping-decision.md).
