Before changing any column types, add a test that (a) round-trips every retained entity through <entity>_to_model -> <entity>_from_model and asserts equality, and (b) asserts every ORM column in db_models.py is referenced by its mapper. This makes the subsequent TypeDecorator migration safe: a forgotten conversion fails a test instead of silently dropping data. Must land green against today's code first.

title: Add db_types.py TypeDecorators: GUID, enum, UTC-datetime
description: Step 2. Add lab_tracker/db_types.py with TypeDecorators backed by identical storage (GUID over String(36); string-backed enum; UTC-normalizing DateTime), plus unit tests for bind/result round-trips on BOTH sqlite and postgres. No schema/data migration — storage representation is unchanged. Rationale + counts in docs/domain-orm-mapping-decision.md (222 _uuid, 86 enum, 38 datetime conversions to remove).

title: Migrate one entity (Session) to TypeDecorators as the proof pattern
description: Step 3. Swap Session's ORM column types to the db_types decorators and delete the now-redundant _uuid/.value/_as_utc conversions from its mapper (session_to_model/from_model/apply). Confirm the mapping-completeness test + full suite stay green under sqlite (and postgres if available). This diff is the reviewable pattern for the sweep.

title: Sweep remaining entities to TypeDecorators (largest churn first)
description: Step 4. Apply the Session pattern to the rest, largest mapper churn first: Dataset, Note, Question, Analysis, Claim, graph-draft rows, then the tail. Expect ~30-40% shrink of sqlalchemy_mappers.py. Each entity: swap column types, delete redundant conversions, keep completeness test + suite green.
notes: ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED. The full sweep falsified the ADR premise that this is storage-layer-local. Migrating all entities' columns broke ~60+ call sites across 20 files because ORM id/enum attrs are consumed as STRINGS codebase-wide: UUID(row.x) (45 sites, loud crash), Python-level row.id==str(x) (5 sites, silent inversion), and dicts/sets keyed by row.id in repository join-code (silent empty counts/joins). UtcDateTime also shifts onupdate timing (benign in prod, breaks timestamp-pinning tests). Enum migration itself is safe (str-enums). Got 405 failures -> 12 before reverting to keep the safe, green baseline (t4x0.5/0.6/0.7). Revised plan in docs/domain-orm-mapping-decision.md (Revision section): do it PER ENTITY (migrate columns + fix that entity's consuming sites + clean its mapper + full suite green), add a tolerant ensure_uuid() helper first, and treat as LOWER priority than assumed. Session (t4x0.7) is the proven per-entity template.

title: Establish typed command/query handlers and remove persistence access from routes
description: docs/internal-boundaries.md says routes enter through LabTrackerAPI/services, but 18 route modules query LabTrackerRepository or raw SQLAlchemy Session directly. List/read optimizations are legitimate, yet authorization, cleanup, storage sequencing, pagination, and persistence details are now split across transport and service layers.
design: Adopt an explicit application boundary: commands invoke one transactional command handler; reads invoke typed query/read-model handlers that may use optimized persistence internally. Routes parse/authenticate, call one handler, and translate the result. Do not force rich domain hydration for every read, and update the architecture document to match the actual retained design.
acceptance_criteria: No route imports or obtains a concrete SQLAlchemy Session; direct repository access is eliminated or restricted to explicitly documented query adapters behind typed handlers; authorization and storage cleanup ownership is unambiguous; route behavior, envelopes, pagination, telemetry, and performance are preserved; docs and tests reflect the boundary.

title: Make Funnel-backed Lab Tracker runtime self-restoring
description: Incident on 2026-06-22: the Tailscale Funnel for https://mwcppc01ysbc155.tail79f9d8.ts.net was configured and reachable, but returned 502 because nothing was listening on 127.0.0.1:8000. Docker Desktop/Postgres were stopped, while .env pointed the live graph at SQLite lab_tracker.db. Manual recovery was: run alembic upgrade head against SQLite, start uvicorn on 127.0.0.1:8000, then verify /health, /readiness, /projects, and /app through localhost and Funnel. Add a durable Windows startup/supervision path so the hosted workstation instance comes back after reboot/crash, and make the intended auth posture for Funnel explicit.
acceptance_criteria: A documented Windows startup/service or scheduled-task path starts the correct Lab Tracker DB/runtime automatically; a health check or restart mechanism covers upstream process death; recovery preserves the intended live graph data source; docs state whether Funnel is allowed with auth disabled or require auth for public exposure; verification covers localhost and Funnel /health, /readiness, and /app.

title: Transactional integrity and human-gated domain invariants
description: Findings from the 2026-07-15 ArjanCodes-style deep review. Make every business command preserve the same atomicity and human-gating guarantees regardless of HTTP, direct façade, background, SDK, CLI, or MCP entry point. Also close verified domain-contract gaps that silently lose provenance or permit inconsistent state.
design: Put transaction ownership at the top-level application command. Preserve retained-v1 human review boundaries. Favor explicit commands and typed tri-state inputs over ambient commits or magic defaults. Add regression coverage at every relevant entry point; do not collapse the documented domain/ORM/request-model separation.
acceptance_criteria: All child correctness issues are fixed or explicitly deferred with rationale; composite commands are atomic across supported entry points; client defaults preserve staging; provenance and PATCH semantics round-trip; focused and full quality gates pass.

title: Make application commands atomic outside HTTP request middleware
description:
RepositoryUnitOfWork commits each service call when ServiceContext is not request-managed (src/lab_tracker/services/base.py:58-83). Composite workflows such as GraphDraftService.commit_graph_change_set and AnalysisService.commit_analysis call several independently committing services. Reproduced via the direct façade: a valid graph create followed by an invalid operation raises but leaves the first entity persisted and the change set stuck in committing; HTTP happens to be atomic because middleware owns a wider request transaction.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Construct a direct repository-backed LabTrackerAPI without LabTrackerRequestScope.
2. Prepare an accepted graph change set whose first operation creates a valid question and whose second references a missing question.
3. Call commit_graph_change_set and observe the exception.
4. Query the repository: the first question exists and the change set remains committing.
design: Introduce a narrow explicit UnitOfWork owned by each top-level application command. Nested services share the same repository/transaction and never commit independently. Preserve the existing HTTP after-commit/rollback side-effect semantics and define an equivalent safe boundary for direct/background use.
acceptance_criteria: A valid-then-invalid graph change set leaves zero applied entities and does not remain committing through both HTTP and direct façade paths; commit_analysis and other identified composite commands roll back as one unit; success commits exactly once; after-commit/rollback actions retain their semantics; SQLite and Postgres tests plus ruff pass.

title: Make MCP evidence bundles transactional and strongly idempotent
description:
record_evidence_bundle validates and writes dataset, analysis, claim, visualization, and note components sequentially in src/lab_tracker/mcp_evidence_bundle.py. A later invalid component can be converted to a warning after earlier entities were committed, while retry lookup scans only the first 200 records and reuses claims/visualizations using incomplete semantic matches.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call record_evidence_bundle with dry_run=false, a valid dataset payload, and an analysis payload missing method_hash.
2. Observe a success-shaped data response containing an analysis warning/skipped plan.
3. List datasets and observe that the dataset was committed despite the invalid bundle.
design: Parse the full request into typed commands, validate all components before writing, then execute one server-side transactional use case. Persist a server-enforced bundle idempotency key and canonical request fingerprint; identical retries reuse the result, while the same key with conflicting canonical input returns a conflict.
acceptance_criteria: Any invalid component causes zero bundle entities to persist; successful bundles commit all intended entities once; an identical retry is a no-op returning the same identities beyond 200 existing records; conflicting reuse returns an explicit error; missing/non-object components fail validation rather than disappearing; MCP and API tests pass.

title: Preserve DatasetFile size_bytes through normalization and provenance export
description:
DatasetFile declares size_bytes, but service-level manifest normalization and acquisition-output promotion reconstruct files with only path/checksum (src/lab_tracker/services/shared.py), and the canonical manifest payload omits the field even though provenance export supports it. Accepted scientific provenance is silently lost.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create or commit a dataset manifest containing a file with path, checksum, and size_bytes=12.
2. Read the persisted dataset and export its provenance.
3. Observe that normalization/canonical manifest handling has dropped size_bytes.
design: Carry size_bytes through input normalization, acquisition-output merging, persistence mapping, reads, and PROV export. Make and document an explicit decision about whether size participates in the canonical commit hash; preserve backward compatibility for manifests that omit it.
acceptance_criteria: Create/commit/read/export round trips preserve size_bytes for submitted and promoted files; legacy manifests without size still work; canonical hash behavior is documented and tested; a regression test covers the existing size_bytes=12 fixture end to end.

title: Standardize PATCH omitted-versus-explicit-null semantics
description:
Several PATCH schemas collapse an omitted optional field and an explicit null to Python None, while routes pass values unconditionally and services update only on non-None. Requests such as {"hypothesis": null} report success but cannot clear the field. The same pattern affects captions, target dates, external references, environment hashes, and other optional fields.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a question with a non-null hypothesis.
2. PATCH the question with {"hypothesis": null}.
3. Observe a successful response whose hypothesis is still present instead of cleared.
4. Repeat the audit pattern for other nullable PATCH fields.
design: Define one application-level NotProvided sentinel or typed patch command populated from Pydantic model_fields_set. Use it consistently: omitted means unchanged, explicit null means clear when the field is nullable, and a supplied value means validate/set. Reuse the existing project group_id and supervision update precedents.
acceptance_criteria: An audited inventory identifies every retained PATCH field with tri-state semantics; omitted, explicit null, and explicit value are behaviorally distinct and tested; non-nullable fields reject null; response/version snapshots reflect real changes only; API compatibility tests pass.

title: Serialize concurrent question-parent updates to preserve the DAG invariant
description:
QuestionService checks for cycles by reading the current graph before replacing parent edges, but persistence does not lock or serialize the relevant graph. Under Postgres, two concurrent opposite-edge updates can both validate against the old state and jointly create a cycle.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Under Postgres, start two concurrent transactions over questions A and B with no parent cycle.
2. In transaction one set A's parent to B; in transaction two set B's parent to A.
3. Let both validate against the old graph and commit.
4. Observe that the resulting graph contains a cycle.
design: Choose and document a transaction-safe strategy for the cross-row DAG invariant: project/question-graph advisory lock, serializable retry, or equivalent scoped locking. Keep the existing fast sequential validation, but make the invariant hold under real concurrent transactions.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic Postgres concurrency test attempts opposite/cyclic parent updates and proves at most one commits; no cycle is persisted; the loser receives a stable conflict/validation response; normal disjoint updates remain concurrent; SQLite behavior remains supported.

title: Enforce local claim invariants at domain and database boundaries
description: Claim confidence range and the rule that SUPPORTED claims require dataset or analysis evidence currently live only in procedural service helpers. Mutable domain records and ORM rows can represent invalid local state when constructed or written outside the expected service path.
design: Use value/domain validation for construction and named status transitions, plus database CHECK constraints for local row invariants where expressible. Keep cross-entity evidence-existence checks in the transactional application layer. Avoid making ORM rows the domain model.
acceptance_criteria: Claim construction and assignment cannot produce out-of-range confidence; supported-without-evidence is rejected through every supported write entry point; suitable database checks protect direct persistence paths; migrations are backward-safe and tests cover service, mapper, and database behavior.

title: Scope POSIX lifecycle fallback regression off native Windows
description: GitHub Actions run 30166036471 is red only in Windows containment/local artifacts: tests/test_bounded_subprocess.py::test_process_lifecycle_fails_when_group_survives_leader_fallback directly constructs _PosixProcessLifecycle on win32. The production platform guard correctly raises ProcessUnsupportedPlatformError before the test's expected ProcessCleanupError. Linux test, PostgreSQL, and browser E2E jobs pass. This blocks the project-defined native Windows release gate for Marion onboarding.
design: Prefer an explicit pytest skipif for non-POSIX on this test, matching its private lifecycle scope. Do not weaken the production fail-closed platform guard. Keep the change test-only unless additional evidence demonstrates a runtime defect.
acceptance_criteria: The fallback regression remains exercised on POSIX; native Windows does not instantiate the POSIX lifecycle; the focused bounded-subprocess suite passes locally; GitHub Actions jobs test, postgres, e2e, and Windows containment/local artifacts all pass on the pushed branch.

title: Make scheduled-run indicator independent of the loaded run window
description: The /app/batches Scheduled pill (frontend_src/features/batches.jsx) correlates a pending batch to its producing run via the loaded run history, but /batches/runs is fetched with limit=20 while /batches uses limit=100. A stale unreviewed pending batch whose producing run is beyond the 20 most-recent runs shows no Scheduled pill even though it was scheduler-produced (cosmetic only; the batch is fully reviewable). Robust fix: surface the producing trigger on the change set itself (add a trigger field to GraphChangeSet populated from the batch run and exposed in the /batches payload) so the UI does not depend on the run-history window. Interim mitigation (bump runs limit to 100) only narrows the gap. Found by the lab-tracker-09ok diff review.
acceptance_criteria: A scheduler-produced pending batch shows the Scheduled indicator regardless of how many runs precede it; covered by a frontend test that places the producing run outside the loaded run window.

title: Add MATLAB runtime smoke coverage
description: The MATLAB consumer package has source-contract tests and a smoke example, but this workstation does not have a MATLAB runtime, so the package was not executed end-to-end locally. Add a MATLAB-runner smoke test or documented CI/manual validation path that runs the capture_figure_smoke.m flow against a test Lab Tracker API when a MATLAB license/runtime is available.

title: Add one-tap voice transcription from pending review
description: Make deferred voice-note review obvious from the pending review UI. A researcher who saved a voice note or photo+voice bundle for later should be able to trigger transcription in one tap from the pending item and then edit the transcript before graph drafting.
design: Keep this mobile-first: avoid desktop-style forms, preserve defer/retry behavior, and make transcript state visually distinct from model inference and graph operations.
acceptance_criteria: Pending review items with raw audio expose a direct transcribe action when no transcript exists. Existing transcripts are visible and editable from the same review path. Transcription failures show an explicit error and do not pretend draft generation succeeded. Photo+voice bundles keep audio, transcript, and image provenance linked together for later drafting.
close_reason: Added one-tap transcription and draft controls to mobile pending review items, with transcript-ready state, bundle transcript blocking, per-item errors, and frontend coverage for deferred bundle transcription before drafting.

title: y5j8 doc ownership: commit the store:// experiment-doc edits (currently uncommitted)
description: From the y5j8 epic analysis (2026-07-03): the epic's acceptance criterion 'the two experiment docs describe store:// as the OneDrive mechanism' is satisfied only by UNCOMMITTED working-tree edits on the workstation checkout — at origin/main neither docs/lab-experiment-documentation.md nor docs/experiment-walkthrough-coverage.md mentions store:// at all, and no y5j8 child owns the doc updates. Commit those edits from the workstation tree, give the criterion an owner, and plan for the interim text ('registration is currently a raw POST') to be updated when pwsb ships lt store verbs. Also: retained-v1-surface.md never names the data-store registry despite declaring itself the exhaustive surface — add its entry in the same change.

title: Fix phone capture mobile option layout
description: On a phone, the Phone capture section option buttons displace labels/text offscreen, making the capture options hard to read. Adjust the mobile layout so option controls wrap or stack without horizontal overflow.

title: Daily Review reading experience
description: Rebuild Daily Review from a JSON triage queue into a short, finite, illustrated reading experience with natural-language feedback and a real closure moment. Morning Read was a presentation metaphor from the 2026-06-16 design round; it is not a separate entity, a persisted dated edition, or a morning-only workflow. The domain and navigation name remain Daily Review, used whenever the scientist chooses within the configured cadence. Design decisions: (a) a HIGHLIGHTS view over the full queue caps attention at roughly seven cards, never deletes or ages items, and keeps /app/batches as the complete record; (b) feedback follows a determinism gradient from instant Keep/Not now, through simple slots, to model-resolved propose-only intent with echo-back and confirmation; (c) closure is role-aware and nothing reaches the graph until an explicit interactive human save. Builds on GraphChangeSet/Operation, context_packet, source_refs, review notes, revision/transcription, next_questions, publication_readiness, and EntityVersionModel. Consumes the Read register from lab-tracker-83m2.8. Multimodal hero photos, voice, TTS, and push remain gated by lab-tracker-jptw. Honors retained-v1: nothing auto-commits, provenance everywhere, fail loudly, no semantic search, and no email digest.
acceptance_criteria: Children deliver a finite Daily Review reading surface, deterministic current-user projection, role-aware human closure, and optional privacy-gated engagement/push; no separate Morning Read or persisted edition entity is introduced, and /app/batches remains the complete queue.

title: Committer role: PI delegates true commit power
description: Today commit is OWNER-ONLY (graph_draft_service.py:804 require_owner; roles in models.py:79-82 are viewer/contributor/owner). The PI can't review everything and wants to grant true commit authority to trusted lab members. Add ProjectMembershipRole.COMMITTER between contributor and owner; add PROJECT_COMMIT_ROLES + require_committer in services/project_authorization.py; swap the commit gate at graph_draft_service.py:804 from require_owner to require_committer. A committer's Keep->Save COMMITS directly (skips submit->review); a contributor's Keep->Save STAGES for the PI (submit). Owner grants the role via the existing owner-gated POST/PATCH /projects/{id}/members (project_service.py:452-478). Update frontend canCommitDraft/canManageGraph (graph-drafts.jsx:206-208, app-shell.jsx:121) to recognize committer. ~30 lines across 3 backend files + frontend. Review (approve/reject submitted drafts) and member management stay owner-only.
acceptance_criteria: A committer can commit a change set directly; a contributor still only submits; owner can assign the role; review + member-management remain owner-only; tests cover each role at the commit gate.

title: Prevent orphaned Daily Review assignments during offboarding
description: Daily Review responsibility is stored separately from creation provenance, but current membership removal and ownership reassignment do not transfer review_assignee fields or per-user GraphDraftBatchSettings. A departed, demoted, or unavailable user can therefore retain pending drafts they can no longer access, while scheduled settings remain stale. Existing ownership reassignment rewrites created_by fields yet leaves assignee-keyed edit checks pointing at the old user. Make open review work and cadence configuration explicit parts of offboarding without falsifying who originally created the capture or draft.
design: Before project membership removal, enumerate open assigned drafts, pending/running batch jobs, personal batch settings, and pending review notifications. Require an explicit transfer, cancellation, or archival disposition. Transfer mutable responsibility fields and append an auditable handoff event; do not silently rewrite immutable creator/proposer provenance. Validate the successor has appropriate current project membership and revoke or disable departed-user scheduling and notification state.
acceptance_criteria: Removing or demoting a project member cannot leave an actionable draft, pending batch, personal cadence row, or review notification assigned to someone without access; transfer/cancel/archive choices are explicit and audited; successors can immediately act within their role; original capture and proposal provenance remains queryable; tests cover contributor departure with ready and changes-requested drafts, pending work, settings, notifications, and multiple project owners.

title: Daily review delivery — Slice 3: email cue via the user's own routine (cue not digest)
description:
The adoption play and the concrete revision of udv1's "no email digest" guardrail (see the delivery decision bead). Lands the daily cue where inbox-dwelling scientists already look — as a CUE, never a digest.

Scope:
(a) A read-only "editions ready since {watermark}" endpoint — a thin filter over existing GraphDraftBatchRun rows plus the daily_review_engagements projection (udv1.7). No new scheduler, no new source of truth for "when".
(b) The SAME external routine that already calls POST /batches/run-due (per docs/scheduled-daily-review.md) gains ONE step: after triggering drafts, poll editions-ready, render the fixed contentless cue, and send through the USER'S OWN mailbox. Lab Tracker holds no SMTP creds and owns no transport — pointer-not-reimplementation per docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md.
(c) Project-coalescing: one cue across N ready projects ("ready across 2 projects — 6 things, ~3 min"), keyed on {user, edition_date}, inheriting run-due idempotency — never N separate emails.

Same contentless payload and egress defaults as the push cue (narrow jptw ruling): count + signed deep link, no science, project name off by default, count suppressed on sensitivity-tagged editions. The email deep-links into the in-app read where every accept/reject still happens.

Slack DM-to-self is a sibling adapter after this — opt-in, never a shared channel (a shared-channel cue would tell teammates "user X has N unreviewed items").

Depends on the push cue slice (the EditionReady event, signed-link machinery, and contentless template are shared).
acceptance_criteria: A read-only editions-ready-since-watermark endpoint exists; the user's own run-due routine sends a contentless email cue (count + deep link, no science) that deep-links to the in-app read; multiple ready projects coalesce into one cue keyed on user+edition_date; Lab Tracker stores no mail credentials; feature opt-in and default-off.

title: Phase 1: Natural-language feedback intent endpoint (propose-only)
description: The headline NL-feedback ask. Add POST /graph-drafts/{id}/operations/{op}/feedback: Tier-2 resolver that takes a free-form utterance + the operation(s) + the stored context_packet and returns a typed, PROPOSE-ONLY ResolvedIntent[] under a CONSTRAINED intent schema (modeled on the existing graph_patch_response_schema) whose only legal verbs map 1:1 onto existing transforms (retarget_link reuses nextPayloadWithTarget, adjust_confidence, reclassify). It MUTATES NOTHING. On user confirm, deterministic code applies each intent through the EXISTING validated PATCH update_graph_change_operation (graph_draft_service.py:567-633; re-runs patch_validator, stamps edited_at/edited_by). Auto-populate the per-op review_note from the resolved turn (this is the principled version of bead cns). Voice input reuses transcribe_audio; surface transcript_confidence. The whole-set revise endpoint survives unchanged as the 'redraft everything' escape hatch. HARD INVARIANT: an NL turn can never commit, never skip the state machine, never edit an applied op; apply re-checks current op state and fails loudly (409) on a stale intent.
acceptance_criteria: Endpoint returns typed propose-only intents from NL/voice; confirm applies via existing validated PATCH; review_note auto-populated; 409 on stale/illegal intent; cannot commit or edit applied ops; folds in cns.

title: Phase 1: Daily Review reading surface (/app/review)
description: Build a mobile-first reading column around 680px wide for the Daily Review. It consumes the personal-review APIs plus GET /graph-drafts/{id}. Each proposal is a plain-language question card in serif prose: the user words from source_refs[].quote are softly highlighted; show a source-region crop when present, otherwise the whole image or none; render confidence as a band and number, with null as unscored. Decisions: Keep / Not now uses the existing operation PATCH with undo; a tell-me-what-is-off composer uses the propose-only feedback endpoint and requires echo-back confirmation; voice reuses transcribe_audio. Fold raw JSON, semantic type, context packet, and model under exact-change detail. Routine high-confidence links may collapse into one expand-to-glance card but never blind clear-all. Explicit Save my kept changes follows role-aware closure: a committer commits, while a contributor submits work that needs a project committer. Keep the desktop graph-draft editor as the power path.
acceptance_criteria: New /app/review Daily Review reading column uses the personal assigned-to-me queue; proposals show grounded quotes, optional source imagery, and confidence; Keep/Not now and confirmed natural-language feedback use existing validated operation transitions; closure is role-aware; deep editor remains available.

title: Phase 2: DailyReviewService projection + curation ranker
description: Add a deterministic DailyReviewService projection for the authenticated user. GET /projects/{id}/daily-review?date= returns four typed sections: (0) a dateline recap from EntityVersionModel rows committed since the previous review date plus the prior commit message, with no LLM or emotion attribution; (1) ranked and capped proposals using confidence, goal proximity, open-question relevance, publication gaps, and staleness, grouped one card per source note; (2) worth-a-thought from next_questions, the goal-free fallback, and publication_readiness; (3) closure. The date parameter is the calendar evaluation date for reproducible ranking and recap, not a persisted edition or separate content object. The projection owns no write state. It is a highlights view over the full queue: unfeatured items roll forward and re-rank, the full set stays one tap away, and failed drafts surface loudly. Extend portfolio.py with a current-user daily_review summary that replaces the generic unreviewed-claim count and all-visible-batches banner.
acceptance_criteria: Endpoint returns the four typed sections for the authenticated user and requested review date without persisting an edition; deterministic ranking caps attention without deleting work; failed drafts surface; portfolio summary reflects only work actionable by the current user.

title: Phase 2: next_questions goal-free fallback
description: next_questions returns EMPTY for any project without an open Goal plus open unanswered questions (assistant_next_questions.py:59-67) — common for exploratory bench work, which would blank the daily review's forward-thread and empty-day spine. Add a deterministic fallback when no ranked question exists: an open Question untouched for N weeks (via EntityVersionModel recency) or a publication_readiness structural gap. Add a per-entity resurfacing cooldown so the same item doesn't nag two days running (small new table or reuse engagement log).
acceptance_criteria: Forward-thread/empty-day spine yields a sensible item for goal-free projects; resurfacing respects a per-entity cooldown; labeled honestly (recency/gap, not 'semantically related').

title: Phase 3: Habit mechanics — in-app cue, closure, empty day (no streaks)
description: Make it a low-friction daily ritual using in-app surfaces only (push is a separate child). The once-daily home card (replacing the count banner) with a finishability promise ('4 things, ~2 min'). The close: literal bottom of page, honest generated reflection from actions actually taken this session, one forward thread, explicit save, then collapses to 'Reviewed - see you tomorrow' and is gone. The empty-day ladder (progress-but-no-notes -> dateline + one resurfaced item; nothing-at-all -> one open question + 'or just enjoy the quiet'); a model FAILURE looks loudly different from a quiet day (maps to 'failed' status + error_metadata). HARD NO on streaks/points/badges (rewarding queue-clearing taxes data quality); only a positive-only, substance-based, never-punitive note ('your graph grew 12 well-supported connections this month'). Backlog dread defused: capped today, un-featured rolls forward (never silently discarded), full /app/batches backstop linked.
acceptance_criteria: Daily cue + finishability promise; closure state with honest reflection + forward thread; empty-day ladder; loud failure distinct from quiet day; no streaks/gamification anywhere.

title: Phase 3: Daily Review engagement + push infrastructure (privacy-gated)
description: Build the optional engagement and Web Push layer on the already-shipped in-process graph-draft scheduler and worker. Add daily_review_engagements keyed by user, nullable project, and review_date with opened/completed/decided_count; derive continuity by query rather than storing a streak. Add a resurfacing cooldown log, per-user reminder time, and live timezone so travel does not produce badly timed reminders. Add a PWA Web Push pipeline and loud surfacing of missed or failed scheduled reviews. Push notifications are delivery for Daily Review assignments, not persisted editions. Reuse the design-system mobile navigation. The current uncommitted user-scoped review-notification and Web Push work belongs to this bead. BLOCKED by lab-tracker-jptw because push content may expose unpublished science on a lock screen.
acceptance_criteria: Per-user reminder time and live timezone are supported; engagement uses review_date and does not create an edition entity or streak counter; existing scheduler events enqueue user-scoped push delivery; missed runs fail loudly; privacy policy lab-tracker-jptw is satisfied before push ships.

title: Add user-scoped Web Push review notifications
description: Implement the Web Push slice of lab-tracker-udv1.7 for daily reviews. Bind each browser push subscription to the authenticated user and optional paired device; when a graph-draft batch transitions successfully to READY, deliver one generic 'Review available' notification to every active subscription for review_assignee_user_id. Tighten the pending-review banner/API to support current-user reviewer scoping. Handle invalid subscriptions, logout/rebinding semantics, secure-context configuration, and deep linking without exposing unpublished science on the lock screen.
design: Use a durable subscription table plus a delivery/outbox record keyed by review and recipient to prevent duplicates. Resolve recipient exclusively from GraphChangeSet.review_assignee_user_id and request authentication. Notification body contains no project, note, claim, or scientific content. Treat a browser service-worker subscription as owned by one current user at a time; rebind an endpoint on authenticated subscribe and remove it on unsubscribe. Keep push fail-soft so batch generation remains successful when delivery fails.
acceptance_criteria: Authenticated users can subscribe/unsubscribe without supplying or impersonating another user_id; multiple subscriptions fan out only for the assigned reviewer; READY delivery is idempotent and generic, with a deep link to the review; service worker handles push and notification clicks; current-user review counts do not include other reviewers' work; invalid/expired endpoints are disabled; configuration and HTTPS/privacy behavior are documented; backend and frontend tests pass.

title: Scope manual Daily Review runs and watermarks by reviewer
description: The authoritative retained surface promises per-(project,user) batch settings and run history, but POST /batches/run-now supplies no reviewer. GraphDraftService therefore selects all staged notes in the project, creates an unassigned run/change set, and falls back to the triggering actor for edit ownership. Repository cursor queries treat a null reviewer as no reviewer predicate, so a manual run can inherit another user latest successful window, skip older captures, or be ignored by later assigned scheduled runs and redraft the same notes. Make every new manual Daily Review run reviewer-scoped by default and remove null-as-all ambiguity from cursor and dedup semantics. If project owners still need an all-project recovery run, expose it as a separate explicit oversight operation with defined assignment rather than overloading the personal Run now action.
design: For the normal path, derive review_assignee_user_id from the authenticated human represented by browser, paired device, or personal access token; filter source notes and watermarks by that user; include the user in the batch key. Treat legacy null-assignee rows explicitly during migration/readback instead of allowing null to mean every reviewer. Keep canonical notes project-visible and preserve created_by as provenance.
acceptance_criteria: Run now creates a batch containing only staged notes assigned to the authenticated user; every new manual run and resulting batch change set has a non-null reviewer user; latest-success and already-drafted lookups cannot cross reviewer boundaries; repeated manual and scheduled runs neither skip nor redraft another user captures; multi-user tests cover interleaved windows, concurrent/redundant triggers, and any explicit owner recovery path.

title: Add personal Daily Review APIs and explicit project oversight
description: The Daily Review banner and /app/batches currently consume project-visible GET /batches and GET /batches/runs results without an assignee filter, so one user can be told that a teammate review is theirs and can open work they cannot edit. The cadence UI also omits user_id and therefore reads and writes the shared project-default row; contributors can alter the fallback used by teammates instead of configuring their own review. Add a first-class personal attention projection across accessible projects, retain explicit project-wide oversight for owners and PIs, and make settings semantics unambiguous.
design: Expose current-user semantics without allowing clients to spoof arbitrary beneficiaries: assigned_to=me or a dedicated /daily-review endpoint resolves the authenticated user server-side and supports optional project filtering. Provide separate, clearly named project-drafts and needs-commit views for shared governance. Settings GET/PATCH default to the current user; project-default template management uses an explicit owner/admin path. Project access continues to control visibility while assignment controls personal queue inclusion.
acceptance_criteria: A user can retrieve one assigned-to-me Daily Review queue across all accessible projects and optionally filter by project; the home banner, /app/review, and personal batch history use that queue and never count teammate-only assignments; Waiting on others and owner/committer oversight are separate explicit views; settings GET/PATCH without an administrative project-default operation affect the authenticated user row; only authorized owners/admins can change the project template; API, repository, and frontend tests cover two contributors and an owner.

title: Fix review-confirmed figure capture and idiom doctor findings
description: Review of the implemented lab-tracker-g88n and lab-tracker-28dz work found one must-fix and six correctness issues. Fix the localized figure-capture and doctor behavior, add regression tests for the corrected behavior, export beads, and push the branch.

title: Review and commit Codex baseline graph drafts before Josh/Yuanchi trial
description: Human review gate for the temporal odor gradient baseline. Codex created READY change sets 13328ee4-36d3-4619-8603-0607360b04c2 (100 source notes, 27 proposed operations) and 67967825-a9eb-4a37-a301-83b10b3462b4 (18 source notes, 4 proposed operations), covering all 118 staged notes through the fixed cutoff 2026-07-26T20:06:19Z. Review and commit them in order. Josh Chen and Yuanchi Ha each have an active editor invitation expiring 2026-08-01, but neither has consumed the invite or joined project ebc75a3b-8304-463c-9b94-f7ff189af4c1 yet.
acceptance_criteria: A human reviews every proposed operation and resolves clarification requests; both change sets are committed in order; the next review cursor remains 2026-07-26T20:06:19Z so later notes are fresh trial updates; Josh and Yuanchi accept their invitations and the project owner adds each account as a project contributor before the trial begins.

title: Require agents to recover timed-out commit captures
description: A Lab Tracker post-commit upload can time out after the server has accepted the evidence, leaving a local outbox event and prompting agents to report it as unsynced without attempting recovery. Teach every managed agent surface to treat timeouts as ambiguous, run 'lt outbox sync' from the originating repository, then verify with 'lt outbox status' before reporting an unresolved event.
acceptance_criteria: Generated AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md activation blocks and AGENTS.lt.md tell agents that after a commit-capture timeout/failure they must run 'lt outbox sync' and then 'lt outbox status'; guidance explains idempotent deduplication and permits unresolved reporting only after the retry fails and status still shows pending events; init/update regression tests cover the canonical text; relevant tests and lint pass.
close_reason: Implemented mandatory sync-then-status recovery guidance in managed agent prompts and hook diagnostics, documented ambiguous timeout semantics, and added init/update/hook regressions. Focused, packaging, MCP tests and Ruff pass.

title: Usage telemetry: local-first usage_events to understand app usage
description: Capture how Lab Tracker is actually used (HTTP, MCP, CLI) without reimplementing an analytics tool and without exposing research content. Approach: a local append-only usage_events table written through one swappable record_usage_event seam in the service layer, below all three surfaces. Locked decisions: default OFF locally and ON for deployments; retention = roll up + prune at 1 year; egress = local-only Postgres with the swappable seam kept (revisitable). Open: confirm egress stays local-only long term; actor identity granularity (raw user_id vs per-instance salted hash). Privacy red line: capture only verb + resource_type + UUID + actor + surface + outcome + timing; NEVER titles, bodies, descriptions, transcripts, filenames, search query strings (act + result count only), request bodies, or raw URL paths. Keep usage_events OUT of PROV-O export. Single shared seam confirmed at services/base.py:105 (run_after_commit/run_after_rollback).

title: usage_events table + UsageEventModel + Alembic migration
description: Foundational schema. Append-only table: event_id, occurred_at, verb (enum), resource_type (enum), resource_id (UUID nullable), actor_user_id, actor_role, principal_type (USER/DEVICE), surface (http/mcp/cli nullable in Phase 1), project_id (nullable), outcome (ok/error), duration_ms (nullable). Enum/UUID/timestamp columns ONLY, no free text. Copy the table+migration precedent from RecordExportEventModel (db_models.py:1021-1045, migration 0032).
design: Run: uv run alembic heads first (single-head invariant). Set down_revision to the printed head. Index occurred_at, verb, resource_type, project_id, actor_user_id.
acceptance_criteria: Migration applies on a fresh DB; model has no Text/free-String columns; single-head test still passes.

title: Retention: roll up + prune usage_events at 1 year
description: LOCKED DECISION: keep raw events 1 year, summarize older rows into a rollup table, then delete. A busy lab emits more usage rows than domain rows, so the append-only table needs bounded growth before it runs in anger.

title: CSV/JSONL admin export of usage_events (separate from PROV-O)
description: Follow record_exports.py mechanics for export, but keep usage telemetry OUT of the PROV-O lineage path. Lets the operator pull raw events into their own tooling.

title: Decision: keep egress local-only, or enable external sink via the swappable seam
description: Default is local-only Postgres (no phone-home, matches docs/mobile-graph-aware-image-draft-review.md:476-492). The record_usage_event seam keeps a LocalFileSink/OTLP/PostHog adapter as a config-only swap. Revisit only if the PI later wants prebuilt dashboards instead of SQL. Also fold in actor identity granularity (raw user_id vs per-instance salted hash) here.

title: record_usage_event() seam on BaseService (emit via run_after_commit)
description: The single shared emit point below HTTP+MCP+CLI. Add record_usage_event(verb, resource_type, resource_id, project_id, outcome, duration_ms) to services/base.py beside run_after_commit/run_after_rollback (base.py:105-114). Successful writes emit via run_after_commit so a telemetry insert can never roll back a domain write; rolled-back/failed attempts emit via run_after_rollback with outcome=error. Gate all emission behind the env flag. Keep the persistence target behind one indirection so an external sink is a future config swap.

title: Config flag LAB_TRACKER_USAGE_EVENTS (off locally, on for deployments)
description: Add the enable flag mirroring the auth posture in config.py: default OFF in local/dev, ON for real deployments. record_usage_event is a no-op when disabled.

title: Instrument ~15 service write methods with record_usage_event()
description: One line per write method: ProjectService.create_project, NoteService.upsert_note, GraphDraftService.submit/review/commit, and the rest of the create/update/delete/submit/review/commit methods. Capture verb + resource_type + real entity UUID + outcome + duration_ms. Re-emitting create events overlaps with created_at/created_by, which is acceptable redundancy but NOT the justification (those are already SQL-answerable).

title: Instrument search endpoint (act + result count, never terms)
description: Record that a search happened and the result count. NEVER record the query string. The one read-side signal worth capturing in Phase 1 because searches are structurally absent from the domain model.

title: CI guard: fail build on any content/free-text column in usage_events
description: A test that introspects UsageEventModel and fails if any column is Text or a free String outside the fixed enum/UUID/timestamp set. Makes the privacy red line structurally enforced, not just documented.

title: Surface attribution: X-LabTracker-Surface header (MCP + CLI) + middleware resolution
description: MCP and CLI re-enter the same FastAPI routes as httpx clients, so set X-LabTracker-Surface in mcp_api_client.py:808 and src/lab_tracker_client/client.py:176-220. Resolve the header in the existing auth/session middleware onto request.state and thread through ServiceContext so usage_events.surface distinguishes http/mcp/cli. Strictly additive over Phase 1.

title: Instrument reads/views on detail endpoints (which entities get looked at)
description: No accessed_at exists anywhere in the domain model, so which questions/projects/claims actually get viewed is unknowable today. Emit view events on detail endpoints. The headline product-usage signal.

title: Read-only admin GET /usage-events/summary endpoint
description: Counts by verb/resource_type/day for the operator. ADMIN-gated. Mirror the existing /metrics precedent at app_parts/observability.py:175-204. Deferred out of Phase 1 because the PI can query Postgres directly day one.

title: Pin Marion deployment base images by digest
description: The Marion application Dockerfile uses python:3.11-slim and Compose uses postgres:16-alpine, both mutable tags. The release image is pinned after build, but rebuilding the same source later can consume different base images.
design: Retain readable tag comments next to immutable digests and update through a controlled maintenance task. Do not silently auto-advance production bases.
acceptance_criteria: Application and Postgres base images are pinned to reviewed digests with a documented update procedure; backup/restore and release smoke remain green; dependency updates are intentional and reviewable.

title: Clarify and harden MCP note creation validation for status and metadata
description:
While recording the 2026-04-28 temporal-gradient projector titration analysis through the Lab Tracker MCP connector, `lab_tracker_create_note` accepted only a reduced payload after two confusing validation failures.

Observed behavior:
- Creating a note with `status="active"` failed, while the analogous question flow accepts `active`. This is technically consistent with `NoteStatus` (`staged`, `committed`, `archived`), but the MCP tool exposes `status` as a free string and the skill/API docs do not make the note-specific allowed values obvious.
- Creating a note with structured metadata failed unless all metadata values were strings. `NoteCreate.metadata` is typed as `dict[str, str]`, so Pydantic rejects non-string JSON values before the request reaches `_normalize_note_metadata`, even though the service normalizer is written to coerce non-string values to strings.
- The successful fallback was to create the note with `status="staged"` and no metadata, which avoided data loss but made the assistant workflow more brittle and less informative.

Concrete example context:
- Project: `b97935f1-42c6-475d-b35f-0e23607d11e6`
- Successful fallback note: `4dc2ec50-7781-475d-ba3d-b89c0c79895b`
- MCP tool: `lab_tracker_create_note`
- Relevant code paths noticed during triage: `src/lab_tracker/schemas.py` (`NoteCreate.metadata: dict[str, str]`, `status: NoteStatus | None`), `src/lab_tracker/mcp_server.py` (`lab_tracker_create_note(status: str | None, metadata: dict[str, str] | None)`), and `src/lab_tracker/services/shared.py` (`_normalize_note_metadata` coerces values).

Why this matters:
Assistant clients will naturally use project/question status vocabulary and structured provenance metadata. The current behavior requires hidden knowledge of note-specific status values and silently discourages preserving useful machine-readable provenance on notes.
acceptance_criteria:
- `lab_tracker_create_note` docs/schema expose the allowed note statuses (`staged`, `committed`, `archived`) clearly, or the MCP layer rejects invalid statuses with a targeted error before the generic API failure.
- Decide whether note metadata should accept JSON scalar values and normalize them, or remain string-only; make the API schema, service normalizer, MCP type hints, and docs agree.
- Add or update tests for MCP note creation covering invalid note status and metadata values with at least one non-string scalar.
- Update the Lab Tracker skill/docs so assistant clients know the note status vocabulary and metadata contract.
close_reason: Clarified note status validation and aligned scalar metadata handling across API, MCP, tests, docs, and installed skills.

title: [reliability] Harden the MCP-facing API + fail-soft error contract so a down server degrades gracefully
description:
Co-prerequisite for the rest of this epic, not a footnote. lab-tracker is HTTP-backed and is currently 502-ing. Salience without reliability is NEGATIVE: the activation work (instructions, hook) RAISES the agent's call rate against the endpoint, so a flaky backend means more 502s and faster abandonment — the opposite of the goal.

The consultation policy already mandates the right behavior ("If Lab Tracker is unavailable or ambiguous, state that explicitly") but the tools must make that easy: when the API is unreachable/5xx, MCP read tools should return a clear, structured "Lab Tracker unavailable — proceeding without graph context" signal rather than a raw error the model misreads as its OWN failure (which leads it to retry or route around the tool permanently).

Two parts: (1) investigate and fix the 502 (root-cause the API/MCP-client path; see src/lab_tracker/mcp_api_client.py); (2) define a fail-soft error contract across read tools (lab_tracker_health/readiness/get_decision_context/list_*/search) with a consistent unavailable shape and a one-line agent-facing message.
acceptance_criteria: When the API is down, every MCP read tool returns a consistent, documented "unavailable" result with an actionable message; the 502 root cause is fixed or has a tracked root-cause; an agent hitting a down server proceeds without graph context instead of treating it as a self-inflicted error.

title: Upgrade frontend test toolchain to resolve npm audit findings
description: npm audit reports 5 moderate vulnerabilities through vitest/vite/esbuild. The suggested npm audit fix requires a breaking update to esbuild 0.28.0, so this should be handled intentionally with frontend test and build verification.
close_reason: Updated frontend dev toolchain to vitest 4.1.5 and esbuild 0.28.0, rebuilt committed bundle, and verified npm audit reports zero vulnerabilities.

title: [bug] `lab-tracker serve` opens the browser before uvicorn is listening
description: Found during the 2026-06-16 re-review (minor polish on lab-tracker-7x77). serve_app() opens the browser (cli.py:69-77) before starting uvicorn, so on a cold start the browser shows a "can't connect" / connection-refused page until the user manually refreshes. For the non-technical persona this looks like the app is broken.
acceptance_criteria: The browser opens only after the server is accepting connections (readiness probe or post-startup hook), so the first page load succeeds without a manual refresh.

title: [medium] In-app first-run empty state, header rename, and navigation
description:
A first-time user lands cold in a dense multi-card dashboard (WorkspaceHome.jsx:29-189) with no onboarding, empty-state guidance, tour, help, or glossary (grep over frontend_src returns 0 real hits), no explanation of Question/Dataset/Claim/Graph-draft, and a header reading "Lab Tracker Frontend MVP" (shared/ui.jsx:111-114) with no navigation.

Add: a first-run empty state when projects.length === 0 ("Welcome — create your first project" with a primary action); rename the header to "Lab Tracker"; add basic nav (Home / Capture / Devices); add lightweight inline definitions or a help link for the core nouns. Keep it consistent with the retained-v1 surface.

Evidence: WorkspaceHome.jsx:29-189; shared/ui.jsx:111-114; audit barrier #7, #17; "In-app UX" dimension.
acceptance_criteria: A logged-in user with no projects sees a clear "create your first project" welcome; the header reads "Lab Tracker"; primary sections are reachable via visible navigation; core terms are explained or linked to help.

title: Add project-scoped graph collaboration
description: Implement project memberships, project-scoped access enforcement, PR-like graph change set submission/review, attribution, member management surfaces, and MCP/decision-context scoping for undergrad collaboration on project graphs.
acceptance_criteria: Project memberships gate read/write access by project. Contributors can add notes/evidence and submit graph change sets. Owners/admins can manage members and review/commit submitted graph change sets. Attribution is persisted and exposed. MCP/decision-context inherits authenticated user project scope. Backend and frontend tests cover collaboration and leakage prevention.

title: Canonicalize client auth env around LAB_TRACKER_TOKEN
description: Implement the auth configuration simplification plan: teach LAB_TRACKER_TOKEN as the canonical bearer token for non-browser clients while preserving LAB_TRACKER_ACCESS_TOKEN and LAB_TRACKER_MCP_* aliases, update LabTracker/MCP env resolution, figure capture compatibility, generated MCP scaffolding, docs, and regression tests. Do not redesign backend auth flows or token types.
notes: Implemented canonical non-browser auth env surface. Focused auth/init/MCP tests pass; uv run ruff check . passes. Full uv run pytest -q currently fails only tests/test_lab_tracker_skill_reference.py because separate in-progress bead lab-tracker-wc9v has unstaged /notes recent_first route changes without regenerated skill API reference.

title: PI-org backlog review follow-ups (2026-06-16)
description: Net-new findings from the adversarial multi-agent review of range 4c4954e..HEAD (PI-org backlog: groups, attribution, supervision, PROV-O, offboarding, goals; plus chv8 cloud-invites and kl8 MCP). Verdict: sound to keep on main - the §2.1 asymmetric group-access contract and the no-domain-column-on-users boundary are both correct, and no data-leak/authorization/boundary blocker exists. These are follow-ups, none a blocker.
notes: Source: review workflow 2026-06-16. The 769 epic is already closed; these are post-implementation follow-ups filed separately.

title: Offboarding guard and per-trainee export miss NULL-FK (legacy/local) records
description: After n1x7 switched the per-trainee filters to the attribution FK, the offboarding guard (_attributed_record_project_ids, project_service.py:543-558) and record export (_collect_records, record_export_service.py:104-129) resolve created_by on the FK only. For rows with a NULL FK - local/offline LOCAL_AUTH_USER_ID rows, or legacy non-UUID strings that 0028 leaves NULL - the records are invisible, so the guard returns an empty project set and membership revocation proceeds while the trainee work is stranded (the exact failure h4ag exists to prevent), and the leaver export is incomplete. Cloud path is healed by the 0028 backfill, so the gap is gated to self-hosted/LAN/offline rows (which chv8 explicitly supports).
design: Filter the guard/export record-discovery on the STRING column (created_by == str(user_id)), or OR both predicates (created_by_user_id == :id OR created_by == :id) in the repository query, reserving the FK-only switch for the public referential-trust list filters. Add a regression test with a NULL-FK record whose created_by string equals the trainee UUID, asserting the guard still blocks revocation. Also document FK-only semantics on the public created_by list filters (legacy non-UUID values now silently return zero rows).
notes: Encompasses the public-list-filter and guard-vs-reassign-predicate facets (same NULL-FK root cause). Relates h4ag, n1x7.

title: Portfolio summary groups projects after pagination - groups split across pages, meta.total mismatch
description: portfolio_summary (portfolio.py:67-71, commit sls 5a2bd43) paginates the flat visible-project list first, then groups only the current page. Projects are ordered by created_at (core.py:90), not group_id, so two projects in one group can land on different pages - the group emits as two PortfolioProjectGroupSummary rows with partial project_count each, unreassemblable by the client. Also meta.total counts PROJECTS while data holds GROUP summaries, so total no longer describes the returned collection. Not a leak (scoping applied before grouping; admin short-circuit preserved). The commit test bakes in the mismatch (meta.total==2 for 2 projects collapsing to 1 group).
design: Group BEFORE paginating: build all group summaries from the full visible_projects list, paginate the group list, set total = number of groups; or order projects by group_id so a group never straddles a page boundary and document that total counts projects. Correct the baked-in test assertion.
notes: Distinct from 4bk.7 (a naive SQL pushdown preserves this bug) and aai.8 (which asserts the endpoint is correct today - this refutes that).

title: Record export is a GET with a write side effect
description: GET /record-exports/users/{id} (and the group variant) unconditionally writes a RecordExportEvent on every call (record_export_service.py:38-70, export_id=uuid4(), no idempotency key), violating HTTP safe-method semantics - retry, double-click, cache/proxy revalidation, or prefetch each persists another audit row. Worse, the offboarding guard passes on the presence of any export event whose project_ids superset the attributed projects (no recency/intent filter), so an accidental/prefetched GET can silently satisfy the release guard. Requires an authenticated ADMIN (user variant) or group-owner (group variant), so not anonymous, but an admin browser retry/prefetch still triggers all three problems.
design: Make export a POST (it both returns a download and writes an audit row), or split a safe compute-only GET from an explicit recording POST. Ensure no prefetch path can hit the recording variant.
notes: Same class as 99x.5 (GET persisting state) on a different endpoint; net-new.

title: Bootstrap admin token printed to logs on every boot
description: docker-entrypoint.sh:55 (added by chv8 fe63767) echoes the LAB_TRACKER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_TOKEN value to stderr unconditionally on every boot, not only at generation - the two generation branches deliberately log only the file path. The token gates first-ADMIN self-registration (routes/auth.py:82-90, hmac.compare_digest) while has_users() is False; the value is constant across restarts and persists in log aggregation (Render), going live again on any disk-loss/empty-users reset while already sitting in historical logs.
design: Scope the echo into the generation else-branch and prefer pointing operators at the on-disk file (as the secret-key branch does), preserving the documented Render first-boot UX without re-leaking on every subsequent boot.
notes: Relates security epic zl9 (no existing child covers token-in-logs).

title: Invitation tokens are multi-use and username case mismatch mints duplicate accounts
description: Invitation HMAC tokens have no consumption record (verify_invitation_token checks only signature + expiry), so one invite link is reusable for its whole TTL (default 168h). register_auth validates the invitee via normalize_email (lowercased) but creates the account via _normalize_username (strip only, NO lowercase) with a case-sensitive uniqueness check, so Bob@Lab.edu and bob@lab.edu both pass the email check yet store as distinct same-role accounts (no ConflictError). Never escalates beyond the granted role; impact is account-table pollution plus a forwardable single-use-intended link.
design: Canonicalize usernames to lowercase so the email check and the uniqueness store agree, and record invite consumption (reject if a user already exists for the invited email).
notes: Relates chv8.

title: Document 0030 goal-nullable downgrade one-way semantics
description: alembic/versions/0030_nullable_goal_project.py downgrade() restores goals.project_id to nullable=False unconditionally; once projectless (spanning) goals exist it aborts mid-batch with a NOT NULL violation (reproduced on SQLite; Postgres ALTER SET NOT NULL fails equivalently). No downgrade round-trip test exists. Acceptable under the forward-only/revision-immutability policy, but a surprised operator mid-rollback is avoidable.
design: Document the one-way nature in the migration docstring, or have downgrade() first delete/reassign rows where project_id IS NULL or raise a clear actionable error.
notes: Distinct from cq5.7 (upgrade NOT-NULL drift in 0014-0024).

title: Make mobile capture feel like a message composer
description: Redesign the phone-first capture controls so the primary upload area resembles an iOS Messages composer: text box, plus affordance for photo/camera/file capture, and mic affordance for voice memo/audio upload while preserving existing photo, voice, bundle, text upload behavior.
design: Keep backend APIs unchanged. Reuse the existing captureMode/photoFile/audioFile/textNote state and uploadCapture behavior; only alter the primary mobile UI presentation and responsive CSS.
acceptance_criteria: Capture route puts a message-style composer before upload details. The plus control exposes photo, voice, bundle, and text options without shoving labels offscreen. Existing upload and draft flows for photo and photo+voice continue to pass tests. Built frontend bundle is refreshed.

title: Web-app easy button: mint LPAT + copyable agent-setup commands (tokens page)
description: Add a frontend page (plus any missing backend support) that lets a signed-in user mint a personal access token (lpat_...) and immediately get copy-paste commands to configure local agent config files: lt setup connect --save-token with the server base URL and token filled in, followed by lt setup init / lt project bind pointers. Complements guided-setup epic lab-tracker-stkn whose consent stance is 'PAT minting stays human-in-browser'. Today /auth/tokens has no UI at all; docs/agent-setup.md section 3 sends users to raw POST /auth/tokens. Include token list + revoke UI (mirror devices.jsx pattern).

title: Restore deployed MCP decision-context authentication and TLS guidance
description: After PR #201 deployment, the hosted MCP container starts healthy but its static LT_MCP_READONLY_TOKEN is rejected with 401 by the live Postgres-backed app. Public HTTPS negotiates successfully for /health and /assistant/decision-context, indicating reports of SSL negotiation failure likely use a wrong scheme/port or MCP URL. Restore a valid human-issued read-only LPAT, verify decision-context over internal and remote paths, and make operational diagnostics fail clearly.
acceptance_criteria: Hosted MCP startup auth probe succeeds with a live read-only LPAT; decision-context returns 200 through the intended client path; documented remote base URL uses the TLS-terminating origin without the raw HTTP app/MCP port; container health/diagnostics do not report success while every authenticated tool will fail.

title: Fix Windows SQLite backup test path using unsupported '?' filename
description: While validating lab-tracker-k69p on Windows, uv run pytest -q --no-cov --maxfail=1 stopped after 674 passes on 	ests/test_sqlite_backup.py::test_copy_sqlite_database_round_trips_path_with_special_characters. The test tries to create weird ? name #1.db; on this Windows filesystem sqlite3.connect raises OperationalError: unable to open database file before the backup code under test runs. Adjust the regression to cover URI delimiter escaping with characters that are legal on Windows, or make the POSIX-only filename variant conditional while keeping Windows coverage for drive-letter/as_uri behavior.

title: Group-aware access: asymmetric inheritance in authorization policy
description:
Make ProjectAuthorizationPolicy.accessible_project_ids() and membership_role() group-aware under the asymmetric privacy contract: a group OWNER inherits OWNER on every child project; group VIEWER/CONTRIBUTOR inherit nothing unless the per-group group_read_all flag is set. Direct project membership resolves first; the admin short-circuit is preserved verbatim.

Design: the single high-leverage edit, so all visibility consumers inherit group scoping through this one chokepoint. Never bypass the policy or use global ADMIN as the access mechanism for non-admins.

Depends on the group schema.

title: Isolate Python tests from deployment .env base URL settings
description: A local dedicated-instance .env defining LAB_TRACKER_PUBLIC_BASE_URL causes 16 otherwise unrelated Python tests to resolve the hosted canonical origin instead of their request/test origin; test_dedicated_instance_deployment also scans ignored local deployment material. This makes the full local suite non-hermetic even though clean GitHub Actions runners are unaffected. Existing beads lab-tracker-g7qo and lab-tracker-qyr2 cover only the database URL serve test, not these base-URL/provenance/export cases.
design: Give tests an explicit configuration boundary that cannot inherit repo-root deployment .env unless a test opts in. Keep deployment configuration tests able to exercise supplied settings without reading ignored operator secrets or private instance identifiers.
acceptance_criteria: The full Python suite passes with a repo-root .env containing a non-local LAB_TRACKER_PUBLIC_BASE_URL and ignored dedicated deployment files; provenance, export, invitation, opacity, and deployment-material tests remain deterministic.

title: Split divergent deployment branch into reviewable PRs
description: Reconcile codex/deploy-latest-20260728 with current origin/main without merging or rebasing the monolithic branch. Port only still-needed behavior into fresh functionally scoped branches, exclude superseded main changes and operational-only bookkeeping, preserve the deployed Marion revision's reachability, validate each slice independently, and open draft PRs with an explicit merge order.
design: Audit by subsystem: production graph-draft schema repair; invitation/onboarding/setup hardening; Marion deployment and backup operations. Base each branch on freshly fetched origin/main or on the preceding PR only where a real code dependency requires stacking. Keep Beads-only status updates out of functional diffs except the reconciliation task export. Prefer retaining original deployed commit reachability through the existing remote branch until a deliberate tag/merge decision resolves lab-tracker-pm85.
acceptance_criteria: Every unique functional change is classified as ported, already on main, operational-only, or intentionally deferred; each ported slice has focused checks plus applicable backend/frontend gates; fresh branches are pushed and draft PRs opened with clean diffs and documented dependencies; the original branch remains unchanged and remotely reachable; current worktree is clean at handoff.
notes: Opened draft PRs #179 deployment revision probe, #180 graph schema repair, #181 review-email capability gating, #182 invitation acceptance hardening, #184 secure client setup primitives, #187 guided source-pinned setup, and #188 sanitized dedicated-instance release workflow. PRs #179/#180 are green; #181/#187/#188 are running after clean follow-up commits; #182 and #184 each have one diagnosed fixture-only CI failure awaiting the explicit approval required by the CI-fix workflow. Deferred unsafe lease/starter drafting to lab-tracker-4b61 and Windows workflow coverage to lab-tracker-pfqn. Original divergent branch remains unchanged and remotely reachable.

title: Recent notes and graph UI cleanup
description: Implement newest-first Recent Notes, inline expansion for long note text, compact non-overlapping project graph nodes, and managed visualization figure thumbnails in graph nodes. Requested from the planned Recent Notes And Graph UI Cleanup work.
acceptance_criteria: Recent Notes loads newest notes first, wraps/clamps long content, and expands inline; Project Graph uses compact nodes and image thumbnails for managed visualization assets; focused backend/frontend tests and quality gates pass.
notes: While landing lab-tracker-v96n, full uv run pytest -q failed only the generated skill-reference checks because the /notes recent_first route change is present without regenerating skills/lab-tracker/SKILL.md's API reference. Regenerate/check that section before closing this bead.

title: [activation] Action-shaped tool outputs: append a structured suggested-next-action to results
description:
Beads raises follow-through by returning outputs that prompt the next move. lab-tracker tools currently return data with no nudge. Add a structured (not prose) suggested-next-action field to tool results, e.g. after `lab_tracker_create_claim` -> "link this claim to a goal via lab_tracker_link_node_to_goal"; after `create_dataset` -> "record the analysis that used it via create_analysis"; after `get_decision_context` -> point at the highest-signal next question (ties into the ready-work tool).

Keep it a structured field so it nudges without bloating the payload, and keep suggestions truthful to the retained-v1 create ordering (datasets -> analyses -> claims/visualizations).
acceptance_criteria: Key write/read tools return a structured next_action hint that reflects the real graph workflow; payloads stay compact; suggestions are consistent with retained-v1 ordering.

title: Make watch-folder setup suggest narrow, low-noise capture roots
description: From the BilateralOdorFlowRl setup on 2026-07-06: after scaffolding and binding, setup status correctly suggested lt watch add <folder>, but this repo's artifacts/ tree is huge and noisy. Improve setup status or the setup guide to detect candidate output roots and recommend narrow watch entries, include/exclude globs, or explicitly say 'skip watch for now; commit snapshots are active' when a repo already has hooks but no safe narrow root.

title: GitHub Copilot MCP support (human IDEs, read-only remote)
description: Make Lab Tracker's MCP server usable from GitHub Copilot in human-driven IDEs (VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains/Eclipse/Xcode). Scope decisions: (1) human IDEs only — the autonomous github.com coding agent is OUT of scope, so no public exposure/Funnel/coding-agent config; (2) all remote/hosted surfaces are READ-ONLY — writes only via local stdio or the app UI, so no token forwarding is needed. Full design: docs/copilot-mcp-support-design.md.

title: P0a: Local Copilot IDE onboarding (config + docs)
description: Make the MCP server usable from GitHub Copilot IDEs over stdio. Add .vscode/mcp.json (top-level 'servers' + 'inputs' prompted secret; lt-mcp command, with a uvx --from git+<repo> fallback instead of PYTHONPATH=src). Add a Visual Studio-shaped repo-root config (same 'servers' schema; note collision with the Claude/Codex .mcp.json which uses 'mcpServers'). Reconcile committed .mcp.json with cli.py::_mcp_json(). Add a short instructions= string to FastMCP(...) carrying 'decision-context first' and 'only a person commits'. Add docs/lab-tracker-copilot.md user doc + a README 'Capture and integrate' pointer. No migration; lowest risk; do first. Design: docs/copilot-mcp-support-design.md (B1, P0a).

title: P0b: MCP tool annotations (read auto-run, write prompt)
description: Drive MCP tool annotations from a per-tool table in register_*_tools (from mcp.types import ToolAnnotations). Read tools: readOnlyHint=True, openWorldHint=True, title — so Copilot/VS Code skips the confirmation dialog. Write tools: leave readOnlyHint false so the IDE prompts; destructiveHint on refactor_question/update_goal; front-load record_evidence_bundle docstring with 'defaults to dry-run; pass dry_run=false to write'. Reclassify list_question_refactors as read-only (currently in WRITE_TOOLS but performs no write). No migration. Design: docs/copilot-mcp-support-design.md (B1).

title: P0c: lpat_ personal access token + client API key + log hygiene
description: Add a per-user lpat_ personal access token, mirroring DeviceAuthService: new personal_access_tokens table (token_hash sha256 only, capped role, read_only default True, REQUIRED expires_at with max TTL), PrincipalType.SERVICE, PersonalAccessTokenService (issue once / verify uncached / revoke), service_principal_can_access policy (read all except /auth; writes denied if read_only else role-gated), a new auth_middleware 'elif lpat_' branch that uses the token's CAPPED role (NOT user.role), /auth/tokens issue/list/revoke router with a dedicated fail-closed throttle on lpat_ 401/403. MCP client: add LAB_TRACKER_MCP_API_KEY (send as Bearer, skip /auth/login). Log hygiene: redact lpat_/Bearer substrings from lab_tracker_api_error/Unavailable error strings before they reach tool output. Add a startup/doctor guard refusing to start the MCP service against an auth-disabled hop-2 target. ONE additive Alembic migration (alembic heads must be 1; rebase down_revision at merge; test_alembic_has_single_head post-merge). Test gates listed in design. Unlocks password-free per-user stdio auth and the read-only token for the hosted endpoint. Design: docs/copilot-mcp-support-design.md (B2, B3, P0c).

title: P1: HTTP transport + private read-only hosted MCP endpoint (optional)
description: OPTIONAL — only if a shared hosted read-only endpoint is wanted (Mode 2). Make mcp_server.py main() read LAB_TRACKER_MCP_TRANSPORT (default stdio) | streamable-http, plus HOST (default 127.0.0.1 loopback)/PORT/PATH; construct FastMCP(stateless_http=True, json_response=True) for the hosted endpoint; keep the server standalone (do not mount under FastAPI). Add a loopback-bound compose 'mcp' service pointed at app:8000 with a read-only lpat_ in LAB_TRACKER_MCP_API_KEY. Add a Caddyfile that terminates TLS, validates Origin/Host (placeholder allowlist — confirm Copilot's real Origin against live logs), strips Authorization from logs, sets no permissive CORS. Expose tailnet-private only (no public Funnel — coding agent is out of scope). READ-ONLY only. No migration. Test gates: boots streamable-http on loopback; reverse-proxy Origin 403; hosted lpat_ cannot write; doctor refuses an auth-off hop-2 target. Design: docs/copilot-mcp-support-design.md (B4, P1).

Detect waiting/controlling service workers on startup and update discovery, let the user reload deliberately, and ensure the prompt does not appear on first install. Cover registration states and UI behavior with frontend tests.
