title: Make clean-machine agent setup install the matching client, Python package, skills, hooks, and MCP
description: Replace the moving GitHub-main setup with a pinned compatible artifact. Ensure Codex and Claude skill homes, a writable staging PAT for commit capture, project-environment lab_tracker_client installation, repository bind, hook sync, Codex MCP launch, and verification are all explicit and tested.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh machine/repo can follow setup to obtain matching lt/lt-mcp, import lab_tracker_client in the project environment, install both supported skills, bind the exact project, sync a hook-generated staged note using least-privilege write credentials, and complete a real MCP health check.

title: De-clutter the project graph view
description: User feedback (2026-07): people actually looking at the knowledge graph find the visuals cluttered/overwhelming. Diagnosis (multi-agent code review, 2026-07-05): the view has one presentation state — everything at full detail, nothing on demand. Root causes: (1) unbounded node labels (questions untruncated) in fixed 220px boxes overlap vertically; (2) prose labels rendered on every edge; (3) no selection/filter/search — elementsSelectable=false, click navigates away, node detail/status fetched but never shown, legend not clickable; (4) mean-of-sources column layout creates long crossing edges and a ~2,400px-wide Full view that fitView shrinks to illegibility; (5) screen chrome: Dashboard card renders next to the graph (two project pickers), duplicated axis+legend rows (~26 pills). All fixes are presentation-only; retained-v1 surface untouched. Children are ranked by impact-per-effort.
notes:
Main files: src/lab_tracker/frontend_src/features/project-graph.jsx, src/lab_tracker/project_graph.py, src/lab_tracker/frontend_src/app-shell.jsx. Verify visually via static demo mode (?demo=1) or hosted GitHub Pages demo — no DB needed. Related but distinct: lab-tracker-83m2.14 (graph theming + phone outline under design-system epic) — coordinate, don't conflate. Full diagnosis in session 024b86b8 workflow kg-clutter-diagnosis.
2026-07-05: Active tier (.1-.7) implemented, reviewed, and closed. Remaining: .8 (dagre layout) and .9 (backend center/depth) stay deferred (P4) — do only if the presentation-tier changes prove insufficient at scale. Epic stays open to track those.

title: Clamp graph node labels; truncate question labels server-side
description: Node labels are up to 180 chars and question text is sent completely unbounded (_question_label at src/lab_tracker/project_graph.py:244 bypasses _truncate_graph_label). Labels wrap in fixed 220px boxes with no height bound, so any node taller than ROW_HEIGHT=118 physically overlaps the node below — the collision loop (project-graph.jsx:258-260) spaces y-centers by 0.75*ROW_HEIGHT, not rendered heights. Fix: (a) 3-line CSS line-clamp in graphNodeToFlowNode (project-graph.jsx:269-294) with full text available on hover (title attr) until the detail panel exists; (b) route _question_label through _truncate_graph_label; consider lowering _GRAPH_LABEL_LIMIT 180→~100 (180 chars = 6-8 wrapped lines at 220px).
acceptance_criteria: No node renders taller than row spacing regardless of label length; full label text reachable on hover; question labels truncated server-side; existing layout tests pass.

title: Show graph edge labels on demand only; de-emphasize edge styling
description: graphEdgeToFlowEdge (project-graph.jsx:296-309) passes label: edge.label unconditionally, so every 'supports'/'used by' string tiles the canvas; edges also get full-contrast 22x22 arrowheads, giving them the same visual weight as nodes. Fix: stop rendering labels by default (keep string in edge.data; show on edge hover and, once selection lands, for edges incident to the selected node); lighten stroke (#9aa3ad → lighter) and shrink arrowheads (~14px); add the missing legend entry explaining dashed = candidate edges (currently applied at :297,307 with no key anywhere). Optional 'Edge labels' checkbox to restore always-on.
acceptance_criteria: Default canvas renders no edge label text; labels appear on hover; dashed-candidate encoding explained in legend; Mermaid export unchanged.

title: Clickable legend chips as per-type graph filters; hide notes/sessions by default in Full view
description: The legend (project-graph.jsx:560-576) already enumerates one chip per entity type with a live count but is display-only. Turn chips into toggles backed by a hiddenTypes Set; filter graph.nodes/edges BEFORE buildFlowGraph (memo at :420) so surviving columns re-flow compactly via computeNodePositions. In Full view seed note+session as hidden (every note and session in the project is a first-class node per project_graph.py:88-90) with dimmed chips still showing counts. Reset hiddenTypes on view change. Add unit test in project-graph.test.jsx: hidden types and incident edges absent, remaining columns re-stack from y=0.
acceptance_criteria: Each legend chip toggles its type; Full view opens with notes/sessions hidden but counts visible; layout re-flows without holes; test added.

title: Merge graph axis strip + legend into one guide row; color MiniMap by type
description: Header chrome duplicates the same up-to-9-type list twice — axis pills with arrows (project-graph.jsx:542-559) and legend swatches with counts (:560-576) — ~26 pills before the canvas. Merge into a single ordered strip (swatch + label + count, separated by the existing arrows; legendTypesForView at :342-348 already yields the ordered list). Replace bare <MiniMap /> (:592) with nodeColor from TYPE_STYLES so the minimap stops being a monochrome blob on large graphs.
acceptance_criteria: One guide row instead of two; minimap shows type colors.

title: Select-to-inspect: in-place node detail panel instead of navigate-away
description: elementsSelectable=false and onNodeClick immediately navigates to node.data.route (project-graph.jsx:585-590), so the canvas is the only place information can live — node.data.detail and .status are fetched and packed (:277-283) but never displayed anywhere. Fix: flip elementsSelectable to true; onNodeClick sets selectedNodeId; render a side panel beside .project-graph-canvas showing full label, detail, status, entity-type chip, and an explicit 'Open {type}' button performing the old navigation. Update the App.test.jsx graph-route navigation test to click the panel button.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a node opens an in-page panel with full label/detail/status; navigation only via explicit button; tests updated.

title: Neighborhood focus: dim non-adjacent graph nodes/edges on selection
description: Builds on select-to-inspect. Compute 1-hop adjacency from graph.edges in a useMemo; when a node is selected, drop non-neighbors and non-incident edges to ~0.15 opacity via node/edge style, and show edge prose labels only for incident edges. onPaneClick clears selection. Makes the selected chain (question→dataset→analysis→claim) pop without layout changes — mitigates the long diagonal crossing edges caused by mean-of-sources y-anchoring (project-graph.jsx:249-251). Follow-up option: 'Focus' button for a k-hop ego re-layout with ?focus= URL param + breadcrumb, reusing the ?view= replaceState pattern (:374-383).
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a node dims everything outside its 1-hop neighborhood; incident edges show labels; background click restores.

title: Stop rendering Dashboard card alongside the project graph route
description: app-shell.jsx renders <Dashboard> on every non-home route (isHomeRoute else-branch, app-shell.jsx:385-387), so the graph screen stacks the New Project form, Project Members management, and a second project picker (dashboard-projects.jsx:54 duplicates the graph's own 'Active project' select at project-graph.jsx:503-513) next to the canvas. Decide the pattern (hide Dashboard on /app/graph, or collapse it) and apply; check the same doubling on draft-review routes (app-shell.jsx:462-487) while there. PendingBatchBanner also renders on every route — consider whether it belongs on the graph screen.
acceptance_criteria: Graph route shows one project picker and no New Project/member-management forms; no regression on other routes.

title: Replace mean-of-sources graph layout with rank-aware dagre (deferred)
description: computeNodePositions (project-graph.jsx:199-267) anchors nodes at the MEAN y of upstream sources (:249-251) — sources at rows 0 and 20 put the node at row 10, creating long diagonals across unrelated rows — and the collision loop only pushes DOWN, so dense columns become one tall stack that defeats fitView. Swap evidence/full placement for @dagrejs/dagre rankdir=LR with entity-type layer as rank constraint, feeding actual clamped node heights (hence dependency on label clamp). Keep computeQuestionLayout for the questions view (genuine tidy tree, directly unit-tested). Requires rewriting the exact-coordinate assertions in project-graph.test.jsx:27-175. Deferred: do after the styling/filtering tier lands and only if still needed.
acceptance_criteria: Fewer edge crossings on evidence/full views; entity-type column order preserved; questions view unchanged; tests rewritten.

title: Optional center/depth params on graph endpoint for very large projects (deferred)
description: build_project_graph loads every entity with limit=None (src/lab_tracker/project_graph.py:58-90) — fine for client-side ego filtering at current scales, but huge projects pay full fetch/layout cost before focusing. Add optional center + depth query params to GET /projects/{id}/graph (routes/project_graph.py:21-44, ProjectGraphView schema) pruning the built graph to a k-hop neighborhood post-build; share with the Mermaid sibling endpoint. Additive to the retained-v1 surface (defaults preserve whole-graph behavior). Defer until a real project demonstrably outgrows client-side filtering; depends on the client focus mode proving the interaction.
acceptance_criteria: center/depth params prune server-side with whole-graph default; frontend ?focus= uses them above a node-count threshold.

title: [quick-win] Set GitHub repo description + homepageUrl for wet-lab discoverability

title: Auto-hydrate data stores during setup (wire the shipped store registry into guided setup)
description: The DataStore registry is shipped (models 0049/0050, POST/GET /data-stores + /health, store:// resolution via local_fs + rclone/OneDrive adapters in artifact_resolution.py, lab_tracker_resolve_artifact MCP read tool) BUT it is orphaned from the guided-setup flow (docs/guided-setup-and-auto-tracking-design.md, src/lab_tracker/setup_guide.py). Guided setup wires watch folders + git hooks; nothing discovers or registers the user's actual stores (OneDrive/GDrive/S3). Consequence for a real trial: the OneDrive story (register once, then address every .fcs/xlsx/Word doc as store://lab-onedrive/... + content_hash, resolvable+hash-verified by an agent) requires a raw POST /data-stores — no web UI, no CLI verb, no setup discovery. Goal: when a scientist starts Lab Tracker, it is readily/automatically hydrated by the software+tools she already uses, so her graph is pre-wired to her stores with minimal friction. Respect the locked consent architecture: setup stays on consent-gated lt CLI verbs (MCP setup tools were explicitly rejected in the guided-setup design) + an optional web pane; agent-led path elicits 'where does your data live' and registers the default store with a --dry-run diff the human approves.
design: Mirror lt watch add. Detection scans for synced cloud folders (OneDrive: %OneDrive%, ~/OneDrive, ~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-*; GDrive ~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-*) and existing rclone remotes (rclone listremotes), proposes them as local_fs or rclone DataStore registrations, runs check_store_health, sets one default. Endgame: once a default store exists, capture clients write store://<default>/... locators + hashes automatically so everything captured is already portable + verifiable.
acceptance_criteria: A new user can go from zero to a registered, health-checked default store for their OneDrive without hand-writing a POST body or editing JSON; setup status reports store presence + suggests detected stores; the two experiment docs describe store:// as the OneDrive mechanism.
notes: MULTI-HOST: setup spans a fleet (her laptop, instrument/experiment PCs, shared core-facility PC), NOT just the server. The server holds shared store DEFINITIONS + the graph; each host binds its own access (credentials, synced-folder path OR rclone remote), watch folders, and hooks. Setup verbs already write per-host config (~/.lab-tracker/config.json, repo-local watch.json, per-repo hooks) and health-checks are 'from this host', so hydration must run per-host and confirm THIS host's reachability — never assume one machine. Hosts that can't be set up (shared core PC) need zero local setup: they upload to a store another host can reach + hash. Per-host binding of a shared local_fs store is tracked in lab-tracker-iquh.

title: Clamp effective figure capture timeout for supplied clients
description: The capture-specific 2-3s timeout applies only to auto-created clients; savefig/capture_figures with a caller-supplied LabTracker client can keep the default 15s timeout. Add an effective per-capture timeout path and tests that assert the wire timeout is clamped.

title: Add noncommercial license and citation metadata
description: Add repository licensing that prohibits commercial reuse and provides required citation metadata for Lab Tracker.

title: [activation] Conditional, fail-soft research-facing prime hook + managed CLAUDE.md block
description:
The dynamic half of the two-layer onboarding. The static block already exists in AGENTS.md:28-43, but nothing fires a dynamic prime, and there is no managed CLAUDE.md block (the only session hook runs `bd prime` for Beads).

CRITICAL: do NOT copy Beads' unconditional SessionStart prime. Beads' prime is local and instant; a lab-tracker prime is an HTTP call to a server that can be down (see the 502 in lab-tracker-<reliability issue>). A SessionStart hook that blocks/errors on a down endpoint EVERY session is worse than no hook — it teaches the agent and annoys the user into ignoring lab-tracker.

Design: a CONDITIONAL, FAIL-SOFT prime — prefer a UserPromptSubmit-style hook that fires only when the prompt looks research-facing (matching the consultation policy's own trigger list), calls a lightweight prime (active goals + open questions for the current project), times out fast, and emits nothing on failure. Plus a sentinel-delimited managed block in CLAUDE.md (an `lt`/setup command that injects it, idempotently, like Beads' init) carrying the same trigger-defined consult guidance.

Depends on the reliability/error-contract work so the prime can fail silently with a clean contract.
design: Implement a conditional hook (UserPromptSubmit or equivalent) with a short timeout and no output on error; add an idempotent injector for a sentinel-delimited managed CLAUDE.md block sourced from the same policy constant. Avoid networked SessionStart.
acceptance_criteria: In a research-facing prompt, the agent receives a fresh, lightweight prime (active goals + open questions) without a blocking/erroring call; on a down API the hook emits nothing and never surfaces an error; a managed CLAUDE.md block is injected idempotently via a command.

title: Epic: Lab Tracker consumer integration toolkit
description:
Coordinate the Lab Tracker consumer integration toolkit so downstream repos can capture project/question/note context without each repo maintaining brittle scripts, MCP config, and skill prose.

Filed from the LiteratureEmbeddings repo after back-filling Lab Tracker integration end-to-end on 2026-05-26/27. A consumer repo that wants to track work in Lab Tracker currently has to reinvent four pieces of plumbing: HTTP client, idempotent upsert pattern, MCP wiring, and API-shape guidance generated by reading /openapi.json. The current external lab-tracker skill prose has drifted from the live API, e.g. it describes question fields/enums such as title/broad/atomic while the API expects text and descriptive | hypothesis_driven | method_dev | other.

Concrete v0 consumer artifacts live in C:/Users/snb6/Documents/GitHub/LiteratureEmbeddings/: scripts/lt.py (~250 lines of HTTP client/idempotency/CLI), scripts/lt_bootstrap.py, scripts/lt_note_*.py, .mcp.json, the Lab Tracker integration section of AGENTS.md, and memory/lt-api-quirks.md in the user's Claude project memory. Those artifacts should become either generated scaffolding or thin callers of Lab Tracker-owned code.

Out of scope: retained-v1 API changes, Dolt mirror changes, and Postgres deployment changes. This is developer-experience and packaging work around how consumers reach the existing API.
design: Track the implementation as focused child beads in priority order: ship the Python client first, own/generated skill docs second, scaffolding third, and portable MCP config as a required support path. Keep downstream consumer scripts thin: scripts/lt.py should become a one-line re-export once lab_tracker_client exists. Do not mutate Lab Tracker research records as part of this work.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads cover lab_tracker_client, repo-owned/generated skill docs, lab_tracker init scaffolding, and portable MCP configuration. Dependencies capture that the init scaffolder needs the client package and portable MCP entrypoint. Each implementation bead references the LiteratureEmbeddings v0 artifacts and defines tests/compatibility expectations for downstream consumer repos.

title: Package lab_tracker_client consumer helpers
description:
Add a supported Python consumer package named lab_tracker_client, or a clearly supported vendored single-file client under clients/python, so downstream repos can import Lab Tracker helpers instead of copying scripts/lt.py.

Minimum public surface: LabTracker client class, EntityRef helper, upsert_project, upsert_question, upsert_note, quick_capture, and list_* helpers for retained-v1 entities needed by consumer repos. This package should replace the ~250-line LiteratureEmbeddings scripts/lt.py HTTP client/idempotency/CLI implementation.
design:
Prefer a small public API backed by HTTP calls to the existing Lab Tracker API. Keep auth/base-url configuration explicit and environment-friendly. Implement canonical idempotency keys: project by name, question by text within project, note by first non-blank line marker. Match the live OpenAPI enum values, and raise a typed LTValidationError or equivalent on bad enum values so consumers do not maintain shadow enum sets.

Include a compatibility shim pattern so a consumer repo scripts/lt.py can collapse to a one-line re-export from lab_tracker_client. Consider an lt console entrypoint for health, ids, note, quick, list-questions, and list-notes commands if it fits the packaging surface.
acceptance_criteria: lab_tracker_client is importable from this package or from clients/python. It exposes LabTracker, EntityRef, upsert_project, upsert_question, upsert_note, quick_capture, and list_* helpers. Idempotency by project name, question text, and note first-line marker is implemented and tested. Bad enum values fail client-side with a typed error informed by the OpenAPI schema or generated constants. A consumer scripts/lt.py can re-export the client helpers without duplicating logic. Backend tests and ruff pass.

title: Make Lab Tracker MCP config portable
description:
Make Lab Tracker MCP configuration portable for consumer repos. The working v0 .mcp.json in LiteratureEmbeddings used a hardcoded absolute path to the lab-tracker .venv Python executable, which breaks across machines and clones.

Consumers need a canonical .mcp.json snippet that does not require per-machine editing.
design: Support one or both portable launch paths: an environment-variable based command such as ${LAB_TRACKER_PYTHON:-python}, or an installed lt-mcp console entrypoint that imports/runs the existing MCP server. The MCP server must remain API-backed and must not write directly to the database. Preserve python -m lab_tracker.mcp_server as a compatibility path.
acceptance_criteria: A portable MCP launch path exists and is documented. .mcp.json examples/templates no longer require hardcoded absolute Python interpreter or repo paths. python -m lab_tracker.mcp_server remains supported. Existing MCP tests pass. The lab_tracker init scaffolder can emit a generated .mcp.json that works after normal package installation or with a documented LAB_TRACKER_PYTHON/LAB_TRACKER_VENV environment variable.

title: Add lab_tracker init consumer scaffolder
description:
Add an lt setup or lab_tracker init command that scaffolds Lab Tracker integration files into any consumer repository in one step.

The LiteratureEmbeddings setup required hand-written scripts/lt.py, .mcp.json, AGENTS.md Lab Tracker guidance, and lt_ids-style state. New consumers should start with those files generated from Lab Tracker-owned templates.
design:
Implement a console entrypoint, e.g. lab_tracker init [--target REPO_PATH] [--project-name ...]. Generate .mcp.json using the portable MCP launch path, scripts/lt.py as a thin re-export from lab_tracker_client, AGENTS.lt.md or an AGENTS.md fragment documenting the three-mechanism decision tree, and lt_ids.json as a placeholder or project-name-driven bootstrap output.

Keep scaffolding idempotent: do not overwrite local changes without an explicit force flag, and report created/skipped files. The AGENTS fragment should distinguish MCP for lightweight reads, script/client upserts for substantive notes, and CLI for terminal scratch work, and it should document the canonical first-line-marker idempotency pattern.
acceptance_criteria: mkdir new-project; cd new-project; lab_tracker init produces a repo state with portable .mcp.json, scripts/lt.py, AGENTS.lt.md or AGENTS fragment, and lt_ids.json. python -m scripts.lt health succeeds when Lab Tracker is reachable and configured. Generated files use lab_tracker_client and portable lt-mcp/LAB_TRACKER_PYTHON wiring rather than absolute local paths. The command is idempotent and has tests for create, already-exists, and force/overwrite behavior. Backend tests and ruff pass.

title: Move lab-tracker skill into repo with generated API reference
description:
Move the lab-tracker Codex skill into the lab-tracker repo so runtime and agent guidance version together, and generate the API-fields/enums section from OpenAPI so it cannot drift.

Current pain: external skill prose has described question payloads as title/broad/atomic while the live API requires text and one of descriptive | hypothesis_driven | method_dev | other. It has also missed live validation constraints such as pagination limit 200, causing agents to discover schema mismatches by failed POSTs in each new consumer repo.
design:
Store the skill source at skills/lab-tracker/SKILL.md or another repo-owned path with a clearly marked generated section. Add a generator/check that reads the live OpenAPI schema, preferably via create_app().openapi() in-process so CI does not require a running server, and rewrites or validates the API field names/enums section. Keep narrative workflow guidance human-editable while deriving schema-specific field names, enum values, and constraints from OpenAPI.

Publishing/syncing to Sam's local skills directory or other skill-distribution mechanism can be handled by the implementation if appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: The lab-tracker skill source lives in this repo. API field/enums guidance is generated from OpenAPI rather than handwritten and includes current retained-v1 field names, enum values, and important constraints for projects, questions, notes, sessions, datasets, analyses, claims, visualizations, graph drafts, and pagination where relevant. A CI-friendly test/check fails if the generated section drifts from OpenAPI. Updating a Pydantic schema or enum causes the next skill generation/check to surface the new field/enum without a manual prose edit. Backend gates pass.

title: One-tap phone pairing: QR + auto-submit + reachable URLs
description:
The pairing flow shipped under lab-tracker-bbd works but has three manual steps that defeat the 'no friction' goal: the enrollment URL contains the laptop's origin (often 127.0.0.1, not phone-reachable), there's no QR code so the user has to ferry the URL manually, and the phone shows a label form before pairing.

This bead replaces all three with: server renders a phone-reachable enrollment URL (resolved from request.base_url, overridable via LAB_TRACKER_PUBLIC_BASE_URL); the enrollment response includes an inline-SVG QR code of that URL; the DevicesPage shows the QR prominently next to the copy-URL fallback; the EnrollPage auto-submits with a User-Agent-derived label as soon as it loads, so scanning the QR ends in 'paired and in capture' with one tap.
design: Use segno for QR rendering (pure-Python, SVG-native, no Pillow dep). Determine base URL preference order: explicit setting, then request.base_url, then a hostname warning. EnrollPage keeps a manual override path (?label=foo) so the user can pair multiple phones distinguishably if needed, but defaults to UA-derived label.
acceptance_criteria:
- /auth/devices/enrollment returns enrollment_url that points to the request's external host, not 127.0.0.1
- LAB_TRACKER_PUBLIC_BASE_URL setting overrides the derived host (for tunnels, prod)
- Response includes enrollment_qr_svg containing valid SVG QR encoding the enrollment URL
- DevicesPage renders the QR inline; copy-URL is the fallback
- EnrollPage auto-submits on load, no label form required, label sourced from User-Agent
- End-to-end smoke: scan QR on iPhone Camera, tap pop-up, lands at /app/capture as paired device with no further taps

title: Guide users to persist the right Lab Tracker base URL before scaffolding MCP configs
description: From the BilateralOdorFlowRl setup on 2026-07-06: setup init scaffolded .mcp.json/.cursor/mcp.json/.gemini/settings.json with http://127.0.0.1:8000 even though this workstation also serves the same instance through the durable Tailscale Funnel URL. setup status reported profile.present=false but did not suggest lt setup connect. Improve setup status/init so users are nudged to persist the intended local-vs-HTTPS base URL before committing repo MCP configs, and make the scaffold source explicit.

title: Test HPC sync dedup (duplicate) and already_synced idempotency paths
description: _sync_event builds an EvidenceNoteIndex on (provider, external_id, content_hash) and returns skipped/duplicate on a server match (hpc.py:757-791); sync_outbox skips terminal already_synced events (586-600). Every HPC test stubs GET /notes empty (tests/test_hpc_client.py:106-209) so neither branch ever runs -> the project's flagged duplicate-graph-node hazard is uncovered. Add: (a) GET /notes returns a note matching the event metadata -> assert skipped/duplicate, no upload, event marked synced with the existing note_id; (b) run sync_outbox twice -> second pass already_synced, zero HTTP writes; (c) first attempt persists server-side then client sees 5xx, retry's GET /notes returns the match -> dedup.
acceptance_criteria: Tests exercise the duplicate and already_synced branches and a persisted-then-failed retry; all assert zero duplicate uploads.

title: Web UI gates project write actions on global role, ignoring project membership
description: Trainee 'josh' (global role viewer, project-contributor on one project) could not write in the web app despite the backend allowing it. Root cause: src/lab_tracker/frontend_src/hooks/useAuthSession.js:75 defines auth.canWrite = (role === 'admin' || 'editor') — a GLOBAL check. app-shell.jsx wires most write surfaces (Dashboard ~188-266, DevicesPage:392, QuestionDetailCard:443, SessionDetailCard:496) to auth.canWrite, so a global viewer is blocked everywhere regardless of project-contributor membership. Only mobile-capture(341), note-detail(456), graph-drafts(467/480) correctly use canContributeToProject (membership-based, app-shell.jsx:117). Backend authorization is membership-based and correct (project_authorization.require_contributor); has_global_read/write are admin-only, so this is purely a UI gating inconsistency. Workaround applied 2026-06-24: raised josh to global 'editor' (which also lets him create projects — undesired). Fix: gate project-scoped write surfaces on project membership (canContributeToProject), reserve global auth.canWrite for genuinely global operations; then trainees can stay global viewer.
acceptance_criteria: A user with global role 'viewer' and a project-contributor membership can initiate writes on all project-scoped surfaces (dashboard items, question/session detail) for that project in the web UI; global-only actions (e.g., create project, manage users) remain gated on global role. After the fix, josh can be reverted to global viewer.

title: [quick-win] Embed existing screenshots in README so the product is previewable
description:
11 screenshots already exist under docs/screenshots/*.png but none are linked from README.md (grep for `![`/`screenshot` in README returns nothing). A PI cannot see what the product looks like without a full build, which is the single cheapest way to let them evaluate.

Embed the most representative screenshots (e.g. project graph, capture/draft-review) into the "What it does" and draft-review sections of README.md. Confirm the chosen images reflect the current retained-v1 UI before linking.

Evidence: docs/screenshots/*.png present and unreferenced; audit barrier #16; PI-evaluator persona had nothing to look at.
acceptance_criteria: README shows at least 2-3 current screenshots inline so a reader can preview the product without building it. Images verified to match the shipping UI.

title: Make SQLite backup URI tests portable on Windows
description: Full pytest on Windows failed in tests/test_sqlite_backup.py after the latest upstream backup changes. One test creates a SQLite filename containing '?', which is not legal on Windows, and another builds a POSIX path with Windows Path('/var/...'), whose as_uri() is not drive-absolute on Windows. Adjust the tests to exercise URI escaping with cross-platform legal names and PurePosixPath for POSIX URI expectations.

title: Google/Gemini graph draft client implementation
description:
Sibling to the OpenAI implementation. Implement GraphDraftClient (defined in lab-tracker-641) against the Gemini generateContent API for both draft_from_note and draft_from_batch. Wire it into make_graph_draft_client when graph_draft_provider='google'.

Gemini supports inline audio input; transcribe_audio can be implemented natively rather than delegated.
acceptance_criteria:
- GoogleGraphDraftClient implements GraphDraftClient (draft_from_note, draft_from_batch, transcribe_audio)
- make_graph_draft_client returns it when settings.graph_draft_provider='google'
- Settings include google_api_key, google_model, google_base_url, google_timeout_seconds
- Tests mock the Gemini API and cover success, error response, and provider switching via factory

title: [medium] Make `docker compose up app` work out-of-the-box (auto-generate secret + bootstrap token)
description:
The Docker path is the only reboot-surviving option (`restart: unless-stopped`, docker-compose.yml:21,43) but it hard-fails for a non-technical user: `docker compose up app` aborts immediately because LAB_TRACKER_AUTH_SECRET_KEY is required via the `:?` guard (docker-compose.yml:15) and must be hand-set.

Make the container self-bootstrap: if LAB_TRACKER_AUTH_SECRET_KEY (and optionally LAB_TRACKER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_TOKEN) is unset, generate a strong value into a persisted volume on first boot instead of aborting. Guard a known irony: docker-entrypoint.sh retries `alembic upgrade head` up to MIGRATION_MAX_ATTEMPTS and can infinite-loop on a bad migration (noted in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md) — surface a clear failure instead of silent retries. Keep production deployments able to supply their own secret.

Evidence: docker-compose.yml:15,21,43; docker-entrypoint.sh; audit barrier #4; lab-manager-deploy persona.
acceptance_criteria: `docker compose up app` on a fresh checkout (Docker installed) brings up a working, auth-enabled, reboot-surviving instance with no manual secret editing; a failed migration fails loudly rather than looping.

title: Fix capture composer dark-mode message box (light-on-white text) + audit capture buttons
description: User report: the capture message box text is a light color that's hard to see, and asked to double-check the capture buttons (mic, add file, camera) do the right thing. Root cause for the text: the app has no data-theme toggle, so the active dark path is @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark). In that block --ink becomes near-white (#e9e7e2), but .capture-composer-input hardcodes background:#ffffff with color:var(--ink); the generic input/textarea dark override (specificity 0,0,1) loses to the .capture-composer-input class (0,1,0), leaving near-white text on a white box. The whole composer family (.capture-composer, -input, -icon, -mic, -send, -attachment-menu/option/chip) hardcodes light backgrounds with no prefers-color-scheme dark override, so they go light-on-light in OS dark mode. Also audit each capture control for correct wiring (htmlFor/accept/capture attributes; camera capture=environment vs 'choose existing photo' intent). Fix: add prefers-color-scheme dark overrides for the composer family in src/lab_tracker/frontend/styles.css, then npm run build to refresh the asset hash.
notes: FIXED + verified. (1) Dark-mode message box: added prefers-color-scheme dark (and mirrored data-theme dark) overrides for the capture composer family in src/lab_tracker/frontend/styles.css (.capture-composer #23272f, .capture-composer-input/.capture-attachment-option/.capture-attachment-chip #181b21 with color var(--ink), .capture-composer-icon #262a32, chip button #262a32), plus a .capture-composer-input::placeholder { color: var(--ink-soft) } rule for both themes. (2) Capture buttons (user chose 'allow both, match labels'): removed capture="environment" from the photo input and bare capture from the menu/bundle audio input so 'Photo or camera' and 'Voice file' now offer camera/recorder AND existing-file pick; added a dedicated capture-audio-record-input (with capture) for the mic icon so it stays a quick-record affordance. Verified: eslint clean; App.test.jsx 29/29; full suite 76/76 tests pass (2 files blocked by missing fake-indexeddb dep / EACCES npm cache — pre-existing env, unrelated); headless-Chrome before/after screenshots on the live prefers-color-scheme:dark path confirm the text is now readable. npm run build re-stamped asset hash to 6ac247d5911a.

title: [quick-win] Add LAB_TRACKER_OPENAI_* to .env.example and fix the default OpenAI model
description:
The headline AI feature (graph draft review + voice-note transcription) requires an OpenAI API key, but .env.example contains zero LAB_TRACKER_OPENAI_* variables, so users who copy that file assume it is complete and the feature silently fails with a generic "Failed to draft graph update." (mobile-capture.jsx:724). Separately, the default model is `gpt-5.4-mini` (config.py:32; README.md:149), which is not available on a standard OpenAI account, so even a user WITH a valid key gets a silent failure.

Fix: (1) add LAB_TRACKER_OPENAI_API_KEY=, LAB_TRACKER_OPENAI_MODEL=, LAB_TRACKER_OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL= to .env.example with comments pointing to platform.openai.com; (2) change the default model in config.py to a model available on standard accounts (e.g. gpt-4o-mini) or document clearly that the default must be overridden; (3) surface a clearer error when the key/model is missing or invalid.

Evidence: .env.example (no OPENAI vars); config.py:32; README.md:149-150; mobile-capture.jsx:724; audit barriers #10 and #14.
acceptance_criteria: .env.example documents all required OpenAI vars with guidance; the default model works on a standard OpenAI account out of the box (or the requirement to override is unmissable); missing/invalid key surfaces an actionable error rather than a generic failure.

title: Per-person / per-group record export
description:
Export the records of a departing trainee (questions/claims/datasets/analyses/notes) as PROV-O JSON-LD plus a scoped record dump, per-person and per-group, so a PI can hand a leaver a copy of their work.

Depends on the attribution FK schema.

title: Close auto-created figure client on circuit-open return
description: If the figure circuit is open after an env-configured client is auto-created, the early return bypasses the close finally block and can leak connection pools in long-running sessions.

title: Exclude generated build artifacts from Ruff gate
description: During lab-tracker-lmc3 verification, uv run ruff check . linted the untracked generated build/ tree and failed on generated package/test copies. Source lint passed with uv run ruff check . --extend-exclude build. Decide whether to add build/ to Ruff exclude and/or .gitignore, or document cleaning generated build output before running the full gate.

title: Security hardening: secrets, exposure defaults, upload serving
description: Deep review 2026-06-12: the default HMAC signing secret is accepted while auth is enabled in the local environment; docker-compose ships a known placeholder secret under environment=production; serve-lan.ps1 binds 0.0.0.0 without checking auth; uploads have no size limit or content-type validation and are served inline (stored XSS); no security headers anywhere.
notes: P1 child issues completed in this session; epic remains open for remaining P2/P3 follow-up work.

title: Reject the default auth secret whenever auth is enabled
description: The config.py:51 validator only rejects DEFAULT_AUTH_SECRET_KEY when environment is not local, but LAB_TRACKER_AUTH_ENABLED=true works in the local environment, so admin HS256 tokens are forgeable with the committed public secret. Change the condition to reject whenever is_auth_enabled() and the secret equals the default, regardless of environment. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Reject .env.example auth secret placeholder
description: Re-review H1: Settings still accepts LAB_TRACKER_AUTH_SECRET_KEY=replace-with-a-strong-random-secret when auth is enabled, and .env.example ships that value with production auth enabled. Add the literal to the insecure denylist, blank the example value so compose :? fails, and add config coverage. Details: docs/runs/re-review-2026-06-12.md#H1.

title: docker-compose must not default a known placeholder signing secret
description: docker-compose.yml:15 defaults LAB_TRACKER_AUTH_SECRET_KEY to replace-with-a-strong-secret while defaulting environment to production and publishing port 8000 on all interfaces; the config validator only rejects the single dev-only literal so this sails through. Make the variable required in compose and extend the validator with a denylist of known placeholders. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: serve-lan.ps1 should refuse to bind 0.0.0.0 with auth disabled
description: scripts/serve-lan.ps1:101 binds uvicorn to 0.0.0.0 and prints firewall-opening instructions but never verifies auth is enabled; the default invocation with no .env serves the whole graph unauthenticated to the LAN. Evaluate effective settings before binding and refuse unless an explicit override flag is passed. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Serve uploaded assets safely - attachment disposition and content-type allowlist
description: Visualization assets are served inline with the client-supplied content type (visualizations.py:192) and no upload route or storage backend validates content types (file_storage.py:138), enabling stored XSS via text/html or SVG uploads. Force attachment disposition plus nosniff and add an allowlist or server-derived content type at the upload boundary. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Add browser security response headers
description: No X-Content-Type-Options, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or HSTS headers are set anywhere (app_parts/frontend.py:65, middleware.py). Add a small header middleware emitting nosniff on all responses and a restrictive CSP on the /app shell and download endpoints. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Enforce upload size limits
description: Dataset file, note, and visualization uploads stream to storage with no maximum-size check at route, service, or storage layer (dataset_files.py:97, file_storage.py:131-174, note_storage.py:36-70). Add a configurable cap enforced in the chunk loop with early Content-Length rejection and partial-object cleanup. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Stop leaking diagnostics from unauthenticated observability endpoints
description: /readiness and /metrics are in the public allowlist even with auth on (middleware.py:28-29) and return absolute filesystem paths, raw SQLAlchemy error text, store row counts, and auth configuration (observability.py:41-80 and :128 and :196). Require credentials or reduce the unauthenticated payload to bare ok/fail and log details server-side. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Remove the /_test/ auth bypass from production middleware
description: _is_public_path unconditionally exempts every path under /_test/ (middleware.py:61) purely so test fixtures can skip credentials; any future route mounted under that prefix silently becomes unauthenticated. Move the exemption into test app wiring. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Add rate limiting to auth endpoints and review open viewer self-registration
description: routes/auth.py:71 has no rate limiting or lockout on login and allows unauthenticated viewer self-registration. Add basic throttling/lockout and consider gating registration behind a setting. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Add daily graph review cadence
description: Implement an end-of-day review envelope that gathers graph drafts from evidence created since the last reviewed window, generates a review report, and exposes the daily review through API/UI for human commit.
acceptance_criteria: Daily review runs are stored durably with window timestamps and linked graph drafts. A script can create an idempotent daily review for a project. API routes list/get/generate/mark review runs. The frontend can open a daily review and navigate to linked graph draft review pages. Docs/tests cover the workflow.

title: Chunk batched goal-link cleanup target filters for large SQLite deletes
description: Follow-up from the rjg1 verification review. lab-tracker-rjg1.10 collapsed project-delete goal-link cleanup into one query_goals(target_entity_keys=...) call using a composite IN predicate. That removes the N+1, but a very large project delete can still exceed SQLite's bound-parameter limit when target_entity_keys is huge. Postgres runtime is unaffected, but SQLite tests/local use should avoid the too-many-SQL-variables failure path.
acceptance_criteria: query_goals or remove_goal_links_to_project_contents chunks target_entity_keys below SQLite's parameter limit while preserving one-goal de-duplication; add a regression test with enough cascaded target entities to exercise chunking; existing goal/project-delete tests pass.

title: Batch runner: agent scheduled at user-set cadence, idempotent draft job
description:
Add a scheduled job driven by a user-facing cadence setting (default daily, e.g. 06:00 local lab time — not hard-coded). Setting or changing the cadence (re)schedules an agent that wakes up at that cadence, collects all notes with status='staged' that arrived since the last successful run, and kicks off the batch context builder + draft generator to figure out proposed graph changes.

Must be idempotent: re-running the same window must not produce duplicate batches. Should record run start/end, window covered, notes included, and outcome (success/error) for observability.
acceptance_criteria:
- Cadence is a user-visible setting (default daily 06:00 local lab time); changing it reschedules the agent/job
- On wake, job collects staged notes since last successful run watermark
- Idempotent: re-running same window does not create duplicate batches
- Run history persisted with window, note count, status, errors
- Manual 'run now' trigger available for admins/dev

title: Authenticate inbound clients at the hosted MCP proxy
description: The private streamable-HTTP MCP endpoint is described as token-authenticated, but deploy/mcp/Caddyfile currently checks only Host and Origin and redacts authorization headers. FastMCP does not authenticate inbound callers, while the compose MCP service uses one server-held read-only LPAT for every hop-two API request. Any client able to reach the private endpoint therefore inherits the entire graph scope visible to that shared token. Add an enforced inbound authentication boundary, or narrow and document the deployment contract so the endpoint cannot be mistaken for an authenticated service. This was discovered while designing remote OKF knowledge serving for MCP-enabled agents.
design: Keep the MCP process loopback-bound behind private TLS. Prefer a proxy or ASGI gate that validates a distinct short-lived inbound client credential before forwarding to FastMCP; do not expose or reuse the server-held Lab Tracker API LPAT as an unaudited public credential. Preserve the API hop as a read-only VIEWER LPAT and keep write denial server-side. If per-user authorization or audit identity is required, implement per-request credential forwarding or OAuth as an explicit larger design rather than implying it exists. Reconcile deploy/mcp/Caddyfile, compose configuration, setup docs, and security tests.
acceptance_criteria: Requests with no or invalid inbound credential are rejected before reaching FastMCP; a valid credential can complete MCP initialization and a read call through TLS; the hop-two Lab Tracker token remains read-only and write attempts remain denied; credentials and Authorization headers are absent from logs; automated proxy or integration coverage exercises missing, invalid, and valid credentials; documentation accurately distinguishes shared hosted scope from per-user stdio and forbids public exposure without the enforced gate; the live tailnet validation task remains separately actionable.
notes: Implemented a fail-closed ASGI bearer gate using distinct LAB_TRACKER_MCP_INBOUND_TOKEN / LT_MCP_INBOUND_TOKEN credentials. Missing, malformed, invalid, and duplicate Authorization headers return 401 before FastMCP; valid credentials complete MCP initialization and lab-tracker://surface resource read; the header is stripped before downstream dispatch and secrets are repr/log-redacted. Compose still uses a separate server-held LT_MCP_READONLY_TOKEN for the read-only API hop. title: Add end-to-end saved photo+voice bundle review test
description: Add an end-to-end regression test for the deferred mobile bundle path. The test should exercise saving a photo plus voice bundle for later, returning to pending review, transcribing the voice artifact, building graph context, drafting graph operations, and committing approved operations through the normal validation path.
design: Prefer the existing app/API test style and fixtures. Avoid external model or speech service dependencies by using the repository's existing test doubles or deterministic local stubs.
acceptance_criteria: The test creates or simulates a photo+voice capture bundle saved for later. Pending review can trigger transcription and draft generation for that bundle. The draft uses a graph context packet and preserves raw image/audio provenance. Approved operations commit only through normal API validation. The test fails clearly if transcription, drafting, or validation silently falls back or is skipped.
close_reason: Added a backend E2E regression for saved photo+voice bundles covering deferred capture, blocked drafting before transcript, explicit transcription, graph-context drafting, operation approval, and commit through normal validation.

title: [quick-win] Correct README phone-capture instructions to reflect device-pairing reality
description:
README implies a phone user can just open http://127.0.0.1:8000/app/capture (README.md:169), but phone capture is actually gated behind a desktop QR / device-pairing/enrollment flow (enroll.jsx:47-49; devices.jsx:31-46). A bench scientist following the README will find capture doesn't work as described.

Fix the docs to describe the real path: how to pair/enroll a phone (the QR/device flow) before capture works, with where to find it in the UI. (Longer term, the cross-platform LAN helper issue adds a QR + quickstart card.)

Evidence: README.md:169 vs enroll.jsx:47-49, devices.jsx:31-46; audit barrier #12.
acceptance_criteria: README accurately describes how to get a phone capturing notes (including any pairing/enrollment step), matching the actual UI flow.
